explanation: Isaac's prayer to God for his barren wife (Rebekah) showed that he believed in God's power and interceded for his wife — demonstrating his faith and reliance on God (Genesis 25:21). The correct answer is C (he had faith in God/interceded for his wife).

Samson's major achievement as Israel's judge was killing the Philistines — he killed more Philistines at his death (when he brought down the pillars) than during his lifetime (Judges 16:30). The correct answer is A (he killed more Philistines at death than in his lifetime).

God guided the Israelites on their journey from Egypt by a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night — providing direction and protection (Exodus 13:21-22). The correct answer is C (a pillar of cloud by day and pillar of fire by night).

King Asa proved to be a godly king by removing the idols and high places, deposing his mother as queen mother for her idolatry, and commanding Judah to seek the Lord (1 Kings 15:11-13). The correct answer is C (removing idols and commanding people to seek God).

The Hebrew midwives (Shiphrah and Puah) who obeyed God rather than Pharaoh were blessed with families/households of their own — God rewarded their fear and obedience (Exodus 1:20-21). The correct answer is D (God gave them families/households).

David's behaviour after Prophet Nathan accused him of murder and adultery was repentance — David confessed his sin immediately, saying 'I have sinned against the Lord' (2 Samuel 12:13). The correct answer is B (he repented and confessed his sin).

King Solomon demonstrated his wisdom in the dispute over the baby by ordering the living child to be cut in two — the true mother immediately gave up her claim to save the child's life, revealing she was the real mother (1 Kings 3:16-28). The correct answer is C (he ordered the child to be divided, revealing the true mother).

When Saul disobeyed God's command to destroy the Amalekites completely, Samuel rebuked him by saying that obedience is better than sacrifice — 'to obey is better than sacrifice, and to heed is better than the fat of rams' (1 Samuel 15:22). The correct answer is B (obedience is better than sacrifice).

Naaman's leprosy was transferred to Gehazi because Gehazi ran after Naaman and deceitfully took silver and garments in Elisha's name, telling lies — his greed and deception brought the punishment of leprosy (2 Kings 5:20-27). The correct answer is C (he ran after Naaman and lied to get gifts).

Obadiah, who was in charge of Ahab's household, demonstrated reverence for God by hiding one hundred prophets of the Lord in two caves and feeding them with bread and water during Jezebel's persecution (1 Kings 18:3-4). The correct answer is C (he hid 100 prophets and fed them).

The prophet who announced the imminent division of the kingdom of Israel from Jeroboam was Ahijah the Shilonite — he tore his garment into twelve pieces and gave ten to Jeroboam, symbolising the ten tribes he would rule (1 Kings 11:29-31). The correct answer is B (Ahijah the Shilonite).

After the dedication of the Temple, Ezra studied the law of the LORD in order to observe and teach its statutes and ordinances in Israel — he devoted himself to study, practice, and teaching of the Law (Ezra 7:10). The correct answer is D (to observe, teach and practise the law in Israel).

Nehemiah's initial reaction to the news about the ruins of Jerusalem and its gates was to sit down and weep, mourn for days, fast, and pray before God (Nehemiah 1:4). The correct answer is C (he wept, mourned, fasted, and prayed).

In Prophet Hosea's analysis, harlotry (prostitution/unfaithfulness) is equivalent to Israel's idolatry — Israel's worship of false gods and abandonment of the covenant with God was likened to an unfaithful wife (Hosea 4:12). The correct answer is B (idolatry/apostasy/unfaithfulness to God).

When Jonah preached God's message of judgement to Nineveh, the Ninevites believed God, proclaimed a fast, put on sackcloth, and repented — from the greatest to the least (Jonah 3:5-10). The correct answer is C (they believed, repented, fasted and wore sackcloth).

Daniel became distinguished above all other presidents and satraps because an excellent spirit was in him — he had exceptional qualities and God-given wisdom (Daniel 6:3). The correct answer is A (an excellent spirit was in him).

God told Ezekiel that the house of Israel would not listen to him because they would not listen to God — 'they will not listen to you, for they are not willing to listen to me' (Ezekiel 3:7). The correct answer is C (they were not willing to listen to God).

'Let justice roll down like waters and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream' — this statement was made by the prophet Amos (Amos 5:24), calling for social justice and righteousness. The correct answer is C (Amos).

'Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, O Lord' — this statement was uttered by Simon Peter (Luke 5:8) after Jesus caused a miraculous catch of fish, Peter's response showing awe at Jesus' divine power and his own unworthiness. The correct answer is C (Simon Peter).

According to Isaiah, God sent him to preach good news to the poor, bind up the broken-hearted, proclaim liberty to captives, and comfort those who mourn — the year of the Lord's favour (Isaiah 61:1-2). The correct answer is A (to preach good news to the poor and proclaim liberty).

After Jesus healed the demoniac (Gerasene demoniac) in the country of the Gerasenes, the people of the city asked Jesus to leave their region because they were afraid (Mark 5:15-17). The correct answer is C (they were afraid and asked Jesus to leave).

Jesus told the parable of the lost sheep to illustrate that there is more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons who do not need repentance (Luke 15:7). The correct answer is D (heaven rejoices more over one repentant sinner than ninety-nine righteous).

According to Mark, after the transfiguration, Jesus charged His disciples to tell no one what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead (Mark 9:9). The correct answer is B (to tell no one until after the resurrection).

According to Luke, the multitude that followed Jesus during the triumphal entry praised God with a loud voice for all the mighty works they had seen (Luke 19:37). The correct answer is B (they praised God for the mighty works they had seen).

'Truly, I say to you, today you will be with me in paradise' — Jesus said these words to the repentant thief (criminal) crucified beside him who asked to be remembered in Jesus' kingdom (Luke 23:43). The correct answer is D (to the repentant thief/criminal on the cross).

Paul informed the Galatians that the gospel he preached came through a revelation of Jesus Christ — not from human beings, not received or taught by any man (Galatians 1:12). The correct answer is A (through a revelation of Jesus Christ).

According to the Gospel of John, Jesus is the true vine while the vine-dresser/husbandman is the Father — 'I am the true vine and my Father is the vine-dresser' (John 15:1). The correct answer is B (the Father/God).

'Why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit' — these words were spoken by Peter to Ananias, who with his wife Sapphira lied about the proceeds from their land sale (Acts 5:3). The correct answer is B (Ananias, who lied about the proceeds of land).

'Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved' — this was taught by certain men (Judaizers) from Judea who taught the Gentile believers in Antioch, causing the Jerusalem Council controversy (Acts 15:1). The correct answer is B (Judaizers/men from Judea who came to Antioch).

'Son of the devil, you enemy of all righteousness, full of all deceit and villainy' — Paul said this to Elymas (Bar-Jesus), the sorcerer who tried to turn the proconsul Sergius Paulus away from the faith (Acts 13:10). The correct answer is A (Paul, to Elymas the sorcerer).

Peter in his teaching on humility admonishes Christians to clothe themselves with humility toward one another and to humble themselves under the mighty hand of God (1 Peter 5:5-6). The correct answer is B (to clothe themselves with humility and humble themselves before God).

Paul in Corinthians advised that Christians should re-affirm their love for the repentant member — 'you should rather forgive and comfort him, reaffirm your love for him' (2 Corinthians 2:8). The correct answer is B (to reaffirm their love for the repentant person).

According to Galatians, the death of Christ eliminated all forms of discrimination — 'there is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus' (Galatians 3:28). The correct answer is C (all racial, social, and gender distinctions/discrimination).

Paul in Thessalonians warned that busybodies and those living in idleness should work — 'if anyone will not work, let him not eat' (2 Thessalonians 3:10). The correct answer is B (they should work for their own living/not be idle).

Paul in Thessalonians told believers that the coming of the Lord would come like a thief in the night — unexpectedly, when people least expect it (1 Thessalonians 5:2). The correct answer is B (like a thief in the night — unexpectedly).

James stated that when believers meet various trials, they should count it all joy because the testing of their faith produces steadfastness/patience (James 1:2-3). The correct answer is C (because trials test and produce steadfastness/patience in faith).

According to Jesus, the seventy disciples should rejoice not because the spirits were subject to them but because their names were written in heaven (Luke 10:20). The correct answer is A (their names were written in heaven).

Jesus was tempted by the devil so as to demonstrate that he was without sin and could fulfil his messianic mission — to show that he could overcome temptation and sympathise with our weaknesses (Hebrews 4:15). The correct answer is C (to show he was without sin and could sympathise with human weakness).

According to Corinthians, the variety of spiritual gifts are inspired by the same Holy Spirit — 'there are varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit' (1 Corinthians 12:4-6, 11). The correct answer is D (the same Holy Spirit).

God was angry with Eli because he failed to restrain his sons from their wickedness — Eli knew his sons were sinning (stealing from offerings, lying with women at the tabernacle) but did not discipline or stop them (1 Samuel 3:13). The correct answer is C (he failed to discipline/restrain his wicked sons).

Laxity in disciplining children is dangerous because it leads to moral failure, as demonstrated by Eli's sons — Eli's failure to discipline Hophni and Phinehas resulted in their wickedness and death, showing that proper discipline is necessary for children's moral development. The correct answer is C (it leads to moral failure and corruption, as in Eli's family).

Saul's decision to consult a medium (the witch of Endor) before his last battle displayed his lack of trust/faith in God — he had turned away from God and sought guidance through forbidden means (1 Samuel 28:6-7). The correct answer is B (lack of trust/faith in God).

'Do not destroy him; for who can stretch out his hand against the LORD's anointed and be guiltless?' — This was said by David to Abishai when they found Saul sleeping in his camp, preventing Abishai from killing Saul (1 Samuel 26:9). The correct answer is B (David, to Abishai when they found Saul sleeping).

Baal did not answer his worshipers at the contest on Mount Carmel because Baal is not real/does not exist — Elijah mocked Baal's worshipers saying their god might be meditating, on a journey, or sleeping. Baal is a false/powerless idol. The correct answer is B (Baal is not real/has no power — is a false god).

'What is this that you have done?' — the people on the ship asked Jonah this when they discovered he was fleeing from God and that his disobedience was the cause of the storm (Jonah 1:10). The correct answer is B (Jonah, who was fleeing from God's presence).

Nehemiah responded to the opposition of the enemies of Israel (Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem) by praying to God and setting up a guard day and night against their threats (Nehemiah 4:9). The correct answer is D (he prayed and set a guard/organised defence).

According to Amos, God desires the knowledge of Himself and justice rather than burnt offerings and sacrifices — 'I hate, I despise your feasts... Let justice roll down like waters' (Amos 5:21-24). The correct answer is D (burnt offerings and religious feasts/sacrifices).
When Zechariah saw the angel of the Lord standing on the right side of the altar of incense, he was frightened/terrified (Luke 1:12). The correct answer is B (he was troubled/frightened).

'What shall I do with you, O Ephraim? What shall I do with you, O Judah? Your love is like a morning cloud, like the dew that goes away early.' — This was said by God through Hosea (Hosea 6:4), expressing God's frustration with Israel's fleeting love. The correct answer is A (God through Hosea, about Israel's/Judah's fleeting love).

The prophet who was ordained/consecrated from the womb for God's service was Jeremiah — 'Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, before you were born I set you apart; I appointed you as a prophet to the nations' (Jeremiah 1:5). The correct answer is A (Jeremiah).

In Isaiah's vision, his guilt was taken away and his sin forgiven after a seraph flew to him with a live coal taken from the altar and touched his lips (Isaiah 6:6-7). The correct answer is B (a seraph touched his lips with a burning coal from the altar).

'Follow me and leave the dead to bury their own dead' — Jesus said this to a would-be disciple who asked to first bury his father, teaching that following Christ takes absolute priority over all other obligations (Matthew 8:22; Luke 9:60). The correct answer is C (following Christ must take absolute priority over all other duties).
Jesus encouraged His followers to rejoice when persecuted because their reward in heaven is great (Matthew 5:12). The correct answer is A (their reward in heaven is great).

In the parable of the sower, the seed that fell among thorns symbolises those who hear the word but the cares of the world, the deceitfulness of riches, and the desires for other things choke the word (Mark 4:18-19). The correct answer is D (those whose faith is choked by the cares and riches of this world).

'Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jona! for flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven' — Jesus said this to Peter after Peter's confession that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God (Matthew 16:17). The correct answer is B (after Peter confessed Jesus as the Christ/Son of God).

The tearing of the curtain of the Temple into two at Jesus' death signified the removal of the barrier between God and humanity — access to God's presence is now open to all through Christ's atoning death (Matthew 27:51). The correct answer is A (the removal of the barrier between God and humanity/open access to God).

'Tell people, His disciples came by night and stole him away while we were asleep' — the chief priests instructed the soldiers to spread this false story to deny the resurrection of Jesus (Matthew 28:13). The correct answer is C (the chief priests instructed the soldiers to say this lie).

Jesus drove the money changers and sellers out of the Temple because they had turned His Father's house of prayer into a den of robbers/marketplace (Matthew 21:12-13). The correct answer is A (they had turned God's house of prayer into a den of robbers/marketplace).
The disciples who went to preach in Samaria after the great persecution was Philip — he went to Samaria and preached Christ there with signs and wonders (Acts 8:5). The correct answer is A (Philip).

In the early Church, believers devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and fellowship, to the breaking of bread, and to prayer (Acts 2:42). The correct answer is C (the apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread, and prayer).

Paul in Romans stated that the righteousness of God has been manifested through faith in Jesus Christ for all who believe — apart from the law (Romans 3:21-22). The correct answer is C (through faith in Jesus Christ/apart from the law).

Saul was converted so that he might bear the name of Christ before Gentiles, kings, and the children of Israel — to be a chosen vessel/instrument to carry the gospel to all nations (Acts 9:15). The correct answer is D (to carry Christ's name before Gentiles, kings, and Israelites).

According to Romans, all who were baptised into Christ were also baptised into His death — buried with Him through baptism, rising with Him through resurrection (Romans 6:3-4). The correct answer is C (baptised into His death/united with Him in His death and resurrection).

In Corinthians, believers are taught to forgive one another in order to prevent Satan from gaining an advantage — 'lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices' (2 Corinthians 2:11). The correct answer is A (to prevent Satan from gaining advantage over them).

'Pay all of them their dues, taxes to whom taxes are due, revenue to whom revenue is due' — Paul taught this principle of civic responsibility in Romans 13:7, teaching submission to governing authorities. The correct answer is B (civic responsibility/submission to authorities — Romans).

In Corinthians, Paul stated that by one Spirit we were all baptised into one body — 'For by one Spirit we were all baptised into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, slaves or free' (1 Corinthians 12:13). The correct answer is D (baptised into one body/one Spirit).

At the second coming of Christ, those who are alive shall be caught up together with the dead in Christ in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air (1 Thessalonians 4:17). The correct answer is B (caught up/raptured to meet the Lord in the air).

Peter in his epistle charged his fellow elders to tend the flock of God willingly, not under compulsion, not for shameful gain, and not domineering but being examples to the flock (1 Peter 5:2-3). The correct answer is D (to shepherd the flock willingly, as examples, not for gain).

According to James, treatment of brethren at fellowship should not be based on partiality/favouritism — James rebuked showing special honour to the rich and dishonour to the poor (James 2:1-4). The correct answer is A (without partiality/favouritism — all should be treated equally).

God blessed and hallowed (sanctified) the seventh day because on it He rested from all His work that He had done in creation (Genesis 2:3). The correct answer is A (He had rested from all His work of creation).

Noah's ark was sustained during the flood by the waters — the waters lifted the ark above the earth while the flood covered everything (Genesis 7:17-18). The correct answer is C (the rising flood waters lifted/sustained the ark).

God visited the children of Israel on Mount Sinai during the giving of the Law through thunder, lightning, thick cloud, and loud trumpet blasts — the people trembled with fear (Exodus 19:16-18). The correct answer is C (thunder, lightning, fire, and thick cloud/smoke).

Nebuchadnezzar ordered his subjects to worship the image he set up when they heard the sound of musical instruments — any who did not fall down and worship would be thrown into a burning fiery furnace (Daniel 3:5-6). The correct answer is C (when they heard the sound of musical instruments).

The sign of God's covenant with Abraham was circumcision — every male in his household was to be circumcised as a sign of the covenant between God and Abraham's descendants (Genesis 17:11). The correct answer is B (circumcision).

The commander of Jabin's (king of Canaan's) army was Sisera — he commanded nine hundred iron chariots and oppressed Israel. Deborah and Barak defeated him; he was killed by Jael (Judges 4:2). The correct answer is B (Sisera).

According to Ezekiel, the new covenant would involve God giving His people a new heart and putting His Spirit within them — replacing their heart of stone with a heart of flesh (Ezekiel 36:26-27). The correct answer is B (a new heart and God's Spirit within them).

God stopped Abraham from sacrificing his son Isaac in the land of Moriah because Abraham had demonstrated complete obedience and had not withheld his only son from God (Genesis 22:12-16). The correct answer is D (Abraham proved his obedience/did not withhold his only son).

Asa removed the abominable image his mother Maacah made for Asherah and burnt it at the Kidron valley — she was removed from being queen mother for this idolatry (1 Kings 15:13). The correct answer is B (he removed his mother from being queen and destroyed her idol).

'Arise, be gone' — this was said by Amnon to Tamar after he had raped her — he hated her even more than he had loved her before and threw her out (2 Samuel 13:15). The correct answer is B (Amnon said this to Tamar after he violated her).

The people who told Saul that David was hiding in the hill of Hachilah were the Ziphites — they came to Saul at Gibeah and betrayed David's location (1 Samuel 26:1). The correct answer is A (the Ziphites).

At Gibeon, the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream — God asked Solomon what he wanted, and Solomon asked for wisdom to govern God's people (1 Kings 3:5). The correct answer is C (a dream/vision at night).

'In the territory of Jezreel the dogs shall eat the flesh of Jezebel' — this prophecy was spoken by Elijah the Tishbite against Jezebel as God's judgement for her wickedness (1 Kings 21:23; 2 Kings 9:36). The correct answer is A (Elijah the Tishbite's prophecy against Jezebel).

God forbade the Israelites from inter-marrying with Gentiles because the Gentiles would turn their hearts away from God to worship their idols — this is exactly what happened with Solomon's foreign wives (Deuteronomy 7:3-4; 1 Kings 11:2). The correct answer is C (the Gentiles would turn their hearts away from God to idolatry).

King Josiah ordered Shaphan, the secretary, to read the book of the law that was found in the house of the Lord (2 Kings 22:8-10). The correct answer is B (to read the book of the law that was found).

'Arise, take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which he refused to give you for money; for Naboth is not alive, but dead' — Jezebel said this to Ahab after she arranged Naboth's murder (1 Kings 21:15). The correct answer is B (Jezebel said this to Ahab after arranging Naboth's death).

'O LORD, let thine ear be attentive to the prayer of thy servant... and grant him mercy in the sight of this man' — this was Nehemiah's prayer before going before King Artaxerxes to request permission to rebuild Jerusalem (Nehemiah 1:11). The correct answer is B (Nehemiah's prayer before approaching King Artaxerxes).
When Jonah fled from God and joined a ship to Tarshish, he boarded a ship at Joppa (Jonah 1:3). The correct answer is D (Joppa).

Ezra was able to gain favour before the king of Persia because the gracious hand of God was upon him — 'the hand of the LORD his God was on him' (Ezra 7:6, 9). The correct answer is C (the hand of God was upon him/God's grace was with him).

According to Prophet Hosea, the Israelites shall play the harlot, but the men shall not be punished — but the daughters who commit harlotry and the brides who commit adultery would be punished, because the men themselves went with harlots (Hosea 4:14). The correct answer is D (the men themselves consorted with harlots and prostitutes).

When Prophet Isaiah saw the Lord of Hosts in the temple, he said 'Woe is me! For I am lost; for I am a man of unclean lips... for my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of hosts!' — he was overwhelmed by a sense of unworthiness (Isaiah 6:5). The correct answer is D (he confessed his unworthiness/unclean lips).

The Israelites' offering of their sons and daughters to Molech was seen as an abomination and a grievous sin — it was child sacrifice to a pagan god, defiling the sanctuary and profaning God's name (Leviticus 20:2-3; Ezekiel 20:31). The correct answer is B (an abomination/profaning God's name through child sacrifice).

When God called Prophet Jeremiah, he claimed that he did not know how to speak because he was only a youth/child — God then touched his mouth and put His words in it (Jeremiah 1:6-9). The correct answer is C (he was too young/a child who did not know how to speak).
The first miracle Jesus performed was turning water into wine at the wedding at Cana in Galilee (John 2:1-11). The correct answer is C (turning water into wine at the wedding in Cana).

Jesus said anyone who put his hand to the plough and looked back would not be fit for the kingdom of God — total commitment to following Jesus is required; there is no turning back (Luke 9:62). The correct answer is C (not fit/worthy for the kingdom of God).

At the time Angel Gabriel appeared to Mary, Elizabeth was pregnant for six months — 'your kinswoman Elizabeth in her old age has also conceived a son; and this is the sixth month' (Luke 1:36). The correct answer is A (six months).

The parable of the prodigal son teaches that God (the Father) rejoices and welcomes back repentant sinners with forgiveness and restoration — God's love is unconditional and He runs to meet those who return to Him (Luke 15:20-24). The correct answer is B (God receives and rejoices over repentant sinners).

Jesus directed those He healed of leprosy to offer gifts of cleansing as a testimony/witness to the priests — 'go and show yourself to the priest and offer the gift Moses commanded for a proof/testimony to the people' (Matthew 8:4; Luke 17:14). The correct answer is D (as a testimony/witness to the priests and people).

The Last Supper took place during the Passover on the first day of Unleavened Bread — 'On the first day of Unleavened Bread the disciples came to Jesus, saying, Where will you have us prepare for you to eat the Passover?' (Matthew 26:17). The correct answer is B (Unleavened Bread/Passover).

'It is finished' — Jesus' statement on the cross implies that the work of redemption/salvation was complete — His atoning sacrifice for the sins of humanity was accomplished (John 19:30). The correct answer is C (the work of redemption/salvation was completed).
The disciple who identified Jesus as the Christ of God was Peter — 'Peter answered him, You are the Christ, the Son of the living God' (Matthew 16:16; Luke 9:20). The correct answer is D (Peter).

In the teaching on the true vine, Jesus said that any branch that bears no fruit would be taken away/cut off by the Father, and any branch that does bear fruit would be pruned to bear more fruit (John 15:2). The correct answer is B (taken away/cut off by the Father).

The offense of Ananias and Sapphira was that they lied to God (the Holy Spirit) — they sold a property but secretly kept part of the money while claiming to give all of it to the apostles (Acts 5:1-4). The correct answer is B (they lied about the price of the property/to the Holy Spirit).

The presiding judge/leader at the Jerusalem Council was James — 'After they finished speaking, James replied...' and gave the final decision (Acts 15:13-19). The correct answer is B (James, the Lord's brother).

The effect of Stephen's death on the early church was that it led to a great persecution, scattering the believers throughout Judea and Samaria — thus spreading the gospel beyond Jerusalem (Acts 8:1). The correct answer is B (persecution and scattering of believers, which spread the gospel).

When Saul sought to persecute the believers, he collected letters from the high priest to the synagogues in Damascus — so that he could arrest any Christians he found there (Acts 9:1-2). The correct answer is D (the high priest/chief priests).

'The crowd joined in attacking them; and the magistrates tore the garments of Paul and Silas and gave orders to beat them with rods' — this happened to Paul and Silas in Philippi after Paul cast out the spirit from the slave girl (Acts 16:22). The correct answer is D (Paul and Silas in Philippi).

According to Galatians, the law was made as a guardian/tutor/schoolmaster to lead people to Christ — 'the law was our guardian until Christ came, in order that we might be justified by faith' (Galatians 3:24). The correct answer is A (guardian/tutor/schoolmaster to lead to Christ).

Paul teaches the Romans that the presenting of their bodies as a living sacrifice is their spiritual/reasonable service of worship — 'present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your spiritual worship' (Romans 12:1). The correct answer is C (spiritual/reasonable worship/service to God).

Peter declares that God exalts those who humble themselves — 'Humble yourselves, therefore, under the mighty hand of God so that at the proper time he may exalt you' (1 Peter 5:6). The correct answer is D (those who humble themselves).

Paul in Corinthians praised the churches of Macedonia because their extreme poverty gave birth to an abundance of generosity — they gave beyond their means to the collection for the saints (2 Corinthians 8:1-3). The correct answer is B (their generosity despite their extreme poverty/they gave beyond their means).

In Corinthians, Paul says that he who prophesies edifies (builds up) the church — 'the one who prophesies speaks to people for their upbuilding and encouragement and consolation' (1 Corinthians 14:3-4). The correct answer is C (the church/body of believers).

In Thessalonians, believers are taught that at the Second Coming, the dead in Christ shall rise first, then the living shall be caught up with them to meet the Lord in the air (1 Thessalonians 4:16-17). The correct answer is A (the dead in Christ shall rise first).

In Colossians, Christians are advised to be diligent at work because it is done in service to the Lord, not to men — 'Whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord and not for men' (Colossians 3:23). The correct answer is A (they are ultimately working for the Lord, not for men).

Because David sought God's will to pursue the Amalekites who had invaded Ziklag and taken captive all the women and children (including David's two wives), God told him to pursue — and he recovered everything (1 Samuel 30:7-8, 18-19). The correct answer is D (God told him to pursue and promised he would recover everything).

'Why then have you not kept watch over your Lord the king?' — This question was asked of Abner (Saul's commander) by David when David had taken Saul's spear and water jar from near his head without Abner knowing (1 Samuel 26:15). The correct answer is B (David asked Abner why he hadn't protected Saul).

When Naboth refused to exchange his vineyard with King Ahab, Ahab reacted by going home sullen and angry, lying on his bed with his face turned away, refusing to eat — he sulked and was depressed (1 Kings 21:4). The correct answer is D (he went home sullen, lay on his bed, and refused to eat).
Solomon's wisdom surpassed the wisdom of all the people of the East and all the wisdom of Egypt (1 Kings 4:30). The correct answer is B (the wisdom of all the East and Egypt).

Saul relied on a medium (the witch of Endor) because God did not answer him through prophets, dreams, or the Urim — God had turned away from Saul (1 Samuel 28:6). The correct answer is A (prophets, dreams, and the Urim).
King Josiah was killed by Pharaoh Neco in a battle at Megiddo — Josiah went to fight against Neco and was shot by archers (2 Chronicles 35:20-24). The correct answer is A (Megiddo).
The book of the law was found in the house of the Lord during the reign of King Josiah — by Hilkiah the high priest during repairs to the Temple (2 Kings 22:8). The correct answer is C (Josiah).

The sins of Israel during the reign of Ahab consisted of Baal worship, building high places, and following the ways of Jeroboam — Ahab's marriage to Jezebel introduced Baal worship on a large scale (1 Kings 16:30-33). The correct answer is A (Baal worship and following the sins of Jeroboam).

When the three Hebrew men (Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego) refused to worship the king's image, Nebuchadnezzar commanded them to be thrown into the fiery furnace, heated seven times hotter than usual (Daniel 3:19-21). The correct answer is C (thrown into the fiery furnace).

The major reason God allowed the Babylonian attack on Jerusalem was the persistent idolatry and disobedience of the people of Judah — they had forsaken God and worshipped other gods (2 Kings 24:3-4; Jeremiah 25:8-9). The correct answer is B (their persistent idolatry and disobedience to God).

God helped Jeremiah overcome his inability to speak as a prophet by touching his mouth and putting His words in it — 'I have put my words in your mouth' (Jeremiah 1:9). The correct answer is C (God touched his mouth and put His words in it).

Before his call as a prophet, Amos was a herdsman (shepherd) from Tekoa who also dressed sycamore trees — he was not a trained prophet but an ordinary farmer (Amos 1:1; 7:14). The correct answer is C (a herdsman/shepherd who tended sycamore trees).

Amos' prophecies were considered a conspiracy against the northern king (Jeroboam II) by Amaziah the priest of Bethel, who accused Amos of conspiring against the king — Amaziah reported him to Jeroboam (Amos 7:10). The correct answer is D (Amaziah the priest of Bethel accused Amos of conspiring against Jeroboam).

'He will be great before the Lord, and shall drink no wine nor strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother's womb' — the angel Gabriel said this to Zechariah about his son John the Baptist (Luke 1:15). The correct answer is A (John the Baptist, as told by the angel to Zechariah).

Prophet Ezekiel was set upon his feet to hear the Lord speak when the Spirit entered into him — 'And when he spoke to me, the Spirit entered into me and set me on my feet' (Ezekiel 2:2). The correct answer is A (the Spirit entered into him and set him on his feet).

The disciples of Jesus could not heal the boy with epilepsy/convulsions because they had little faith — Jesus said 'Because of your little faith' (Matthew 17:20). They had not prayed and fasted (Mark 9:29). The correct answer is D (their little faith/lack of prayer and fasting).

One quality of a good disciple exhibited by the first disciples called was immediate obedience — when Jesus called Peter, Andrew, James, and John, they immediately left their nets and boats and followed Him (Matthew 4:20-22). The correct answer is C (immediate and wholehearted obedience).

'Lord, if you will, you can make me clean' — this statement was made by a leper who fell before Jesus asking to be healed of leprosy (Matthew 8:2; Mark 1:40; Luke 5:12). The correct answer is C (a leper who came to Jesus for healing).

The promise to those who are persecuted for righteousness' sake is that theirs is the kingdom of heaven — 'Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness' sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven' (Matthew 5:10). The correct answer is D (theirs is the kingdom of heaven).

The seeds that fell among thorns in the parable of the sower refer to those who hear the word but the cares of the world and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word (Matthew 13:22). The correct answer is B (those whose faith is choked by worldly cares and riches).

According to Peter during the great confession, people believed that Jesus was John the Baptist, or Elijah, or Jeremiah, or one of the prophets (Matthew 16:13-14). The correct answer is B (Elijah, Jeremiah, or one of the prophets).

'Behold, your king is coming to you, humble and mounted on an ass' — this was a prophecy by Zechariah (Zechariah 9:9) fulfilled by Jesus' triumphal entry into Jerusalem. The correct answer is A (Zechariah's prophecy — fulfilled at the triumphal entry).

According to Mark, the young man the women saw in Jesus' tomb told them that Jesus had risen and they should tell His disciples and Peter that He would meet them in Galilee (Mark 16:6-7). The correct answer is B (Jesus had risen and would meet the disciples in Galilee).

After his arrest in Gethsemane, Jesus was first taken to Annas (the father-in-law of Caiaphas), then to Caiaphas the high priest (Matthew 26:57; John 18:13). The correct answer is A (Annas, then Caiaphas the high priest).

The appointment of deacons became necessary because of the complaint by the Hellenist Jews (Greek-speaking Jews) that their widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution of food (Acts 6:1). The correct answer is D (the Hellenist widows were being neglected in the food distribution).

According to Paul, before his conversion, he persecuted the church violently, trying to destroy it — 'I persecuted the church of God violently and tried to destroy it' (Galatians 1:13; Acts 22:4). The correct answer is A (he violently persecuted the church and tried to destroy it).

'He was not the light but was sent to bear witness to the light' — this statement refers to John the Baptist, who was sent to witness to the true light (Jesus Christ) who was coming into the world (John 1:8). The correct answer is A (John the Baptist).

'It is necessary to circumcise them, and to charge them to keep the law of Moses' — this was taught by certain Pharisee believers who argued that Gentile converts must be circumcised (Acts 15:5). The correct answer is A (Pharisee believers/Judaizers who insisted on circumcision for Gentiles).

'Lord, I have heard from many about this man, how much evil he has done to your saints in Jerusalem' — Ananias said this to God in a vision about Saul, before God sent him to restore Saul's sight (Acts 9:13). The correct answer is B (Ananias said this to God about Saul).

According to Galatians (more likely James), judgment is without mercy to one who has shown no mercy — 'For judgment is without mercy to one who has shown no mercy. Mercy triumphs over judgment' (James 2:13). The correct answer is A (shown no mercy — mercy triumphs over judgment).

According to Paul in his letter to Philemon, forgiveness should not be forced or coerced but should come from Philemon's own free will — Paul sent Onesimus back and appealed to Philemon to receive him as a brother (Philemon 1:14). The correct answer is A (freely/voluntarily, not under compulsion).

According to Peter, when Christians humble themselves under God's mighty hand, God will exalt/lift them up in due time (1 Peter 5:6). The correct answer is B (God will exalt/lift them up in due time).

Paul in Timothy urged believers to make supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgiving for all people — for kings and all who are in authority, so that Christians may live peaceful lives (1 Timothy 2:1-2). The correct answer is C (for kings and all who are in authority).

In Corinthians, Paul said that one can only say 'Jesus is Lord' by the Holy Spirit — 'no one can say Jesus is Lord except by the Holy Spirit' (1 Corinthians 12:3). The correct answer is B (by/through the Holy Spirit).

When Christians give freely, God will supply all their needs — 'And my God will supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus' (Philippians 4:19). The correct answer is D (all their needs according to God's riches in glory).

'As each has received a gift, employ it for one another, as good stewards of God's varied grace' — this teaches that spiritual gifts are given to serve others, acting as stewards (1 Peter 4:10). The correct answer is C (stewards of God's varied grace/using gifts in service to others).

According to Thessalonians, the second coming of the Lord will be like a thief in the night — sudden and unexpected, catching people unprepared (1 Thessalonians 5:2). The correct answer is B (like a thief in the night/suddenly and unexpectedly).

According to James, when we meet various trials in life, we should count it all joy because the testing of faith produces steadfastness/patience (James 1:2-4). The correct answer is A (count it all joy/rejoice, because trials produce steadfastness).

'Fear not, stand firm, and see the salvation of the Lord, which He will work for you today' — Moses said this to the Israelites when they were trapped between the Red Sea and Pharaoh's army (Exodus 14:13). The correct answer is B (Moses said this to the fearful Israelites at the Red Sea).

The enormity of sins of Judah before Josiah's reforms was exemplified by idolatry in the Temple — vessels made for Baal were in the Temple, male shrine prostitutes, child sacrifice at Topheth, and worship of the host of heaven (2 Kings 23:4-7). The correct answer is A (idolatry and abominations practiced in the very Temple).

'Behold, this has touched your lips; your guilt is taken away, and your sin forgiven' — a seraph (angel) said this to Isaiah after touching his lips with a burning coal from the altar (Isaiah 6:7). The correct answer is A (a seraph/angel said this to Isaiah after touching his lips with a live coal).

The wise men from the East were able to know about the birth of Jesus by a star they saw in the East — 'Where is he who has been born king of the Jews? For we saw his star when it rose' (Matthew 2:2). The correct answer is D (they saw his star in the East/a star guided them).

The effect of Stephen's death on the Early Church was that a great persecution arose, and the believers were scattered throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria (Acts 8:1). The correct answer is A (great persecution scattered believers throughout Judea and Samaria).

Paul advised the Philippians to manifest humility of mind — to count others more significant than themselves, having the same humble mind as Christ Jesus (Philippians 2:3-5). The correct answer is A (humility of mind/considering others better than themselves).

According to Paul, the second coming of Christ will take place at the last trumpet — 'in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet' (1 Corinthians 15:52; 1 Thessalonians 4:16). The correct answer is C (at the last trumpet/at the sound of the trumpet).

The first lead of the river in the Garden of Eden that parted was Pishon — 'The name of the first is Pishon. It is the one that flowed around the whole land of Havilah' (Genesis 2:11). The correct answer is C (Pishon).

Maranatha means 'Come, Lord Jesus' or 'Our Lord, come!' — an Aramaic expression used in early Christian worship expressing the longing for Christ's return (1 Corinthians 16:22; Didache 10:6). The correct answer is B (Come, Lord/Our Lord, come).

The prophet known for the statement 'Can two walk together, except they be agreed?' was Amos (Amos 3:3) — this rhetorical question introduces Amos' message that Israel's disasters come because they have broken their agreement with God. The correct answer is B (Amos).

The first atonement for sin through sacrifice was done at the altar — specifically when God made coats of skins for Adam and Eve, implying the first animal sacrifice for covering sin (Genesis 3:21). Or in some interpretations, when Cain and Abel brought offerings. The correct answer is C (the altar/when God provided skins for Adam and Eve).

'This man is that power of God which is called Great' — this statement was made about Simon the Sorcerer (Simon Magus) by the people of Samaria who had been amazed by his magic (Acts 8:10). The correct answer is C (Simon the Sorcerer/Simon Magus).

In his first letter to Timothy, Paul warned believers against the love of money — 'For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evils' (1 Timothy 6:10). The correct answer is B (the love of money).

According to Paul to Colossians, the credit for giving (and all good work) belongs to God who supplies all the needs and equips believers to give — 'God who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your seed for sowing' (2 Corinthians 9:10; Colossians 3:17). The correct answer is C (God/Christ who enables all things).

The Israelites said 'All that the Lord has spoken we will do' at Mount Sinai (Horeb) — when Moses read the Book of the Covenant to them (Exodus 24:3-7). The correct answer is B (at Sinai/when Moses read the covenant/Book of the Covenant to them).

Saul was rejected as king over Israel because he disobeyed God's commandment to destroy all the Amalekites and their possessions — he spared King Agag and the best livestock (1 Samuel 15:11, 23). The correct answer is C (he disobeyed God's command to destroy the Amalekites completely).

'Hear this word, you cows of Bashan... who oppress the poor, who crush the needy' — this was said by Prophet Amos to the wealthy, pampered women of Israel who enjoyed luxury while the poor suffered (Amos 4:1). The correct answer is C (Amos said this to the wealthy oppressive women of Israel).

The instrument used by God to destroy Babylon and set the Israelites free was Cyrus the Great (king of Persia) — God called Cyrus His anointed and instrument to overthrow Babylon and decree the return of the exiles (Isaiah 44:28; 45:1). The correct answer is A (Cyrus, king of Persia).

'I called to the Lord, out of my distress, and he answered me, out of the belly of Sheol I cried' — this was said by Jonah from inside the great fish's belly (Jonah 2:1-2). The correct answer is A (Jonah, from inside the fish/from distress).

The sign of God's covenant with Abraham was circumcision — 'You shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskins, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and you' (Genesis 17:11). The correct answer is B (circumcision).
According to Matthew, true wisdom is proved/shown by its deeds/actions — 'wisdom is justified by her deeds' (Matthew 11:19). The correct answer is D (wisdom is justified by its deeds/actions).

St. Paul had already boasted to the Macedonians about the Achaians' eagerness/generosity, and he sent Titus and the brothers ahead to ensure the Corinthians' collection was ready (2 Corinthians 9:2-4). The correct answer is A (the Macedonians).

The sin of the Israelites that led to the punishment by fiery serpents was speaking against God and Moses, complaining about the lack of food and water, and expressing impatience with the manna (Numbers 21:5-6). The correct answer is B (they complained/spoke against God and Moses/despised the manna).

'Go into the hills, lest the pursuers meet you; and hide yourselves there three days' — the two spies (sent by Joshua to Rahab's house) were told this by Rahab when she hid them and helped them escape (Joshua 2:16). The correct answer is C (Rahab told the spies to hide in the hills for three days).

In Jotham's parable of the trees, Abimelech is likened to the bramble (thornbush) — the most worthless and useless shrub that nonetheless offered to be king, representing Abimelech's illegitimate and destructive rule (Judges 9:14-15). The correct answer is B (the bramble/thornbush).

During the confirmation of the covenant, Moses was invited by the Lord to come up the mountain with Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel (Exodus 24:1). The correct answer is A (Aaron, Nadab, Abihu and seventy elders of Israel).

'After me comes he who is mightier than I, the thong of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and untie' — John the Baptist said this about Jesus, acknowledging his own lesser role (Mark 1:7). The correct answer is D (John the Baptist said this about Jesus).

'The Holy Spirit will come upon you and the power of the Most High will overshadow you' — the angel Gabriel said this to Mary about the conception of Jesus (Luke 1:35). The correct answer is C (the angel Gabriel said this to Mary).
The Lord healed the blindness of Paul (Saul) through Ananias — a disciple in Damascus whom God sent to lay hands on Saul and restore his sight (Acts 9:17-18). The correct answer is A (Ananias).

'Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!' — this was addressed to Jesus by blind Bartimaeus (Timaeus' son) sitting by the roadside at Jericho (Mark 10:46-47). The correct answer is A (blind Bartimaeus).

'Blessed are you among women and blessed is the fruit of your womb' — this greeting was spoken by Elizabeth to Mary when Mary visited her during their pregnancies (Luke 1:42). The correct answer is D (Elizabeth said this to Mary/when Mary visited Elizabeth).

When complaints were made to the apostles about the neglect of Hellenist widows, the apostles told the community to choose seven men full of the Spirit and wisdom to handle the daily distribution — they appointed deacons (Acts 6:2-6). The correct answer is C (they instructed the community to choose seven deacons to handle food distribution).

'Cursed be the man who takes food before evening, before I have been avenged on my enemies' — this oath was made by Saul during the battle with the Philistines, which Jonathan unknowingly violated by eating honey (1 Samuel 14:24). The correct answer is D (Saul made this oath before the battle, which Jonathan unknowingly violated).

'Which is better for you, that all seventy of the sons of Jerubbaal rule over you, or that one man rule?' — this question was asked by Jotham (the youngest son of Gideon/Jerubbaal) in his parable from Mount Gerizim (Judges 9:2). The correct answer is A (Jotham, from Mount Gerizim).

'Rule over us, you and your son and your grandson also; for you have delivered us from the hand of Midian' — this was addressed to Gideon by the Israelites who wanted him to be their king (Judges 8:22). The correct answer is C (the Israelites said this to Gideon after his victory over Midian).

The man who, in an attempt to prevent a disaster, touched the Ark of the Covenant and was struck dead was Uzzah (also spelled Uzzah) — when the Ark was being transported and the oxen stumbled, he reached out and touched it (2 Samuel 6:6-7). The correct answer is C (Uzzah).

At childhood, the word of the Lord came to Samuel because the Lord had chosen to reveal Himself to Samuel and reveal His plans — Samuel did not yet know the Lord (1 Samuel 3:7). The correct answer is C (the Lord chose Samuel/Samuel did not yet know the Lord but God revealed Himself to him).

The suggestion made by Prophet Nathan to Bathsheba to foil Adonijah's plot (to become king in place of David's appointed heir Solomon) was to go to King David and remind him of his oath that Solomon would be king (1 Kings 1:11-14). The correct answer is B (go to King David and remind him of his oath that Solomon would be king).

'The jar of meal shall not be spent and the cruse of oil shall not fail' — Elijah the prophet said this to the widow of Zarephath, who had used her last flour and oil to make bread for him (1 Kings 17:14). The correct answer is C (Elijah said this to the widow of Zarephath).

'He burned his son as an offering, practised soothsaying and divination' — this refers to King Ahaz of Judah, who engaged in the most extreme forms of pagan worship (2 Kings 16:3; 2 Chronicles 28:3). The correct answer is B (King Ahaz of Judah).

'Then the spirit of the Lord will come mightily upon you, and you shall prophesy with them and be turned into another man' — this was said to Saul by Samuel when Saul was anointed and sent to meet a band of prophets (1 Samuel 10:6). The correct answer is B (Samuel said this to Saul at his anointing).

The evil spirit that tormented Saul left him whenever David played the lyre (harp) — the music soothed Saul when the evil spirit was upon him (1 Samuel 16:23). The correct answer is D (David played the lyre/harp for him).

When the Queen of Sheba heard of Solomon's fame concerning the name of the Lord, she came to test him with hard questions (1 Kings 10:1). The correct answer is A (she came to test him with hard questions).

Besides wisdom, the Lord also promised Solomon riches and honour — 'I give you also what you have not asked, both riches and honour, so that no other king shall compare with you all your days' (1 Kings 3:13). The correct answer is C (riches and honour).

Though Herod wanted to put John the Baptist to death, he feared the people because they regarded John as a prophet (Matthew 14:5). The correct answer is C (he feared the people who regarded John as a prophet).

Jesus asked his disciples not to disclose their vision of the transfiguration until after the Son of Man was raised from the dead (Matthew 17:9). The correct answer is B (until after the Son of Man rose from the dead).

NOT included in the instructions given to the disciples when Jesus sent them out: they were NOT to carry gold, silver, or copper; NOT to take a bag, two tunics, sandals, or a staff. Being given a sword to defend themselves is NOT in the instructions. The correct answer is B (the instruction not given to disciples).

'I have sinned this time; the Lord is in the right and I and my people are in the wrong' — Pharaoh said this to Moses after the plague of hail (Exodus 9:27). The correct answer is A (Pharaoh said this after the plague of hail/to Moses).

'Mahanaim is so called because Jacob saw the angels of God' as God's army/camp — when Jacob was returning from Paddan-aram, he met angels of God and named the place Mahanaim (meaning 'two camps') (Genesis 32:1-2). The correct answer is D (Jacob named it Mahanaim because he saw God's angels/camp).

Moses' request for Israel to be allowed to go and worship God was rejected by Pharaoh multiple times — Pharaoh kept hardening his heart after each plague and initially refused to let the people go (Exodus 5:1-2). The correct answer is B (Pharaoh rejected Moses' request/hardened his heart).

Pharaoh's horsemen and his army overtook the fleeing Hebrews encamped at the edge of the Red Sea — by the sea, beside Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, in front of Baal-zephon (Exodus 14:9). The correct answer is D (by the sea/beside Pi-hahiroth near Baal-zephon).

'Then render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's and to God the things that are God's' — Jesus said this to the Pharisees and Herodians who tried to trap him with a question about paying taxes to Caesar (Matthew 22:21). The correct answer is B (Jesus said this in response to the trick question about paying taxes).

Joseph of Arimathea requested the body of Jesus after his death — he was a rich man, a member of the council, who had not consented to the crucifixion (Matthew 27:57-58; Mark 15:43). The correct answer is D (Joseph of Arimathea).

'Did not our hearts burn within us while he talked to us on the road?' — this was expressed by the two disciples on the road to Emmaus after Jesus had explained the Scriptures to them (Luke 24:32). The correct answer is C (the two disciples on the road to Emmaus).

Paul was accused of being a preacher of foreign divinities at Athens because he preached Jesus and the resurrection — 'He seems to be a preacher of foreign divinities because he preached Jesus and the resurrection' (Acts 17:18). The correct answer is C (he preached Jesus and the resurrection).

Paul told the Athenians that they were very religious because he had observed an altar with the inscription 'To the Unknown God' — showing their thoroughness in worship of unknown gods (Acts 17:23). The correct answer is B (he saw their altars, including one to an unknown God).

'Do not be afraid, but speak and do not be silent, for I am with you, and no one will attack you to harm you' — the Lord said this to Paul in a vision at Corinth, encouraging him to stay and preach (Acts 18:9-10). The correct answer is A (the Lord said this to Paul in a vision at Corinth).

To the Philippian jailer's question 'What must I do to be saved?', Paul and Silas replied: 'Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household' (Acts 16:31). The correct answer is B ('Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ').

The elders at Jerusalem advised Paul on his arrival to the city to purify himself along with four men who had taken a vow, to show that he lived in observance of the law (Acts 21:23-24). The correct answer is B (to purify himself and join the men with a vow to show he lived by the law).

'Let it be known to you then that this salvation of God has been sent to the Gentiles; they will listen' — Paul said this to the Jewish leaders in Rome after they refused to believe his message (Acts 28:28). The correct answer is A (Paul said this to the Jews in Rome who rejected his message).

The two disciples on the road to Emmaus recognised Jesus in the breaking of bread — when He took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them, their eyes were opened (Luke 24:30-31). The correct answer is D (in the breaking of bread).

'Then after fasting and praying, they laid their hands on them and sent them off' — this refers to the church at Antioch commissioning Paul and Barnabas for their first missionary journey (Acts 13:2-3). The correct answer is A (the church at Antioch commissioned Paul and Barnabas).

The reason for the first Apostolic Council in Jerusalem was that certain men from Judea were teaching that Gentile believers must be circumcised to be saved — this controversy needed resolution (Acts 15:1-2). The correct answer is B (controversy over whether Gentiles must be circumcised to be saved).

'You shall indeed hear but never understand, and you shall indeed see but never perceive' — Paul quoted this prophecy of Isaiah when the Jewish leaders in Rome refused to believe his message (Acts 28:26-27; Isaiah 6:9-10). The correct answer is A (Paul quoted Isaiah to the unbelieving Jews in Rome).

The Jews asked Jesus whether they should pay tax or not because they wanted to trap him in his words — if he said yes, they could accuse him of being pro-Roman; if no, they could accuse him of sedition (Matthew 22:15-16). The correct answer is A (to trap/test him with the question).

'For the Son of Man also came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many' — Jesus said this when James and John requested positions of honour (Mark 10:45). The correct answer is C (Jesus said this to James and John/to teach about servant leadership).

'I have no silver and gold, but I give you what I have; In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, rise up and walk!' — Peter said this to the lame man at the Beautiful Gate of the Temple (Acts 3:6). The correct answer is C (Peter said this to the lame man at the Temple gate).

'But when they recognised that he was a Jew, for about two hours they all cried out with one voice, Great is Artemis of the Ephesians' — this was the crowd's response in Ephesus when Paul's preaching threatened the silversmith trade (Acts 19:34). The correct answer is B (the Ephesian crowd chanting 'Great is Artemis' against Paul's message).

Very early on the first day of the week (Sunday), three women who went to the tomb were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome (Mark 16:1). The correct answer is C (Mary Magdalene, Mary mother of James, and Salome).

'Let all the house of Israel therefore know assuredly that God has made him both Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified' — Peter declared this on the Day of Pentecost after the outpouring of the Holy Spirit (Acts 2:36). The correct answer is C (Peter declared this on the Day of Pentecost).

'You have not lied to man but to God' — Peter said this to Ananias. The immediate effect of this was that Ananias fell down and died immediately (Acts 5:5). The correct answer is C (Ananias fell down and died immediately).

When Saul escaped from Damascus to Jerusalem after his conversion, the disciples in Jerusalem were afraid of him because they did not believe he was truly a disciple (Acts 9:26). The correct answer is B (the disciples were afraid and did not believe he had truly converted).

The apostles created a new office — deacons — to handle the daily distribution (service/ministry) of food to widows, so the apostles could focus on prayer and the ministry of the word (Acts 6:1-4). The correct answer is A (deacons — to serve tables/handle food distribution).

'Abstain from what has been sacrificed to idols and from blood and from what has been strangled and from sexual immorality' — this was the decision of the Jerusalem Council regarding requirements for Gentile believers (Acts 15:29). The correct answer is B (the Jerusalem Council's requirements for Gentile believers).

'I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees; it is with respect to the hope and the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial' — Paul said this before the Sanhedrin, cleverly dividing the Pharisees from the Sadducees (Acts 23:6). The correct answer is C (Paul said this before the Sanhedrin to divide the council).

Paul and Barnabas were referred to as 'gods' in Lystra because they healed a man who had been lame from birth — the people concluded that gods had come down to them in human form (Acts 14:11-12). The correct answer is C (they healed a lame man, and the people thought they were gods).

According to Paul, the greatest of faith, hope, and love is love (charity) — 'And now these three remain: faith, hope, and love. But the greatest of these is love' (1 Corinthians 13:13). The correct answer is B (love/charity).

The law book used for the great reformation of Israel's social and religious institutions was the book of the law — the book of Moses found in the Temple during Josiah's reign (2 Kings 22:8; 23:2). The correct answer is A (the book of the law/book of Moses found in the Temple).

The prophet of hope in Babylon (during the exile) was the Deutero-Isaiah (Second Isaiah) — chapters 40-55 of Isaiah contain comfort and hope for the exiles in Babylon: 'Comfort, comfort my people' (Isaiah 40:1). The correct answer is B (Second Isaiah/Deutero-Isaiah).

In Paul's letter, Paul explains that everyone, both the Jews and Gentiles, need salvation — this is the theme of Romans where Paul shows all have sinned and need God's righteousness. The correct answer is D (the Romans — Paul's letter to the Romans explains universal need for salvation).
Paul's companion on his First Missionary Journey was Barnabas (and John Mark initially) — they were sent out from the church at Antioch (Acts 13:2-3). The correct answer is A (Barnabas).

The Holy Spirit descended on the followers of Christ and they began to speak in other tongues (languages) as the Spirit gave them utterance — this was the event of Pentecost (Acts 2:4). The correct answer is E (they spoke in other tongues/languages).
David took Jerusalem from the Jebusites — he captured the stronghold of Zion (the City of David) from the Jebusites (2 Samuel 5:6-7). The correct answer is A (the Jebusites).

In Mark's Gospel, the women are told at the empty tomb that Jesus has risen and they should go tell His disciples and Peter that He is going before them to Galilee (Mark 16:6-7). The correct answer is C (to go tell the disciples that Jesus has risen and will meet them in Galilee).

Jeremiah the prophet was called to prophesy to Israel and the nations before he was born — God told him 'Before I formed you in the womb I knew you' — Jeremiah was known as the 'weeping prophet' who prophesied the fall of Jerusalem. The correct answer is C (prophesied before his birth/was appointed before birth).

In the parable of the friend at midnight, the man will get up and give his friend bread not because of friendship but because of the man's persistence/boldness/shamelessness — teaching perseverance in prayer (Luke 11:8). The correct answer is B (because of the man's persistence/boldness in asking).

Gamaliel advised the council to release the apostles because if their work is of human origin it will fail, but if it is from God, they cannot stop it — and they might be fighting against God (Acts 5:38-39). The correct answer is D (if it is from God, they cannot stop it — they might be fighting God).
Martha's sister was called Mary — when Jesus visited their home, Martha was busy serving while Mary sat at Jesus' feet listening to his teaching (Luke 10:39). The correct answer is B (Mary).
Isaac's wife was Rebekah — chosen by Abraham's servant and brought from Mesopotamia (Paddan-aram) to be Isaac's wife (Genesis 24:67). The correct answer is A (Rebekah).

Israel (Jacob) charged his people to bury him in the cave of Machpelah in the field of Ephron the Hittite, with his fathers Abraham and Isaac (Genesis 49:29-30). The correct answer is C (in the cave of Machpelah with his fathers).

After his arrest in Jerusalem, Paul was supported by the Pharisees because he claimed he was on trial for his belief in the resurrection of the dead — the Pharisees believed in resurrection while the Sadducees did not (Acts 23:8-9). The correct answer is B (he claimed he was on trial for belief in the resurrection).

The last plague inflicted upon the Egyptians was the death of the firstborn — the death angel passed through Egypt killing the firstborn of every family not protected by the blood of the Passover lamb (Exodus 12:29). The correct answer is E (death of the firstborn).
Moses, after killing the Egyptian who was beating a Hebrew, fled to the land of Midian — he settled there, married Zipporah, and lived as a shepherd (Exodus 2:15). The correct answer is B (Midian).

The Acts of the Apostles tells the story of how the early Church grew and spread from Jerusalem to all parts of the world, guided by the Holy Spirit (Acts 1:8). The correct answer is A (how the early Church grew and spread through the Holy Spirit).
The Acts of the Apostles was initially written for Theophilus — Luke addressed both his Gospel and Acts to 'most excellent Theophilus' (Luke 1:3; Acts 1:1). The correct answer is B (Theophilus).

Paul's First Missionary Journey started from Antioch in Syria — the church at Antioch laid hands on Paul and Barnabas and sent them off (Acts 13:1-3). The correct answer is D (Antioch/Syrian Antioch).
The first Christian martyr was Stephen — he was stoned to death after his powerful sermon before the Sanhedrin (Acts 7:59-60). The correct answer is C (Stephen).

Paul and Barnabas were mistaken for gods in Lystra — after they healed a crippled man, the crowd called Barnabas 'Zeus' and Paul 'Hermes' (Acts 14:12). The correct answer is E (Paul and Barnabas — called Zeus and Hermes by the Lystrans).
Deborah was a prophetess and judge in Israel — the only female judge mentioned in the book of Judges (Judges 4:4). The correct answer is D (a prophetess and judge).
God commanded Abraham to circumcise his male descendants as a sign of the covenant between God and Abraham (Genesis 17:10-11). The correct answer is B (a sign of the covenant).
During the time of Amos the prophet, Amaziah was the priest of Bethel — Amaziah told Amos to stop prophesying in Bethel and go back to Judah (Amos 7:10-13). The correct answer is A (Amaziah).

The king of Assyria who took (captured) Samaria was Shalmaneser V (2 Kings 17:3-6) — he besieged Samaria for three years and then Sargon II completed its capture. The correct answer is B (Shalmaneser/Sargon of Assyria).
'The soul that sins shall die' — this prophecy was given by Ezekiel, who emphasised individual responsibility for sin (Ezekiel 18:4). The correct answer is E (Ezekiel).

The meaning of Emmanuel (Immanuel) is 'God with us' — 'Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel' (Isaiah 7:14; Matthew 1:23). The correct answer is C (God with us).

About almsgiving, Jesus says when you give your gift (alms), you should not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing — give in secret, so the Father who sees in secret will reward you (Matthew 6:3-4). The correct answer is C (give secretly/not let the left hand know what the right does).

Mark's Gospel starts with the baptism of Jesus by John the Baptist — there is no birth narrative; it begins with 'The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God' and then goes straight to John's ministry (Mark 1:1-4). The correct answer is C (the ministry of John the Baptist/baptism of Jesus).

Pilate released Barabbas in place of Jesus — Barabbas was a robber/murderer and revolutionary whom the crowd chose to be freed instead of Jesus (Matthew 27:26; John 18:40). The correct answer is D (Barabbas).

Matthias was chosen in place of Judas Iscariot — he was selected by lot from two candidates (Joseph Barsabbas and Matthias) to restore the twelve apostles (Acts 1:26). The correct answer is D (Matthias).

According to Luke, the first statement made by Jesus on the cross was 'Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do' — a prayer for those who crucified him (Luke 23:34). The correct answer is C ('Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do').

The promise of God made with Abraham was that he would be the father of many nations and his descendants would be as numerous as the stars — and through him all nations would be blessed (Genesis 17:4-5). The correct answer is A (he would be father of many nations/his seed would inherit the land).

The name Moses means 'drawn out' or 'because I drew him out of the water' — Pharaoh's daughter named him Moses when she found him floating in the basket on the Nile (Exodus 2:10). The correct answer is E ('drawn out of the water').

One reason Saul was rejected as king was that he disobeyed God's command to destroy the Amalekites completely — he spared King Agag and the best animals, keeping them against God's instructions (1 Samuel 15:9-11). The correct answer is B (he disobeyed God's command regarding the Amalekites).

God's covenant with Abraham took the form of circumcision — as a sign of the covenant, every male among Abraham's descendants was to be circumcised (Genesis 17:10-13). The correct answer is B (circumcision as the sign of the covenant).

The great reformation of Israel's social and religious institutions took place during the reign of King Josiah — who removed idols, repaired the Temple, celebrated Passover, and reinstated the law (2 Kings 22-23). The correct answer is B (King Josiah).

'But as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord' — this statement was made by Joshua when he challenged the Israelites to choose whom they would serve (Joshua 24:15). The correct answer is E (Joshua said this at Shechem).

Gideon was called Jerubbaal because he tore down Baal's altar and cut down the Asherah pole — 'Let Baal contend against him, because he has broken down his altar' (Judges 6:32). The correct answer is A (he broke down Baal's altar — 'Let Baal contend with him').

'Bring your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon and serve him' — Jeremiah said this to the kings who sent envoys to King Zedekiah, urging them to submit to Nebuchadnezzar (Jeremiah 27:12). The correct answer is A (Jeremiah urged submission to Babylon).

David was responsible for the death of Uriah the Hittite — David arranged for Uriah to be put at the front of the fiercest battle so he would die, in order to hide his adultery with Bathsheba (2 Samuel 11:15). The correct answer is A (David).

Jephthah vowed that if he defeated the Ammonites, he would sacrifice as a burnt offering whatever came out of his house first to greet him — which turned out to be his daughter (Judges 11:30-31). The correct answer is C (he would offer as a burnt offering whatever came out of his house first).
The meaning of the name Samuel is 'heard of God' or 'asked of God' — Hannah said 'I have asked him of the Lord' (1 Samuel 1:20). The correct answer is B ('heard/asked of God').

Ezekiel was usually referred to as the prophet of the exile/hope — he prophesied to the exiles in Babylon and gave hope of restoration. The correct answer is A (the exile/prophet of hope to the exiles).

The King of Assyria took Samaria and carried Israel away into Assyria because the Israelites had sinned against God, rejected His laws, followed other gods, and did not obey His commands (2 Kings 17:7-12). The correct answer is B (their persistent sin and disobedience to God/following other gods).

'The lion has roared; who will not fear? The Lord God has spoken; who can but prophesy?' — this was said by Amos (Amos 3:8), expressing the compulsion he felt to prophesy when God spoke. The correct answer is E (Amos).

'My father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions' — Rehoboam said this to the Israelites when they asked for lighter taxation, following the advice of his young friends rather than the elders (1 Kings 12:14). The correct answer is C (Rehoboam said this to the Israelites/northern tribes).

Sisera was put to death by Jael — the wife of Heber the Kenite, who drove a tent peg through his temple while he slept in her tent after fleeing from Deborah and Barak's forces (Judges 4:21). The correct answer is C (Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite).

David first reigned as king in Hebron — he was anointed king over the tribe of Judah in Hebron, where he reigned for seven and a half years before moving to Jerusalem (2 Samuel 2:4; 5:5). The correct answer is B (Hebron).

The kingdom of Judah was finally defeated by the Babylonians (Nebuchadnezzar's forces) — Jerusalem was destroyed, the Temple burned, and the people taken into exile in Babylon (2 Kings 25:8-11). The correct answer is B (Babylon/the Babylonians).
The judges of Israel include: Othniel, Ehud, Deborah, Gideon, Jephthah, Samson, Eli, Samuel. The correct answer is E (the judge listed among the options — Samson, Gideon, Deborah, etc.).

'If this plan or this undertaking is of men, it will fail; but if it is of God, you will not be able to overthrow them' — Gamaliel said this to the Sanhedrin about the apostles, urging them not to persecute them (Acts 5:38-39). The correct answer is A (Gamaliel said this to the Sanhedrin).

Stephen was stoned to death because of his unyielding devotion to the Gospel — he was the first Christian martyr, killed by the Sanhedrin after his powerful speech (Acts 7:57-60). The correct answer is E (Stephen).

The term 'sons of thunder' (Boanerges) was applied by Jesus to James and John, the sons of Zebedee — because of their fiery temperament (Mark 3:17). The correct answer is B (James and John, the sons of Zebedee).

In the Acts of the Apostles, Philip was one of the seven deacons chosen to serve tables — he also became an evangelist, preaching in Samaria and to the Ethiopian eunuch (Acts 6:5; 8:5). The correct answer is B (one of the seven deacons/an evangelist).

Herod's son who succeeded his father as ruler of Judea was Archelaus — when Herod died, his kingdom was divided among his sons; Archelaus received Judea and Samaria (Matthew 2:22). The correct answer is D (Archelaus).

Saul (later Paul) was a persecutor of the church before his conversion — he consented to Stephen's stoning and went house to house dragging off Christians to prison (Acts 8:3). The correct answer is E (Saul/Paul).

'This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased' — this statement was made at the baptism of Jesus, when the Spirit descended like a dove and God spoke from heaven (Matthew 3:17; Mark 1:11). The correct answer is C (God/the Father said this at Jesus' baptism).
Moses and Elijah appeared to Jesus on the Mount of Transfiguration — they represented the Law (Moses) and the Prophets (Elijah) (Matthew 17:3; Mark 9:4). The correct answer is D (Moses and Elijah).

Jesus said 'I will; be clean' to a leper who came to him saying 'Lord, if you will, you can make me clean' — Jesus stretched out his hand and touched him, and he was immediately healed (Matthew 8:2-3). The correct answer is C (a leper who asked to be made clean).
The disciples were first called Christians at Antioch — 'And in Antioch the disciples were first called Christians' (Acts 11:26). The correct answer is A (Antioch).

The story of the prodigal son indicates that God is forgiving/merciful — the father (representing God) runs to meet his returning son, showing God's unconditional love and eagerness to forgive repentant sinners (Luke 15:20). The correct answer is E (forgiving/merciful/loving).
Complete: 'Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven' (Matthew 5:3). The correct answer is D (for theirs is the kingdom of heaven).
After his resurrection, Jesus first appeared to Mary Magdalene — who had stayed at the tomb weeping (Mark 16:9; John 20:14-16). The correct answer is A (Mary Magdalene).
Paul cured a slave girl who had a spirit of divination (pythonic spirit) in Philippi — this led to his and Silas' arrest and imprisonment (Acts 16:16-18). The correct answer is A (Philippi).

Peter declared the messiahship of Jesus at Caesarea Philippi — when Jesus asked 'Who do you say I am?', Peter answered 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God' (Matthew 16:13-16). The correct answer is B (Caesarea Philippi).

'This night your soul is required of you' — this statement is found in the parable of the Rich Fool (Luke 12:20), when God says this to the man who built bigger barns. The correct answer is D (the parable of the Rich Fool in Luke).

Peter was released from prison as a result of the prayer of the church — the believers were earnestly praying for him, and an angel appeared and released him from Herod's prison (Acts 12:5-11). The correct answer is D (the prayers of the church/believers).

Jesus cursed a fig tree because it had leaves but no fruit — it symbolised Israel's outward religiosity without genuine faith/fruit for God (Matthew 21:19; Mark 11:13-14). The correct answer is C (it had leaves but bore no fruit/represented fruitless religion).

Before Jacob died, he asked his children to bury him in the cave of Machpelah in the field of Ephron the Hittite — where Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebekah were buried (Genesis 49:29-30). The correct answer is A (the cave of Machpelah/with his fathers).

Abraham and his nephew Lot decided to separate into different camps because their herdsmen were quarrelling over the land that could not support both their large flocks (Genesis 13:6-9). The correct answer is D (the land could not support both their flocks/their herdsmen quarrelled).
At the bank of the River Jabbok, the name of Jacob was changed to Israel — after he wrestled with the divine being/angel through the night (Genesis 32:28). The correct answer is C (Jacob).
Othniel was one of the Judges of Israel — the first judge mentioned in the book of Judges who delivered Israel from Cushan-rishathaim (Judges 3:9). The correct answer is A (Othniel/the judge listed).

The name Abraham means 'father of many nations' or 'father of a multitude' — God changed his name from Abram ('exalted father') to Abraham when making the covenant (Genesis 17:5). The correct answer is D ('father of many nations/multitude').

God promised Abraham in the covenant that his descendants would be as numerous as the stars, that he would be the father of many nations, and that Canaan would be given to his descendants as an eternal possession (Genesis 17:4-8). The correct answer is C (his descendants would inherit the land/be as numerous as the stars).

Joshua's first military victory was over the people of Jericho — after the Israelites marched around the city for seven days, the walls fell and they conquered Jericho (Joshua 6:20). The correct answer is D (Jericho/the people of Jericho).

The laws given by Moses to the children of Israel have striking similarities with the Code of Hammurabi — both contain similar civil and criminal laws showing the common ancient Near Eastern legal tradition. The correct answer is C (the Code of Hammurabi).

The period of bondage of the children of Israel in Egypt was characterised by harsh slavery and forced labour — building store cities for Pharaoh under cruel taskmasters (Exodus 1:11-14). The correct answer is C (harsh slavery/forced labour under cruel oppression).
