Elijah was a prophet during the reign of Ahab — the Bible says 'Now Elijah the Tishbite... said to Ahab...' (1 Kings 17:1). He was the great prophet who challenged Ahab and Jezebel's Baal worship. The correct answer is B (Ahab).

Saul was rejected by God because of his disobedience — specifically for disobeying God's command to destroy the Amalekites completely and for keeping the best livestock and King Agag (1 Samuel 15:23). The correct answer is A (his disobedience to God's commands).
'When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son' — this was said by God through the prophet Hosea (Hosea 11:1). The correct answer is A (Hosea).

Joab murdered Abner because Abner had killed Asahel (Joab's brother) during the battle at Gibeon — Joab took revenge by killing Abner treacherously at Hebron (2 Samuel 3:27, 30). The correct answer is A (revenge for Abner killing his brother Asahel).

'But let justice roll down like waters and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream' — Amos (Amos 5:24). The complete statement is: 'let justice roll down like waters and righteousness like an overflowing stream'. The correct answer is D (righteousness like an overflowing stream).

The division of the kingdom of Israel took place during the reign of Rehoboam (Solomon's son) — when he refused to lighten the people's burden, the northern ten tribes rebelled under Jeroboam (1 Kings 12:16-20). The correct answer is A (Rehoboam).

David was brought to Saul's palace initially because he was a skilled musician/lyre player — Saul's servants recommended David to play music to soothe Saul when the evil spirit tormented him (1 Samuel 16:18-23). The correct answer is C (to play music and soothe Saul when the evil spirit troubled him).

The exiles returned to Jerusalem in the reign of Cyrus the Great of Persia — he issued a decree allowing the Jewish exiles to return and rebuild the Temple (Ezra 1:1-4). The correct answer is A (Cyrus the Great/king of Persia).

A prophet of hope in Babylon was Second Isaiah (Deutero-Isaiah) — Isaiah chapters 40-55 are often attributed to a prophet in Babylon who comforted exiles with messages of hope and return (Isaiah 40:1-2). The correct answer is B (Second Isaiah/Deutero-Isaiah).

Jesus' teaching about swearing was that one should not swear at all — 'Do not swear at all: either by heaven... or by the earth... Let what you say be simply 'Yes' or 'No'' (Matthew 5:34-37). The correct answer is E (not at all — let your yes be yes and no be no).
The Acts of the Apostles was written by Luke — the same author of the Gospel of Luke, addressing both books to Theophilus (Acts 1:1; Luke 1:3). The correct answer is C (Luke).

Hezekiah (king of Judah) ran to prophet Isaiah for prayers when the Assyrians threatened Jerusalem under King Sennacherib — God responded through Isaiah promising Jerusalem would be delivered (Isaiah 37:1-6; 2 Kings 19:1-7). The correct answer is B (Hezekiah).

Matthew's Gospel relates the death of Judas — 'When Judas, who had betrayed him, saw that Jesus was condemned, he was seized with remorse and returned the thirty pieces of silver... and went away and hanged himself' (Matthew 27:3-5). The correct answer is B (Matthew).

Gamaliel defended the Apostles before the Sanhedrin — he advised the council to leave them alone, for if their work was from God, they could not stop it (Acts 5:34-39). The correct answer is C (Gamaliel).

The last temptation of Jesus by the devil was to bow down and worship Satan in exchange for all the kingdoms of the world — 'All these I will give you, if you will fall down and worship me' (Matthew 4:9-10). The correct answer is C (to bow down and worship Satan for all the kingdoms of the world).

The promise of sending the Holy Spirit was fulfilled on the Day of Pentecost — fifty days after Easter/Passover, when the Spirit came upon the disciples in Jerusalem with wind and fire (Acts 2:1-4). The correct answer is D (Pentecost/the Day of Pentecost).
'Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness' sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven' (Matthew 5:10). The correct answer is E (for theirs is the kingdom of heaven).
Ephphatha means 'Be opened' — Jesus said this when he healed a deaf-mute man by putting his fingers in his ears and touching his tongue (Mark 7:34). The correct answer is A ('Be opened').

The Council of Jerusalem decided that Gentiles should abstain from pollutions of idols, from sexual immorality, from what is strangled, and from blood (Acts 15:29). The correct answer is C (food offered to idols, blood, strangled animals, and sexual immorality).

According to Mark's Gospel, Herod said that Jesus was John the Baptist raised from the dead — because he had beheaded John and felt guilty (Mark 6:16). The correct answer is C (John the Baptist raised from the dead).

In the parable of the ten virgins, the foolish ones are blamed because they did not take extra oil with their lamps — they ran out of oil when the bridegroom was delayed and were shut out (Matthew 25:8-12). The correct answer is C (they did not take extra oil/were unprepared).

Jesus was presented in the Temple of the Lord because it was required by the law of Moses — every firstborn male was to be consecrated to God (Exodus 13:2; Luke 2:22-24). The correct answer is C (it was required by the law of Moses for every firstborn).

Jesus healed the leper at Galilee because He was moved with compassion/pity — the leper said 'if you will, you can make me clean' and Jesus, moved with compassion, touched and healed him (Mark 1:41). The correct answer is C (He was moved with compassion/pity).

'Truly this man was the Son of God' — this statement was made by a Roman centurion (soldier) who was present at the crucifixion of Jesus (Mark 15:39; Matthew 27:54). The correct answer is A (the centurion/Roman soldier at the cross).

The canticle beginning 'Blessed be the Lord God of Israel' (the Benedictus) was uttered by Zechariah — the father of John the Baptist, after his tongue was loosed following the naming of his son (Luke 1:68). The correct answer is B (Zechariah).

The parable peculiar to Luke (found only in Luke's Gospel) includes the Good Samaritan, the Prodigal Son, the Rich Man and Lazarus. The correct answer is D (the parable found only in Luke — e.g., the Prodigal Son/Good Samaritan).
Matthias was the one chosen to make up the twelve apostles in place of Judas — selected by lot after prayer (Acts 1:26). The correct answer is D (Matthias).

'O man of little faith, why did you doubt?' — Jesus said this to Peter when he began to sink after walking on water toward Jesus (Matthew 14:31). The correct answer is C (Jesus said this to Peter when he began to sink while walking on water).

The Sadducees did not believe in the resurrection — they also rejected oral tradition and believed only in the written Torah. This is stated in Acts 23:8 and Matthew 22:23. The correct answer is E (Sadducees).

'Beware of practicing your piety before men in order to be seen by them' — this statement is from Jesus' Sermon on the Mount regarding almsgiving, prayer, and fasting (Matthew 6:1). The correct answer is B (Jesus said this in the Sermon on the Mount about religious hypocrisy).
Parables teaching about God's love include: the Prodigal Son, the Lost Sheep, the Lost Coin. The correct answer is E (the parable listed that teaches about God's unconditional love for sinners).

Saul was pleased when told that his daughter Michal was in love with David because he saw it as an opportunity to use her as a snare/trap against David by the hand of the Philistines (1 Samuel 18:21). The correct answer is D (he wanted to use Michal as a snare/trap against David).

God changed the name of Abraham's wife from Sarai to Sarah when He established the covenant of circumcision — promising she would bear a son (Genesis 17:15-16). The correct answer is D (when God established the covenant of circumcision with Abraham).
Moses was nursed by his own mother — Pharaoh's daughter paid his mother (Jochebed) to nurse him as a baby (Exodus 2:9). The correct answer is C (his own mother/Jochebed).

Hosea married Gomer, a harlot, to symbolize the unfaithfulness of Israel to God — God used Hosea's marriage to an unfaithful wife as a living parable of Israel's spiritual adultery/idolatry (Hosea 1:2). The correct answer is A (unfaithfulness/spiritual adultery of Israel toward God).

Amos condemned the women of Samaria and called them 'cows of Bashan' — referring to the wealthy, pampered women who oppressed the poor and demanded their husbands bring them drinks (Amos 4:1). The correct answer is D (cows of Bashan).

The valiant men of Jabesh-gilead buried Saul and his sons — they traveled all night, took the bodies from Beth-shan, burned and buried them under a tamarisk tree in Jabesh (1 Samuel 31:11-13). The correct answer is B (the men of Jabesh-gilead).

Nebuchadnezzar (king of Babylon) carried Judah into captivity — he conquered Jerusalem, burned the Temple, and took the people into exile in Babylon (2 Kings 25:1-12). The correct answer is B (Nebuchadnezzar/the Babylonians).

'As the Lord the God of Israel lives, before whom I stand, there shall be neither dew nor rain these years, except by my word' — Elijah said this to King Ahab at the beginning of the drought (1 Kings 17:1). The correct answer is A (Elijah said this to Ahab).

'The soul that sins shall die' (Ezekiel 18:4) indicates individual responsibility for sin — each person will be judged for their own sins, not inherited from parents (Ezekiel 18:20). The correct answer is A (individual responsibility for sin).

Saul, the first king of Israel, was of the tribe of Benjamin — 'There was a man of Benjamin whose name was Kish... He had a son whose name was Saul' (1 Samuel 9:1-2). The correct answer is E (Benjamin).

'The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge' — this proverb was used to argue that children suffer for their fathers' sins, which Ezekiel refuted by emphasising individual responsibility (Ezekiel 18:2-4). The correct answer is B (Ezekiel used it to teach about individual responsibility).

The mountain where Moses saw the burning bush was Horeb (also called Sinai) — the mountain of God where God appeared to Moses and commissioned him (Exodus 3:1-2). The correct answer is A (Horeb/Mount Horeb).
Isaac's wife Rebekah was the sister of Laban — she was the daughter of Bethuel and the granddaughter of Nahor, Abraham's brother (Genesis 24:29; 29:10). The correct answer is C (Laban).

Moses offered his own life for the people by asking God to forgive them or else blot him out of God's book — after the incident of the golden calf (Exodus 32:32). The correct answer is D (to be blotted from God's book/sacrificed himself for Israel's forgiveness).

The prophet from Tekoa whose main concern was social justice was Amos — 'The words of Amos, who was among the shepherds of Tekoa' (Amos 1:1). He condemned oppression of the poor and called for justice. The correct answer is B (Amos).

The prophet who demonstrated that Yahweh is more powerful than Baal was Elijah — at the contest on Mount Carmel, God sent fire to consume Elijah's sacrifice while Baal could not respond (1 Kings 18:38-39). The correct answer is B (Elijah).

The prophet who rebuked King David for having Uriah killed and committing adultery with Bathsheba was Nathan — he told David the parable of the ewe lamb and then declared 'You are the man!' (2 Samuel 12:7). The correct answer is E (Nathan).

The children of Israel wanted to have their own king so they could be like all other nations — 'Give us a king to judge us like all the nations' (1 Samuel 8:5). The correct answer is B (to be like all other nations).

The instrument used by God to destroy Babylon and set the Israelites free was Cyrus, king of Persia — God called him His anointed who would overthrow Babylon and decree the return of the exiles (Isaiah 45:1). The correct answer is A (Cyrus, king of Persia).

King Jehoiachin of Judah and a large number of the kingdom's able-bodied men were taken into captivity by Nebuchadnezzar to Babylon — the first major deportation (2 Kings 24:14-16). The correct answer is A (taken to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar in the first major deportation).

After the death of Solomon, the kingdom was split but Judah and some Benjaminites (the tribe of Benjamin) remained loyal to Rehoboam and the house of David (1 Kings 12:21). The correct answer is D (Benjamin/the tribe of Benjamin stayed with Judah).
Saul was the first anointed king of Israel who took over from Samuel — Samuel anointed Saul as the first king when the people demanded a king (1 Samuel 10:1). The correct answer is C (Saul).

One of the greatest achievements of David as king over Israel was capturing Jerusalem (the City of David) and making it the capital — David took the stronghold of Zion from the Jebusites and established it as his capital (2 Samuel 5:7). The correct answer is B (capturing Jerusalem and making it the capital/bringing the Ark to Jerusalem).
Stephen replied to the charge by arguing that the most High does not dwell in houses made with hands — God transcends any physical temple (Acts 7:48). The correct answer is D.
Herod was very glad to see Jesus because he had long desired to see him, hoping to witness a miracle (Luke 23:8). The correct answer is C.
Jesus told the parable of the Good Samaritan to show who is one's neighbour, in response to a lawyer's question 'Who is my neighbour?' (Luke 10:29-37). The correct answer is B.
Zacchaeus climbed up into a sycamore tree in order to see Jesus because he was short and could not see over the crowd (Luke 19:4). The correct answer is C.
Matthias was chosen by lot to take the place of Judas among the twelve apostles (Acts 1:26). The correct answer is B.
Jesus said that whoever humbles himself like a child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven (Matthew 18:4). The correct answer is E.
Bartimaeus, a blind beggar, was healed by Jesus at Jericho (Mark 10:46-52; Luke 18:35-43). The correct answer is C.

The healing of the paralytic demonstrates that Jesus has the authority to forgive sins — He forgave the man's sins before healing him, causing controversy among the scribes (Mark 2:5-10). The correct answer is D.
Jesus said 'Today you will be with me in paradise' to the penitent thief during His crucifixion (Luke 23:43). The correct answer is B.
Ananias and Sapphira kept back some of the proceeds of land they sold while pretending to give everything to the apostles (Acts 5:1-2). The correct answer is E.
Beelzebub is the prince of demons — the Pharisees accused Jesus of casting out demons by Beelzebub, the prince of demons (Matthew 12:24; Mark 3:22). The correct answer is D.
'Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani' means 'My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?' — Jesus cried this out on the cross (Mark 15:34). The correct answer is B.
God's love and forgiveness for repentant sinners are illustrated by the parable of the prodigal son, where the father runs to receive his returning son (Luke 15:11-32). The correct answer is B.
St. Luke's Gospel was addressed to Theophilus — 'It seemed good to me also...to write an orderly account for you, most excellent Theophilus' (Luke 1:3). The correct answer is E.

'God has shown me that I should not call any man common or unclean' was said by Peter in connection with his visit to Cornelius, after his vision of the sheet with unclean animals (Acts 10:28). The correct answer is B.
Paul's hometown was Tarsus — he identified himself as 'a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia' (Acts 21:39; 22:3). The correct answer is D.
'Corban' means 'given to God' — it was a declaration that a thing was dedicated to God, used as an excuse to avoid obligations to parents (Mark 7:11). The correct answer is D.
Tabitha (also called Dorcas) was raised from death at Joppa by Peter through prayer (Acts 9:36-40). The correct answer is A.

The one terrible sin the Pharisees were often condemned for was hypocrisy — Jesus called them hypocrites because they performed religious duties outwardly while their hearts were far from God (Matthew 23:13-29). The correct answer is C.
Jesus said 'Son, your sins are forgiven' to the paralytic who was let down through the roof by his friends (Mark 2:5; Luke 5:20). The correct answer is B.
Andrew was one of the disciples Jesus called as He was passing along the Sea of Galilee — Andrew and his brother Simon Peter were the first called (Mark 1:16-18). The correct answer is A.
Philip said to the Ethiopian eunuch 'Do you understand what you are reading?' as he approached the eunuch's chariot (Acts 8:30). The correct answer is B.
Esau was the first of the twins born to Isaac — he came out red all over, like a hairy garment (Genesis 25:25). The correct answer is C.

Meribah referred to the time when Moses brought water out of the rock — the people quarreled and tested the Lord, so the place was called Meribah (meaning 'quarreling') (Exodus 17:7; Numbers 20:13). The correct answer is E.

Gideon put God to test with a fleece of wool — he laid a fleece on the ground and asked God to make the fleece wet with dew while the ground remained dry, then the reverse (Judges 6:36-40). The correct answer is C.
'Choose this day whom you will serve' was said by Joshua when he was about to die, challenging the people to commit to serving the Lord (Joshua 24:15). The correct answer is B.

God instructed that if the Passover remained till morning it should be burnt — 'you shall let none of it remain until the morning; anything that remains until the morning you shall burn' (Exodus 12:10). The correct answer is C.
After Moses was picked up by Pharaoh's daughter, he was nursed by his own mother — Miriam arranged for Moses' mother to be the one to nurse him (Exodus 2:7-9). The correct answer is A.
After the Israelites divided the land by casting lots, they gave Joshua the city of Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim, which he had requested (Joshua 19:49-50). The correct answer is D.

'I tell you, if these were silent, the very stones would cry out' was said by Jesus at the triumphal entry into Jerusalem, when Pharisees asked Him to rebuke His disciples (Luke 19:40). The correct answer is C.
The significant miracle Jesus performed at Jericho was the healing of Bartimaeus the blind man (Mark 10:46-52; Luke 18:35-43). The correct answer is D.
When the Israelites saw that Moses stayed long at Mount Sinai, they asked Aaron to produce another god for them — 'make us gods who shall go before us' (Exodus 32:1). The correct answer is D.
Jacob loved Joseph more than any of his other children because he was the son of his old age (Genesis 37:3). The correct answer is A.
Saul wanted to kill David because Saul regarded David as a danger to his kingship — Saul saw David's growing popularity and feared he would take the throne (1 Samuel 18:8-9). The correct answer is E.
Elijah was a prophet during the reign of King Ahab of Israel (1 Kings 17:1; 18:1). The correct answer is B.

The elders of Israel agreed to make David king over Israel because God had promised to save Israel through David — 'The LORD said to you, You shall be shepherd of my people Israel, and you shall be prince over Israel' (2 Samuel 5:2). The correct answer is C.
Amos was a shepherd from Tekoa — 'The words of Amos, who was among the shepherds of Tekoa' (Amos 1:1). The correct answer is C.

Amos saw Bethel, Gilgal and other high places of worship as seats of corruption in the guise of worship — they had become places of idolatry and empty ritual rather than true worship (Amos 4:4; 5:5). The correct answer is B.

Prophet Isaiah assisted Hezekiah with prayers when Hezekiah was ill and facing death — Isaiah prayed and God added 15 years to Hezekiah's life (2 Kings 20:1-6; Isaiah 38:1-5). The correct answer is D.
Samuel judged Israel by going on a circuit annually — he made an annual circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah (1 Samuel 7:15-17). The correct answer is A.
Solomon's mother was Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah whom David had taken after committing adultery with her (2 Samuel 12:24; 1 Kings 1:11). The correct answer is B.
In order to maintain his harem, Solomon taxed his people heavily — he imposed heavy labor and tax burdens on Israel to support his lavish lifestyle (1 Kings 12:4). The correct answer is D.

King Josiah was popular because of his religious reforms — he tore down idols, destroyed high places, and renewed the covenant with God after the book of the law was found (2 Kings 23:1-25). The correct answer is C.

Jeremiah was the radical prophet who called on Israel to remember her desert days and made the most severe criticisms against priests and false prophets (Jeremiah 2:2; 6:13-14; 23:1-2). The correct answer is B.

The prophecy that Judah should expect a foe from the North came from Jeremiah — 'Out of the north evil shall break out on all the inhabitants of the land' (Jeremiah 1:14; 4:6). The correct answer is D.
Joel and Daniel were the prophets whose messages were no 'Hope' in Babylon — they focused on judgment and apocalyptic visions rather than comfort for exiles in Babylon. The correct answer is E.

Jesus condemned the tradition of Corban because it contradicted one's obligations to one's parents — people would declare their resources 'Corban' (given to God) to avoid supporting their parents, violating the command to honor father and mother (Mark 7:9-13). The correct answer is C.
In Matthew's Gospel, the 'cup' is a metaphor for suffering — Jesus prayed 'Let this cup pass from me' referring to His coming suffering and death (Matthew 26:39). The correct answer is C.

The Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5-7) best summarizes Jesus' teachings in Matthew's Gospel — it covers the Beatitudes, the Lord's Prayer, and extensive moral and spiritual instruction. The correct answer is C.
Philip baptized the Ethiopian Eunuch after explaining the scripture to him (Acts 8:38). The correct answer is E.
In the Beatitudes, 'for they shall inherit the earth' is said to the meek — 'Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth' (Matthew 5:5). The correct answer is D.
Philip was the first to preach in Samaria according to Acts — after the persecution following Stephen's death, Philip went down to Samaria and proclaimed Christ (Acts 8:5). The correct answer is E.

In answer to the Syrophoenician woman's request, Jesus first said 'it is not right to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs' — referring to the priority of the Jews first (Mark 7:27). The correct answer is B.
When Jesus was arrested, a young man followed Him but later ran away naked, leaving his linen cloth behind (Mark 14:51-52). The correct answer is D.

Luke's Gospel best presents Jesus as a man yet with authority — Luke emphasizes Jesus' humanity, compassion, and concern for all people, while showing His divine authority (Luke 1:1-4). The correct answer is B.
Thaddeus is the name of one of the original twelve apostles — also called Judas son of James (Matthew 10:3; Luke 6:16). The correct answer is A.
'A prophet is not without honor, except in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house' was said by Jesus at His rejection in Nazareth (Mark 6:4). The correct answer is C.

Jesus answered the question 'Why does he eat with tax collectors and sinners?' by saying 'Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick' — implying He came to call sinners (Mark 2:17). The correct answer is A.

The parable of the prodigal son signifies God's love for all men — the father's unconditional acceptance of his returning son represents God's universal love and forgiveness (Luke 15:11-32). The correct answer is D.
In answer to the question 'Who is my neighbor?' Jesus told the parable of the Good Samaritan (Luke 10:29-37). The correct answer is D.

The Gospel of Luke takes special interest in the universality of the gospel — Luke shows Jesus' concern for all people: Gentiles, women, the poor, and outcasts (Luke 2:32; 4:25-27). The correct answer is C.
Paul was converted on his way to Damascus, where he intended to persecute Christians but was struck down by a light from heaven (Acts 9:3-6). The correct answer is D.
Stephen was the first Christian martyr — he was stoned to death by the Jewish council after his speech (Acts 7:59-60). The correct answer is E.
The father of John the Baptist was Zacharias (Zechariah), a priest of the division of Abijah (Luke 1:5). The correct answer is E.
Simon the sorcerer thought he could obtain the gift of God with money — he offered money to Peter and John to receive the power of laying on hands (Acts 8:18-19). The correct answer is A.

The Acts of the Apostles shows that the power behind the spread of the Gospel is the Holy Spirit — the Spirit directed, empowered, and guided the apostles throughout their mission (Acts 1:8). The correct answer is E.
'There shall be neither dew nor rain these years except by my word' was said by Elijah the Tishbite, announcing a drought as judgment on Israel's idolatry (1 Kings 17:1). The correct answer is C.
The Sanhedrin is a Jewish council of priests, scribes, and elders — it was the supreme religious and judicial council in ancient Israel (Matthew 26:59; Acts 5:27). The correct answer is B.
The first church council on circumcision was held at Jerusalem — the Jerusalem Council debated whether Gentile converts needed to be circumcised (Acts 15:1-2). The correct answer is B.

Before Moses died, God appointed Joshua to succeed him — 'Take Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the Spirit, and lay your hand on him' (Numbers 27:18; Deuteronomy 31:14). The correct answer is A.

In the case before Solomon over the dead and living child, the mother of the dead child supported killing the living child — she said 'It shall be neither mine nor yours; divide it' (1 Kings 3:26). The correct answer is B.

The treatment for those bitten by fiery serpents was to look at the bronze serpent that Moses made and set on a pole — anyone who was bitten and looked at it would live (Numbers 21:8-9). The correct answer is B.
When Joseph's brothers came to him in Egypt, he said to them 'You are spies' — he accused them of coming to see the weakness of the land (Genesis 42:9). The correct answer is A.
Sarah gave birth to Isaac in her old age — God fulfilled His promise to Abraham that Sarah would bear a son (Genesis 21:1-3). The correct answer is B.
God wanted to destroy the world because the earth was filled with violence — 'The earth was corrupt in God's sight, and the earth was filled with violence' (Genesis 6:11-13). The correct answer is E.
Before creation, the earth was without form and void — 'The earth was without form and void, and darkness was over the face of the deep' (Genesis 1:2). The correct answer is A.
As a condition of His covenant with God, Abraham had to circumcise every male — circumcision was the sign of the covenant between God and Abraham (Genesis 17:10-11). The correct answer is A.

Adonijah showed that he feared Solomon by catching hold of the horns of the altar — he clung to the altar as a place of sanctuary, fearing that Solomon would kill him (1 Kings 1:50-51). The correct answer is C.

According to Jeremiah's prophecy, the domination of nations by Nebuchadnezzar was part of the divine purpose — God called Nebuchadnezzar 'my servant' and used him as an instrument of divine judgment (Jeremiah 25:9; 27:6). The correct answer is B.
Solomon got the timber for his building from Lebanon — King Hiram of Tyre supplied cedar and cypress timber from Lebanon for Solomon's temple (1 Kings 5:6-9). The correct answer is D.

Ezekiel was ordered to eat a scroll and then go to speak to the house of Israel — God gave him a scroll to eat, and it tasted sweet as honey; this symbolized receiving God's word fully before proclaiming it (Ezekiel 2:8-3:3). The correct answer is E.

Rebekah was identified as the wife for Isaac because she said 'Drink, and I will water your camels also' — this was the sign Abraham's servant had prayed for as confirmation of God's choice (Genesis 24:14-20). The correct answer is C.
The place where Abraham was asked to sacrifice Isaac was Moriah — 'Go to the land of Moriah, and offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains' (Genesis 22:2). The correct answer is A.
Ezekiel was the prophet regularly addressed as 'son of man' — God repeatedly called him by this title throughout the book of Ezekiel (Ezekiel 2:1; 3:1, etc.). The correct answer is B.

'How is it you were not afraid to put forth your hand to destroy the Lord's anointed?' was said by David to the Amalekite who claimed to have killed Saul — David rebuked and then executed him (2 Samuel 1:14-15). The correct answer is B.

Achan was the one who took some of the devoted things when Jericho fell — he secretly took a beautiful robe, silver, and gold, violating God's command, causing Israel's defeat at Ai (Joshua 7:1, 20-21). The correct answer is D.

The last miracle/plague before the Israelites were released from Egypt was the slaughter of the firstborn — the death of the firstborn in every Egyptian household, including Pharaoh's son, finally compelled Pharaoh to let Israel go (Exodus 12:29-31). The correct answer is E.
Elijah proved on Mount Carmel that Yahweh is greater than Baal — he challenged the 450 prophets of Baal and God answered by fire, consuming the sacrifice (1 Kings 18:20-39). The correct answer is A.

God told Moses to cut two stone tablets like the first ones at the renewal of the Covenant — Moses had broken the first tablets after the golden calf incident, so God commanded new tablets be made for the renewed covenant (Exodus 34:1). The correct answer is A.

Jericho was captured at the blast of the trumpets of the priests — the Israelites marched around the city for seven days and on the seventh day the walls collapsed when the priests blew the trumpets (Joshua 6:16-20). The correct answer is D.
The call of Isaiah took place in the year of the death of King Uzziah — 'In the year that King Uzziah died I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne' (Isaiah 6:1). The correct answer is B.

The main lesson of the parable of the prodigal son is that God forgives those who sincerely repent — the father's joyful reception of the returning son represents God's forgiveness of repentant sinners (Luke 15:20-24). The correct answer is C.

Herod wanted to kill the child Jesus because he learned that Jesus was born king of the Jews — the Magi told Herod they had come to worship the one born king of the Jews, threatening Herod's rule (Matthew 2:2-3). The correct answer is B.

When Zechariah doubted the announcement of the birth of John the Baptist, he was struck dumb — Gabriel said he would be unable to speak until the day these things came true (Luke 1:20). The correct answer is B.

'These men who have turned the world upside down, have come here also, and Jason received them' — this was said about Paul and Silas in Thessalonica, where the Jews accused them before the city authorities (Acts 17:6). The correct answer is D.

'And you, child, will be called the prophet of the Most High' refers to John the Baptist — these are the words Zechariah spoke about his son John in his prophecy (the Benedictus) (Luke 1:76). The correct answer is D.
When the women got to the tomb of Jesus, they found the stone rolled away and Jesus was no longer in the tomb — the angel told them He had risen (Luke 24:2-3; Mark 16:4-6). The correct answer is B.

Paul was first arrested in Jerusalem because he brought Greeks into the temple — Jews from Asia saw him in the temple and accused him of bringing Trophimus the Ephesian into the temple (Acts 21:28-29). The correct answer is A.
'You shall be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria and to the end of the earth' — Jesus spoke these words before His ascension (Acts 1:8). The correct answer is D (Samaria).

Egypt provided Jesus with a refuge when Herod sought to destroy Him — Joseph was warned in a dream to flee to Egypt, fulfilling the prophecy 'Out of Egypt I called my son' (Matthew 2:13-15). The correct answer is B.

Bartimaeus the blind beggar addressed Jesus at Jericho saying 'Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me' — he cried out persistently despite being told to be quiet (Mark 10:47-48). The correct answer is A.

'After me comes he who is mightier than I, the thong of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and untie' was said by John the Baptist, referring to the coming of Jesus (Mark 1:7). The correct answer is D.
The Lord healed the blindness of Paul through Ananias — a disciple in Damascus named Ananias was directed by God to go to Saul and restore his sight (Acts 9:17-18). The correct answer is A.

'The Holy Spirit will come upon you and the power of the Most High will overshadow you, therefore the child to be born will be called holy, the Son of God' was said by the angel Gabriel to Mary (Luke 1:35). The correct answer is C.

Stephen insisted in his speech that God does not dwell in houses made with hands and that it was wrong for Solomon to have built a house for Him — he quoted Isaiah 66:1-2 to support this (Acts 7:47-48). The correct answer is E.

When Paul came to Rome, the first set of people to whom he preached were the Jews — he called together the local leaders of the Jews and explained his situation and preached to them (Acts 28:17-23). The correct answer is B.

'But I say to you that hear, love your enemies, do good to those who hate you' — Jesus said this during the Sermon on the Mount (the Sermon on the Plain in Luke) (Luke 6:27; Matthew 5:44). The correct answer is E.

When complaints were made that some sections of the new Christian community were not being supplied with their needs, the apostles appointed seven deacons to undertake the care of the new Christians (Acts 6:1-6). The correct answer is C.
Jesus came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up, and as His custom was, He went into the synagogue on the Sabbath Day — Jesus was raised in Nazareth (Luke 4:16). The correct answer is C.
Jesus was led into the wilderness by the Holy Spirit — 'Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil' (Matthew 4:1; Luke 4:1). The correct answer is B.

Paul was converted so that he might bear the name of the Lord before the Gentiles — God told Ananias, 'He is a chosen instrument of mine to carry my name before the Gentiles and kings and the children of Israel' (Acts 9:15). The correct answer is D.

Pilate gave Jesus to the Jews to be crucified because the Jews brought pressure upon him — though Pilate found no fault in Jesus, the crowd's pressure and threat to report him to Caesar led him to capitulate (John 19:12-16). The correct answer is E.

'In the resurrection, whose wife shall she be of the seven, for they all had her?' was put to Jesus by the Sadducees, who used this scenario to challenge belief in resurrection (Matthew 22:23-28; Mark 12:18-23). The correct answer is D.
'Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples born of you shall be divided' was addressed by God to Rebekah while she was pregnant with Jacob and Esau (Genesis 25:23). The correct answer is C.
After the flood, God allowed all food to be eaten except flesh with its blood in it — 'But you shall not eat flesh with its life, that is, its blood' (Genesis 9:4). The correct answer is B.

Paul and Silas were imprisoned at Philippi — after Paul cast out the spirit of divination from a slave girl, her owners had Paul and Silas arrested and thrown into prison (Acts 16:19-24). The correct answer is B.
The three sons of Noah were Shem, Ham, and Japheth (Genesis 5:32; 6:10). The correct answer is D.
The statement 'I the LORD your God am a jealous God' was made when God gave the Ten Commandments to Moses on Mount Sinai — it is part of the second commandment (Exodus 20:5). The correct answer is A.
The wife of Moses was Zipporah, daughter of Jethro (Reuel), a Midianite priest (Exodus 2:21). The correct answer is B.
The cure for the snake bites was a look at the bronze serpent — Moses made a bronze serpent and put it on a pole; anyone bitten who looked at it would live (Numbers 21:8-9). The correct answer is E.

Joshua was appointed to lead the Israelites to the Promised Land because of Moses' rebellion in the wilderness of Zin — Moses struck the rock instead of speaking to it at Meribah/Kadesh, and God told him he would not enter the Promised Land (Numbers 20:12; 27:12-14). The correct answer is C.

The Israelites were instructed to eat the Passover with loins girded, shoes on feet, staff in hand — 'you shall eat it in haste' (Exodus 12:11). They were NOT to eat it raw (they were to roast it with fire), and not to leave remnants till morning (burn them). So the incorrect instruction is eating it raw or leaving remnants — 'you shall not eat any of it raw' (Exodus 12:9). The correct answer is E (leaving remnants the following morning is incorrect — they should burn it, but technically 'remnants the following morning' means they should burn them, not leave them, so this instruction 'leave remnants' would be wrong).
Each of the twelve spies sent by Moses to report on the Promised Land was a leader in his own tribe — 'every one a leader among them' (Numbers 13:2). The correct answer is E.
The Judges were those inspired by God to lead the tribes of Israel in battle — God raised up judges who delivered Israel from their oppressors (Judges 2:16). The correct answer is A.

The covenant was renewed on Mount Sinai because Aaron had made the golden calf — Moses broke the first tablets when he saw the golden calf; God renewed the covenant with new tablets (Exodus 34:1-4). The correct answer is D.
The sun stood still when Joshua defeated the Amorites at Gibeon — Joshua prayed and the sun stood still so the Israelites could complete their victory (Joshua 10:12-13). The correct answer is D.

'I repent that I made Saul king' refers to when Saul disobeyed God over Amalek — Saul spared King Agag and the best livestock despite God's command to destroy everything, and Samuel declared that God repented of making Saul king (1 Samuel 15:11). The correct answer is E.

God revealed to Samuel that He was going to punish Eli because he did not correct his sons' sinful behaviour — Eli knew his sons were sinning grievously but only gave them mild rebukes without restraining them (1 Samuel 2:29; 3:13). The correct answer is A.
Hannah prayed to God at Shiloh for a son because Peninnah provoked her sorely — Peninnah taunted Hannah year after year because Hannah was barren (1 Samuel 1:6-10). The correct answer is B.
David's first reaction after being rebuked by God through Nathan was to beg for forgiveness — he said to Nathan 'I have sinned against the LORD' (2 Samuel 12:13). The correct answer is A.

'If he (Baal) is a god, let him contend for himself because his altar has been pulled down' — Gideon's father Joash said this after Gideon pulled down the altar of Baal (Judges 6:31). The correct answer is C (Gideon pulled down the altar).

God pronounced utter destruction on the Amalekites because they opposed Israel on their way from Egypt to the Promised Land — 'I will punish what Amalek did to Israel in opposing them on the way' (1 Samuel 15:2; Exodus 17:8-16). The correct answer is D.

David charged Solomon to keep God's statutes so that Solomon might prosper and the Davidic dynasty be preserved forever — 'that you may prosper in all that you do and wherever you turn' (1 Kings 2:3). The correct answer is A.
In the trade treaty, Solomon was to supply wheat and oil while Hiram was to supply timber — cedar and cypress timber from Lebanon (1 Kings 5:10-11). The correct answer is D.

'Your father made our yoke heavy. Now therefore lighten the hard service of your father and his heavy yoke upon us and we will serve you' was addressed to Rehoboam, Solomon's son, by the assembly of Israel requesting relief from the heavy burdens (1 Kings 12:4). The correct answer is D.
'I have been very jealous for the LORD...I even I only, am left, and they seek my life to take it away' was said by Elijah at a cave in Mount Horeb (1 Kings 19:10, 14). The correct answer is E.

Jeremiah proclaimed a new covenant of God with Israel and Judah — 'Behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah' (Jeremiah 31:31). The correct answer is B.

The synoptic gospels refer to the first three books of the New Testament — Matthew, Mark, and Luke are called synoptic because they share a common perspective and much of the same material. The correct answer is C.
Isaiah gave the cry 'Woe is me! for I am lost, for I am a man of unclean lips' — he said this when he saw the Lord of hosts in his vision in the temple (Isaiah 6:5). The correct answer is C.

'You brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?' was said by John the son of Zechariah (John the Baptist), spoken to the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism (Matthew 3:7; Luke 3:7). The correct answer is A.

'You shall not tempt the Lord your God' was said by Jesus to the devil in the wilderness during His temptations — Jesus quoted Deuteronomy 6:16 in response to Satan's challenge (Matthew 4:7; Luke 4:12). The correct answer is D.

'He will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children' — the angel Gabriel spoke this about John the Baptist in his announcement to Zechariah (Luke 1:17). The correct answer is B.

In the parable of the sower, the seeds on good ground represent those who accept and live by God's word — they hear the word, hold it fast in an honest and good heart, and bear fruit with patience (Luke 8:15). The correct answer is A.

The people of Nazareth found it difficult to believe what Jesus preached because they knew Him from childhood — 'Is not this the carpenter's son? Is not his mother called Mary?' They were offended at Him (Matthew 13:55-57; Mark 6:3). The correct answer is C.

'An evil and adulterous generation seeks for a sign, but no sign shall be given to it except the sign of Jonah' — Jesus said this to the Pharisees and Sadducees who came to test Him by asking for a sign (Matthew 16:1-4). The correct answer is E.

Hosanna means 'save now' — it is derived from the Hebrew 'Hoshia-na' meaning 'save us now' or 'grant salvation.' The crowd cried 'Hosanna' at Jesus' triumphal entry (Matthew 21:9). The correct answer is E.

'Follow me and I will make you fishers of men' was addressed to Simon Peter and Andrew — Jesus called them both as they were casting a net into the sea (Matthew 4:18-19; Mark 1:16-17). The correct answer is E.
Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome went to the tomb on the third day to anoint the body of Jesus (Mark 16:1). The correct answer is B.
Jesus denounced the Scribes and Pharisees because they did not practise what they preached — 'they preach but do not practice' (Matthew 23:3). The correct answer is B.
Simon the Canaanean was one of the twelve apostles (Matthew 10:4; Mark 3:18). The correct answer is B.
To some who trusted in themselves that they were righteous and despised others, Jesus told the parable of the Pharisee and the tax collector (Luke 18:9-14). The correct answer is B.

Peter and John were arrested because they proclaimed in Jesus the resurrection from the dead — the Sadducees were greatly annoyed because they were teaching the people and proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection (Acts 4:1-3). The correct answer is B.

'Let his habitation become desolate, and let there be no one to live in it' and 'His office let another take' refers to Judas Iscariot — Peter quoted these psalms to explain the need to replace Judas (Acts 1:20). The correct answer is A.
The conversion of Paul was made possible by the risen Jesus — Jesus appeared to Saul on the road to Damascus in a blinding light and spoke to him directly (Acts 9:3-6). The correct answer is D.
The proconsul when Paul arrived in Corinth was called Gallio — when the Jews brought Paul before the judgment seat, Gallio was proconsul of Achaia (Acts 18:12). The correct answer is C.
'Now I know that the Lord has sent his angel to deliver me out of the hand of Herod' — Peter said this after the angel released him from prison (Acts 12:11). The correct answer is D.
King Agrippa said 'In a short time you think to make me a Christian' in the course of Paul's defence before him (Acts 26:28). The correct answer is B.

The seven deacons were appointed to help in the distribution of food — the apostles appointed them specifically to serve tables and ensure fair distribution to widows (Acts 6:1-6). The correct answer is D.
When Paul arrived in Rome, he first addressed the local leaders of the Jews — he called together the leaders of the Jews and began explaining his case (Acts 28:17). The correct answer is A.

'For I am ready not only to be imprisoned but even to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus' was said by Paul when his companions urged him not to go to Jerusalem (Acts 21:13). The correct answer is D.

Paul's vision completed: 'Do not be afraid, Paul...God has granted you all those who sail with you' — the angel assured Paul that all on board would be saved, even though the ship would be lost (Acts 27:24). The correct answer is E.
'Walk before me, and be blameless' was addressed to Abraham — he was 99 years old when this voice came (Genesis 17:1). The correct answer is C.
According to Genesis 1, on the 6th day God created man and living creatures — land animals and humans were created on the sixth day (Genesis 1:24-31). The correct answer is D.
The flood lasted a hundred and fifty days while Noah was in the ark — 'the waters prevailed on the earth 150 days' (Genesis 7:24). The correct answer is E.
The father of Moses was of the tribe of Levi — Amram, the father of Moses, was from the house of Levi (Exodus 2:1). The correct answer is A.

'You would bring down my grey hairs with sorrow to Sheol' — Jacob said this because he feared that Benjamin would be lost to him like Joseph, as the brothers were demanding Benjamin go to Egypt (Genesis 42:38; 44:29). The correct answer is E.

'This is the finger of God' was said by the magicians to Pharaoh after the plague of gnats — the magicians could not replicate the third plague (gnats) and declared it was the finger of God (Exodus 8:18-19). The correct answer is E.

'Hear now, you rebels, shall we bring forth water for you out of this rock?' was spoken by Moses in the wilderness of Zin at Kadesh — this was when Moses struck the rock instead of speaking to it (Numbers 20:8-11). The correct answer is C.

The Israelites said 'All that the LORD has spoken we will do' at Mount Sinai — they made this covenant commitment when Moses came and told them all the words of the LORD (Exodus 19:8; 24:3). The correct answer is B.
Sisera was put to death by Jael — she drove a tent peg through his temple while he slept, after he fled from the battle and took refuge in her tent (Judges 4:21). The correct answer is D.
Joshua's first victory was at Jericho — the walls of Jericho fell after the Israelites marched around it and the priests blew the trumpets (Joshua 6:1-20). The correct answer is E.
Joshua was chosen to lead the Israelites after Moses' death — God commanded Moses to commission Joshua as his successor (Numbers 27:18-23; Joshua 1:1-2). The correct answer is D.

Samuel's sons were rejected as judges because they perverted justice and took bribes — Joel and Abijah 'turned aside after gain; they took bribes and perverted justice' (1 Samuel 8:3). The correct answer is C.
The name 'Samuel' means 'I have asked him of the LORD' — Hannah gave him this name saying 'I have asked him from the LORD' (1 Samuel 1:20). The correct answer is C.
'But I will be with you and you will smite the Midianites as one man' was said by God to Gideon when He called him to deliver Israel from Midian (Judges 6:16). The correct answer is D.
The commander of David's army was Joab — Joab son of Zeruiah served as David's chief military commander throughout his reign (2 Samuel 8:16). The correct answer is B.

God took the kingdom from Saul because he disobeyed the LORD by offering burnt sacrifices himself — Saul offered sacrifice before Samuel arrived at Gilgal, usurping the priestly role (1 Samuel 13:9-14). The correct answer is C.
The city of Samaria was built by Omri, king of Israel — he bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer and built on it, naming the city after Shemer (1 Kings 16:24). The correct answer is A.
King David committed adultery with Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah the Hittite (2 Samuel 11:2-4). The correct answer is B.
The prophet Ahijah encouraged Jeroboam I to revolt at the initial stage — Ahijah of Shiloh told Jeroboam he would reign over ten tribes of Israel (1 Kings 11:29-37). The correct answer is D.

The complaint that was NOT made was 'The strength of the burden-bearers is failing' — the actual complaints were about food, mortgaging fields, paying the king's tax, and children being sold into slavery (Nehemiah 5:1-5). The correct answer is D (this is the one NOT listed as a complaint).
The king who reigned after Hezekiah was Manasseh, his son — Manasseh was Hezekiah's son and succeeded him, reigning for 55 years (2 Kings 21:1). The correct answer is E.
The prophet from Tekoa was Amos — 'The words of Amos, who was among the shepherds of Tekoa' (Amos 1:1). The correct answer is E.
'You brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?' was part of the preaching of John the Baptist (Matthew 3:7; Luke 3:7). The correct answer is D.

Jesus was said to be 'of Nazareth' because He was brought up in the city of Nazareth — though He was born in Bethlehem, He grew up in Nazareth, and it became His hometown (Luke 2:39-40; 4:16). The correct answer is D.

Luke gave the most detailed account of Christ's infancy because he was writing an orderly account of events — 'it seemed good to me also...to write an orderly account' (Luke 1:3). The correct answer is C.

'I am not worthy to have you come under my roof' was said by the centurion at Capernaum — a Roman centurion asked Jesus to heal his servant but said he was unworthy for Jesus to enter his house (Matthew 8:8; Luke 7:6). The correct answer is C.

The correct statement is that the order in which Jesus was tempted varies in Matthew and Luke, but the tests remain the same — Matthew and Luke record the three temptations in different sequences, but the actual temptations are identical (Matthew 4:1-11; Luke 4:1-13). The correct answer is A.

Luke was NOT one of the Twelve apostles — Luke was a physician and companion of Paul who wrote the Gospel of Luke and Acts, but was not among the twelve disciples (Colossians 4:14). The correct answer is D.

The renowned interpreters of the Mosaic Law in the time of Jesus were the Pharisees — they were known as the strict interpreters and teachers of the law, devoted to Torah observance (Matthew 23:2-3). The correct answer is E.

'The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field' teaches about the preciousness of the kingdom — just as a man joyfully sells everything to buy the field containing the treasure, the kingdom of heaven is of supreme value worth any sacrifice (Matthew 13:44). The correct answer is E.

When Herod the Tetrarch heard of the fame of Jesus, he thought that Jesus was John the Baptist raised from the dead — 'This is John the Baptist. He has been raised from the dead' (Matthew 14:2; Mark 6:16). The correct answer is C.
'Grant us to sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your glory' was petitioned by James and John, the sons of Zebedee (Mark 10:35-37). The correct answer is D.

In the parable of the weeds, the owner of the field who sowed good seed is the Son of Man — Jesus explained 'The one who sows the good seed is the Son of Man' (Matthew 13:37). The correct answer is B.

'I find no crime in this man' was said by Pilate — he declared Jesus innocent three times during the trial but eventually handed Him over to be crucified under pressure (Luke 23:4; John 19:6). The correct answer is E.

In the parable of the ten maidens, the five were called foolish because they did not take additional oil with them — when the bridegroom was delayed, their lamps went out because they had no extra oil (Matthew 25:3-8). The correct answer is E.

'Today salvation has come to this house, for this man also is a son of Abraham' was said by Jesus of Zacchaeus the tax collector, after he repented and promised to restore what he had wrongly taken (Luke 19:9). The correct answer is C.
Theophilus was the one to whom the Acts of the Apostles was written — Luke dedicated both his Gospel and Acts to 'most excellent Theophilus' (Luke 1:3; Acts 1:1). The correct answer is B.

Apollos was an eloquent Jew from Alexandria, well versed in the scriptures — 'Now a Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, came to Ephesus. He was an eloquent man, competent in the Scriptures' (Acts 18:24). The correct answer is D.

On the road to Gaza, Philip converted and baptized a minister of the Candace (the queen of Ethiopia) — the Ethiopian eunuch who was an official in charge of the treasury (Acts 8:27). The correct answer is A.

An altar was set up to the unknown God in the Greek town of Athens — Paul found this altar in Athens and used it as a starting point for his sermon to the Athenians (Acts 17:23). The correct answer is A.

The Ecumenical Council of 49 A.D. held in Jerusalem was mainly to discuss the fate of Gentile Christians — specifically, whether Gentiles needed to be circumcised and follow the law of Moses (Acts 15:1-2). The correct answer is D.

When God called Abram out of Haran, his first place of call in Canaan was Shechem — 'Abram passed through the land to the place at Shechem, to the oak of Moreh' (Genesis 12:6). The correct answer is C.

The people of Malta thought Paul must be a murderer because he was bitten by a poisonous snake — they expected him to swell up or drop dead, thinking justice had caught up with a criminal (Acts 28:3-4). The correct answer is A.

'This at last is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called woman, because she was taken out of man' — Adam said this when God brought Eve to him (Genesis 2:23). The correct answer is D.

The Passover was to remind the Israelites of God's smiting of all the firstborn in Egypt — the blood of the lamb on the doorposts caused the destroyer to pass over the Israelite houses while striking the firstborn of Egypt (Exodus 12:12-14). The correct answer is B.
The Egyptians enslaved the Israelites and forced them to build store-cities — specifically Pithom and Raamses (Exodus 1:11). The correct answer is A.

'This is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven' was said by Jacob at Bethel — after his dream of the ladder reaching heaven, Jacob called the place Bethel (house of God) (Genesis 28:17). The correct answer is B.

The statement 'it is not the sound of shouting for victory or the sound of the cry of defeat, but the sound of singing that I hear' reflects the apostasy of Aaron and the people — Moses heard this singing as he came down from the mountain and found the Israelites dancing around the golden calf (Exodus 32:17-18). The correct answer is D.

The consecration of the people of Israel took place at the foot of Mount Sinai — the people washed their garments and consecrated themselves before God spoke the Ten Commandments (Exodus 19:10-11). The correct answer is C.

Joshua gave this advice: 'Fear the Lord and serve him in sincerity and faithfulness; put away the gods...and serve the Lord' — this was part of Joshua's farewell address to Israel at Shechem (Joshua 24:14). The correct answer is B.

Jotham asked this question: 'Which is better for you, that all seventy of the sons of Jerubbaal rule over you, or that one rule over you?' — Jotham spoke this parable to the people of Shechem after Abimelech killed his brothers (Judges 9:2). The correct answer is A (Abimelech is the subject, but Jotham asked the question).

'Rule over us, you and your son and your grandson also, for you have delivered us out of the hand of Midian' was addressed to Gideon — the Israelites asked him to be their king (Judges 8:22). The correct answer is C.
Uzzah was the man who touched the Ark and died — he put out his hand to steady the ark when the oxen stumbled, and God struck him dead (2 Samuel 6:6-7). The correct answer is C.

At childhood, the word of the Lord came to Samuel because he was to announce the punishment for the house of Eli — God chose Samuel to reveal His judgment against Eli's family (1 Samuel 3:11-14). The correct answer is C.

'Cursed be the man who takes food before evening, before I am able to avenge myself on my enemies' was said by Saul during the battle between Israel and the Philistines (1 Samuel 14:24). The correct answer is D.

The Israelites on forced labour in Lebanon were allowed two months at home for every month at the labour camp — 'a month in Lebanon and two months at home' (1 Kings 5:14). The correct answer is A (Two months at home for every one month away).

It was wrong for Solomon to have married foreign women because they would entice him to worship idols — exactly what happened: his foreign wives turned his heart after other gods (1 Kings 11:2-4). The correct answer is A.

'Behold your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt!' was said by Jeroboam — he set up two golden calves at Bethel and Dan to prevent Israel from going to Jerusalem to worship (1 Kings 12:28). The correct answer is C.

Pekahiah did not assassinate his predecessor but was assassinated by his successor Pekah — Pekahiah was the son of Menahem (who assassinated Shallum), and Pekahiah was later assassinated by Pekah (2 Kings 15:22-25). The correct answer is D.

The statement that is UNTRUE is that the widow and her son ate the food and waited for their death — the widow had been going to prepare the last meal when Elijah arrived; after she fed Elijah first, the meal was miraculously sustained (1 Kings 17:12-16). The correct answer is C.

'He burned his son as an offering, and practised soothsaying and augury, and dealt with mediums and with wizards' refers to Manasseh — the most wicked king of Judah, he also built altars to Baal and worshipped the host of heaven (2 Kings 21:2-6). The correct answer is B.
Hosea said Israel shall dwell many days without king or prince, without sacrifice or pillar, without ephod or teraphim (Hosea 3:4). The correct answer is A.

Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim king of Judah and changed his name to Jehoiakim — after killing Josiah at Megiddo, Neco deposed Jehoahaz and placed Eliakim/Jehoiakim on the throne (2 Kings 23:34). The correct answer is B.
'Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and his name shall be called Emmanuel' — Emmanuel means 'God with us' (Isaiah 7:14; Matthew 1:23). The correct answer is B.

Isaiah made the prophecy: 'The ransomed of the Lord shall return, and come to Zion with singing; everlasting joy shall be upon their heads' — this is from Isaiah 35:10 and 51:11, a prophecy of Zion's happy future. The correct answer is B.

Jeremiah wrote to the exiles in Babylon and encouraged them to seek the welfare of Babylon — 'seek the welfare of the city where I have sent you into exile, and pray to the LORD on its behalf' (Jeremiah 29:7). The correct answer is C.
When Christ called Levi to follow Him, Levi left everything and followed Him — 'And leaving everything, he rose and followed him' (Luke 5:28). The correct answer is D.

John the Baptist's specific reply to the soldiers during his preaching was 'Be content with your wages' — he told them not to extort or falsely accuse anyone, and to be satisfied with their pay (Luke 3:14). The correct answer is D.

The parable of the unmerciful servant teaches that we should forgive our debtors from our hearts — the king forgave the servant's enormous debt, but the servant refused to forgive a small debt; Jesus taught that God expects us to forgive as we have been forgiven (Matthew 18:35). The correct answer is B.

The ways in which various people hear the word of God are described in the parable of the sower — the different types of soil represent different ways people receive and respond to God's word (Matthew 13:3-23; Mark 4:3-20). The correct answer is A.
The miracle which touched on ingratitude is the cure of the ten lepers — Jesus healed ten lepers but only one, a Samaritan, returned to give thanks (Luke 17:12-19). The correct answer is C.

Jesus taught that fasting in addition to prayers is necessary in some situations during the healing of the epileptic boy — the disciples could not cast out the demon, and Jesus said 'This kind cannot be driven out by anything but prayer and fasting' (Mark 9:29). The correct answer is D.

'But if it is by the Spirit of God that I cast out demons, then the kingdom of God has come upon you' — Jesus said this in response to the accusation that He cast out demons by Beelzebub (Matthew 12:28). The correct answer is C.

Jesus did not grant the request of the sons of Zebedee because it was not His to grant — 'to sit at my right hand or at my left is not mine to grant, but it is for those for whom it has been prepared by my Father' (Matthew 20:23). The correct answer is C.

To give the widow's mite is to give everything possible — the widow gave two small coins which was all she had, giving out of her poverty, unlike others who gave out of their abundance (Mark 12:44; Luke 21:4). The correct answer is C.

The parable which teaches persistence in prayer is that of the Unjust Judge — a widow kept coming to an unjust judge until he gave her justice; Jesus used this to teach that God will answer persistent prayer (Luke 18:1-8). The correct answer is A.

Elizabeth was absent during the crucifixion of Jesus Christ — the Gospels mention Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of Jesus, Salome, and other women at the crucifixion, but Elizabeth is not mentioned (John 19:25; Mark 15:40). The correct answer is B.

'While it remained unsold, did it not remain your own? And after it was sold, was it not at your disposal? How is it that you have contrived this deed in your heart? You have not lied to men but to God' — Peter addressed this to Ananias about the deceit regarding the land sale (Acts 5:4). The correct answer is B (Ananias).

To explain the outpouring of the Holy Spirit on Pentecost, Peter quoted Prophet Joel — 'This is what was uttered through the prophet Joel: In the last days...I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh' (Acts 2:16-17; Joel 2:28). The correct answer is C.
The proconsul of Paphos during the visit of Paul and Barnabas was Sergius Paulus — he was an intelligent man who sought to hear the word of God (Acts 13:7). The correct answer is C.
After killing James, Herod arrested Peter because the Jews were pleased with the murder of James — 'he proceeded to arrest Peter also' seeing it pleased the Jews (Acts 12:3). The correct answer is B.

'Truly I perceive that God shows no partiality' was said by Peter — he said this after God led him to Cornelius, realizing the gospel was for all people regardless of nationality (Acts 10:34). The correct answer is B.
Paul used the teaching of the poets to introduce God the Creator at Athens — 'For we are indeed his offspring' (quoting Aratus) at the Areopagus in Athens (Acts 17:28). The correct answer is B.

Lydia received Paul and Silas into her house when they came to Philippi — she was a seller of purple goods who was converted and urged them to stay at her house (Acts 16:14-15). The correct answer is A.
Judas and Silas, leading men among the brethren and prophets, were sent to Antioch with a letter in company with Paul and Barnabas (Acts 15:22-27). The correct answer is D.

The final port of departure for Italy where the centurion put Paul on board was Myra — the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italy at Myra in Lycia (Acts 27:5-6). The correct answer is A.
'In a short time you think to make me a Christian' was said by King Agrippa to Paul during Paul's defence (Acts 26:28). The correct answer is D.
On his final journey to Jerusalem, Paul lodged at the house of Mnason, an old disciple from Cyprus (Acts 21:16). The correct answer is C.

'Thorns and thistles it shall bring forth to you, and you shall eat the plants of the field. In the sweat of your face you shall eat bread' — these words were spoken to Adam as part of the curse after his disobedience (Genesis 3:17-19). The correct answer is C.

'Cast out this slave woman with her son, for the son of this slave woman shall not be heir with my son Isaac' — the slave woman was Hagar, Sarah's Egyptian servant (Genesis 21:10). The correct answer is C.

'Our sister, be the mother of thousands and ten thousands; and may your descendants possess the gate of those who hate them' — this blessing was spoken to Rebekah as she left to marry Isaac (Genesis 24:60). The correct answer is B.

Joshua was buried in the hill-country of Ephraim, at Timnath-serah — 'They buried him in the territory of his inheritance at Timnath-serah, in the hill country of Ephraim' (Joshua 24:30). The correct answer is D.
Abraham circumcised his son Isaac on the eighth day because God commanded him to do so — circumcision on the eighth day was the sign of the covenant (Genesis 17:12; 21:4). The correct answer is B.
Joseph bound Simeon when his brothers came to Egypt to buy grain — he kept Simeon as a hostage while sending the others back for Benjamin (Genesis 42:24). The correct answer is A.
'Take handfuls of ashes from the kiln and let Moses throw them toward heaven' — the resultant plague was boils and sores on man and beast throughout Egypt (Exodus 9:8-10). The correct answer is C.

'Take off the rings of gold which are in the ears of your wives, your sons and your daughters and bring them to me' — Aaron collected the gold rings and fashioned a molten calf with them (Exodus 32:2-4). The correct answer is D.

On the sixth day the leftover bread did not become foul because God commanded them to keep it — God told Moses on the sixth day they should gather double, and the portion kept over the Sabbath did not spoil because God commanded it (Exodus 16:23-24). The correct answer is B.

Moses was regarded as the greatest prophet in the Old Testament for seeing God face to face — 'And there has not arisen a prophet since in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face' (Deuteronomy 34:10). The correct answer is D.

God commanded that Aaron should speak for Moses, but Moses should be to Aaron as God — 'He shall be your spokesman to the people, and you shall be as God to him' (Exodus 4:16). The correct answer is A.

Achan, who took some of the devoted things at Jericho, was from the tribe of Judah — 'Achan the son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah' (Joshua 7:1, 18). The correct answer is B.

'Whoever rebels against your commandment and disobeys your words...shall be put to death; only be strong and of good courage' was addressed to Joshua — Rahab said this and the Israelites told Joshua this at his commissioning (Joshua 1:18). The correct answer is B.

'Alas, my daughter! You have brought me very low...for I have opened my mouth to the LORD and I cannot take back my vow' — Jephthah made the vow to sacrifice whatever came out of his house first if God gave him victory, and his daughter came out to meet him (Judges 11:35). The correct answer is D.

Jael was connected with the war between Israel and King Jabin of Canaan — she killed Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, by driving a tent peg through his head (Judges 4:21). The correct answer is B.

'Then the spirit of the LORD will come mightily upon you, and you shall prophesy with them' was addressed to Saul — Samuel told him this sign would confirm his anointing as king (1 Samuel 10:6). The correct answer is B.

Uriah did not wish to go down to his house because the Ark was in the battlefield — 'The ark and Israel and Judah dwell in booths; shall I then go to my house to eat and to drink?' (2 Samuel 11:11). The correct answer is C.

The evil spirit that tormented Saul left him whenever he heard David's music — David would play the lyre and Saul would be refreshed, and the evil spirit would depart (1 Samuel 16:23). The correct answer is D.

The greatest of David's domestic problems that broke his heart was the murder of Absalom by Joab — David wept bitterly for Absalom: 'O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! Would I had died instead of you' (2 Samuel 18:33). The correct answer is D.

Saul was made king publicly before the LORD and before all the people of Israel at Mizpah — Samuel gathered all Israel at Mizpah and Saul was chosen by lot and proclaimed king (1 Samuel 10:17-24). The correct answer is B.
When the Queen of Sheba heard of Solomon's fame, she came to test him with her questions — 'she came to test him with hard questions' (1 Kings 10:1). The correct answer is A.

When Joseph discovered that Mary was with child, he decided to divorce her quietly because he was a just man — 'Joseph, being a just man and unwilling to put her to shame, resolved to divorce her quietly' (Matthew 1:19). The correct answer is D.

Though Herod wanted to put John the Baptist to death, he feared the people because they held John to be a prophet — the people regarded John as a true prophet from God (Matthew 14:5). The correct answer is C.

Besides wisdom, God promised Solomon long life, but with the condition of walking in His ways — 'And if you walk in my ways, keeping my statutes and my commandments, as your father David walked, then I will lengthen your days' (1 Kings 3:14). The correct answer is C.

The instruction to 'judge the people' is NOT included in the mission instructions given to the disciples — they were told to heal the sick, cleanse lepers, raise the dead, and cast out demons, but not to judge (Matthew 10:8). The correct answer is B.

When Peter confessed Jesus as the Christ, Jesus replied that it had been revealed to Peter by 'my Father' — 'Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah! For flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven' (Matthew 16:17). The correct answer is A.

Jesus asked His disciples not to disclose their vision of the transfiguration until after the resurrection — 'Tell no one the vision, until the Son of Man is raised from the dead' (Matthew 17:9). The correct answer is B.

According to Jesus, every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste — 'Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and no city or house divided against itself will stand' (Matthew 12:25). The correct answer is A.
Daniel prophesied the signs of the end — the book of Daniel contains extensive apocalyptic prophecies about end-time events (Daniel 12:1-4). The correct answer is B.

The Pharisees and Scribes accused the disciples of transgressing the tradition of the elders because they ate with unwashed hands — they did not follow the ritual hand-washing tradition (Matthew 15:1-2; Mark 7:2-5). The correct answer is C.

'Why this waste? For this ointment might have been sold for a large sum and given to the poor' — this event took place in Bethany, at the house of Simon the leper, where a woman anointed Jesus with expensive ointment (Matthew 26:6-9). The correct answer is D.

'You are wrong, because you know neither the scriptures nor the power of God. For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven' — Jesus gave this answer to the Sadducees who tried to disprove resurrection with a question about a woman with seven husbands (Matthew 22:29-30). The correct answer is A.

At His triumphal entry into Jerusalem, Christ sat on an ass because He wanted to fulfill the scriptures — Zechariah 9:9 prophesied 'your king is coming to you, humble, and mounted on a donkey' (Matthew 21:4-5). The correct answer is C.

'Let both grow together until the harvest, and at harvest time...Gather the weeds first...but gather the wheat into my barn' — this is from the parable of the tares (weeds), explaining that the righteous and wicked will be separated at the end (Matthew 13:30). The correct answer is C.
On their return to Jerusalem after the Ascension, the apostles devoted themselves to prayer — 'All these with one accord were devoting themselves to prayer' (Acts 1:14). The correct answer is D.
The promise of the Father — 'wait for the promise of the Father' — was fulfilled when the Holy Spirit filled the disciples on the day of Pentecost (Acts 2:1-4). The correct answer is B.
'Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be satisfied' (Matthew 5:6). The correct answer is B.

Gamaliel advised the Sanhedrin to keep away from the apostles and let them alone — 'if this plan or this undertaking is of man, it will fail; but if it is of God, you will not be able to overthrow them' (Acts 5:38-39). The correct answer is C.

Peter explained the disciples were filled with the Holy Spirit according to the prophecy of Joel — 'This is what was uttered through the prophet Joel: In the last days...I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh' (Acts 2:16-17). The correct answer is A.

Agabus prophesied a great famine over all the world at Antioch — 'one of them named Agabus stood up and foretold by the Spirit that there would be a great famine over all the world' (Acts 11:28). The correct answer is A.

Saul travelled to Damascus to arrest those belonging to the Way — he obtained letters from the High Priest to bring any Christians he found in Damascus to Jerusalem as prisoners (Acts 9:1-2). The correct answer is D.
Peter was criticized by the circumcision party because he ate with the Gentiles — they said 'You went to uncircumcised men and ate with them' (Acts 11:3). The correct answer is C.

'Then they cast him out of the city and stoned him, and the witnesses laid down their garments at the feet of a young man' — Stephen was the one cast out and stoned; the young man at whose feet the garments were laid was Saul (Acts 7:58). The correct answer is D.
While Peter was still speaking, the Holy Spirit fell on all who heard the word at Caesarea — this happened at the house of Cornelius in Caesarea (Acts 10:44). The correct answer is B.

'Two nations' in Rebekah's womb refers to the Edomites and Israelites — Esau became the father of the Edomites and Jacob became Israel; they were the two nations (Genesis 25:23). The correct answer is C.

Joseph's rough treatment of his brothers was to prove their sincere contrition — he tested them to see if they had truly changed and repented of what they had done to him (Genesis 42:7; 44:1-12). The correct answer is D.
'I have sinned this time; the LORD is in the right, and I and my people are in the wrong' — Pharaoh said this after the plague of the hailstorm (Exodus 9:27). The correct answer is A.

'Mahanaim' is so called because Jacob saw the angels of God as God's army — when Jacob saw the angels, he named the place Mahanaim meaning 'two camps' or 'God's army' (Genesis 32:2). The correct answer is D.

The request of Moses that Israel should be allowed to go and worship God was interpreted by Pharaoh to mean idleness — Pharaoh said 'You are idle, you are idle; that is why you say, Let us go and sacrifice to the LORD' (Exodus 5:17). The correct answer is B.

The sin that led to punishment by fiery serpents was speaking against God and Moses — 'the people spoke against God and against Moses, Why have you brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness?' (Numbers 21:5). The correct answer is B.
Pharaoh's horsemen overtook the fleeing Hebrews at Pihahiroth — they found them encamped by the sea at Pihahiroth, before Baal-zephon (Exodus 14:9). The correct answer is D.

The passover lamb was to be killed in the evening on the fourteenth day of the first month — 'the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall kill their lambs at twilight/evening' (Exodus 12:6). The correct answer is C.
Joshua put the king of Ai to death by hanging — 'he hanged the king of Ai on a tree until evening' (Joshua 8:29). The correct answer is C.

During the confirmation of the covenant, Moses was invited by the Lord along with Aaron, Nadab and Abihu — 'Come up to the LORD, you and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel' (Exodus 24:1). The correct answer is A.

'Go into the hills, lest the pursuers meet you and hide yourselves there three days' was the advice given by Rahab — she told the two spies she had hidden to hide in the hills until the pursuers returned (Joshua 2:16). The correct answer is C.

Joshua preserved the twelve stones in Gilgal to remind Israel of the crossing of the River Jordan — 'When your children ask their fathers in time to come, What do these stones mean? then you shall let your children know, Israel passed over this Jordan on dry ground' (Joshua 4:21-22). The correct answer is C.

In Jotham's parable of the trees, Abimelech is likened to the bramble — the bramble (thornbush) accepted kingship when the noble trees (olive, fig, vine) refused; just as Abimelech, an unworthy man, became king (Judges 9:14-15). The correct answer is B.

Samson, as a Nazirite, was required to avoid alcohol, unclean things and shaving — the angel told Manoah's wife that the child must avoid wine, strong drink, unclean food, and no razor should touch his head (Judges 13:4-5). The correct answer is B.

'I have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and I have utterly destroyed the Amalekites' was declared by Saul — he disobeyed God by sparing Agag and the best livestock (1 Samuel 15:20). The correct answer is D.
The city captured by Joshua before the disaster at Ai was Jericho — Jericho fell first, then the Israelites suffered defeat at Ai due to Achan's sin (Joshua 6-7). The correct answer is B.

'Saul fell at once full length upon the ground, filled with fear because of the words of Samuel' — this happened when Samuel was invoked from the dead by the medium of Endor and appeared to pronounce doom on Saul (1 Samuel 28:20). The correct answer is B.

Eli fell down and died because of the capture of the Ark of the Covenant — when a messenger brought news that Israel was defeated and the Ark of God captured, Eli fell backward off his seat, broke his neck, and died (1 Samuel 4:17-18). The correct answer is C.

God promised to give the kingdom after Solomon's death to Jeroboam — the prophet Ahijah told Jeroboam he would rule over ten tribes when Solomon's son proved unworthy (1 Kings 11:31-35). The correct answer is C.

Solomon provided food for Hiram in exchange for timber of cedar and cypress — he gave Hiram twenty thousand cors of wheat and twenty thousand cors of fine oil annually (1 Kings 5:11). The correct answer is B.

As David fled Jerusalem, he was apprehensive about the role of Ahithophel — Ahithophel was David's trusted counselor who had defected to Absalom, and David feared his advice to Absalom (2 Samuel 15:31; 16:23). The correct answer is A.

'And you, O Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah; for from you shall come a ruler who will govern my people Israel' fulfills the prophecy of Micah — Micah 5:2 prophesied the ruler would come from Bethlehem (Matthew 2:6). The correct answer is B.
The gift of gold to the infant Jesus indicated His royal status — gold was a symbol of kingship, acknowledging Jesus as the King of kings (Matthew 2:11). The correct answer is A.

The young man who asked about eternal life went away sorrowful because he had great possessions — when Jesus told him to sell everything and give to the poor, he was unable to do so (Matthew 19:22). The correct answer is C.
