According to Mark, the disciples were forbidden to take bread, bag and money for their journey — 'take nothing for your journey except a staff; no bag, no bread, no money in your belts' (Mark 6:8). The correct answer is D.

'You shall not tempt the LORD your God' — Jesus gave this reply to the temptation of jumping from the pinnacle of the temple, when Satan asked Him to throw Himself down (Matthew 4:7; Luke 4:12). The correct answer is C.

Peter's confession 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God' was given in the neighbourhood of Caesarea Philippi — 'Now when Jesus came into the district of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples...' (Matthew 16:13-16). The correct answer is C.

In Matthew's ethical teachings (chapters 5-7), the most important divine demand for inheriting the kingdom of God is doing the will of God — 'Not everyone who says to me, Lord, Lord, will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of my Father' (Matthew 7:21). The correct answer is A.

'If anyone would be first he must be last of all and servant of all' teaches humility — Jesus used a child as an example to show that true greatness in the kingdom means humble, servant-hearted living (Mark 9:35). The correct answer is C.

The appearance of Elijah and Moses at the transfiguration indicates the significance of the prophets and the law — Moses represents the Law and Elijah represents the Prophets; both testified to Jesus as the fulfillment of God's revelation (Matthew 17:3). The correct answer is B.

The Dragnet parable teaches about judgment and separation — the net gathers fish of every kind, then the good are separated from the bad at the end of the age (Matthew 13:47-50). The correct answer is B.

Jesus sent two disciples from Bethphage to make preparation for His last entry into Jerusalem — 'When they drew near to Jerusalem and came to Bethphage, to the Mount of Olives...' (Matthew 21:1-2). The correct answer is B.

One of Jesus' illustrations of true greatness is becoming like a child — He set a child before the disciples saying 'whoever humbles himself like this child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven' (Matthew 18:2-4). The correct answer is C.

The three thousand converts on the day of Pentecost devoted themselves to breaking of bread and the prayers — they also devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and fellowship (Acts 2:42). The correct answer is A.

In his speech concerning the replacement of Judas Iscariot, Peter quoted from the Psalms — he quoted Psalm 69:25 and Psalm 109:8 to justify choosing a replacement (Acts 1:20). The correct answer is D.
Nicanor and Nicolaus were two of the seven deacons — the seven deacons were Stephen, Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas (Acts 6:5). The correct answer is C.

According to the apostles' speech before the Sanhedrin, the Holy Spirit is given by God to those who obey God — 'the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey him' (Acts 5:32). The correct answer is C.
Philip was the one among the seven Hellenists who preached in Samaria and from Azotus to Caesarea (Acts 8:5, 40). The correct answer is D.

Simon the magician was rebuked by Peter because he wanted to purchase spiritual powers with money — 'May your silver perish with you, because you thought you could obtain the gift of God with money!' (Acts 8:20). The correct answer is C.
When Peter escaped from prison during the Passover, the guards were fast asleep — Peter walked past the guards unnoticed, led by an angel (Acts 12:6-9). The correct answer is D.

The first generation of mankind was destroyed in the great flood because of corruption and violence — 'the earth was corrupt in God's sight, and the earth was filled with violence' (Genesis 6:11). The correct answer is A.
The disciples were for the first time called Christians in Antioch — 'And in Antioch the disciples were first called Christians' (Acts 11:26). The correct answer is B.
'It is not good that the man should be alone' — God made a helper fit for him — the Hebrew 'ezer' means helper or helper suitable for him (Genesis 2:18). The correct answer is C.
God appeared to Jacob in a dream and Jacob made a vow to pay tithe to God — 'of all that you give me I will give a full tenth to you' (Genesis 28:20-22). The correct answer is D.

The sign of the covenant between God and Abraham is circumcision in the flesh of the foreskins — 'This is my covenant...every male among you shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskins' (Genesis 17:10-11). The correct answer is D.

Joseph saw his sale by his brothers as God's plan to preserve life — 'God sent me before you to preserve life' and 'God intended it for good, to preserve a numerous people' (Genesis 45:5; 50:20). The correct answer is D.

The fourth plague, which the Egyptian magicians could not reproduce, was gnats from the dust — after the magicians failed to produce gnats, they said 'This is the finger of God' (Exodus 8:18-19). The correct answer is A.

The possibility of crossing the Red Sea was seen by Israel as God's active presence in their midst — the parting of the sea demonstrated God's mighty power and presence fighting for Israel (Exodus 14:31). The correct answer is A.
The two Hebrew midwives instructed by Pharaoh to kill the Hebrew male babies were Shiphrah and Puah (Exodus 1:15). The correct answer is C.

The only commandment which has a promise attached to it concerns respecting/honouring parents — 'Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long in the land' (Exodus 20:12; Ephesians 6:2-3). The correct answer is A.
'What is sweeter than honey? What is stronger than a lion?' — Samson gave this riddle to the Philistines at his wedding feast (Judges 14:18). The correct answer is C.

Gideon was also called Jerubbaal because he pulled down the altar of Baal and cut down the Asherah beside it — 'Let Baal contend against him, because he has broken down his altar' (Judges 6:32). The correct answer is A.
Deborah was a famous prophetess who was also a judge in Israel — 'Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, was judging Israel at that time' (Judges 4:4). The correct answer is D.
'Draw your sword and kill me, lest men say of me, A woman killed him' — Abimelech said this after a woman dropped a millstone on his head (Judges 9:54). The correct answer is C.

'What portion have we in David?...To your tents, O Israel!' — this declaration marked the end of the united kingdom in Israel, as the ten northern tribes rebelled against Rehoboam under Jeroboam (1 Kings 12:16). The correct answer is B.

'My little finger is thicker than my father's loins' means that compared with his father, Rehoboam will be harsher — he threatened to impose even heavier burdens than Solomon (1 Kings 12:10-11). The correct answer is C.

Joshua was full of the spirit of wisdom because Moses had laid his hands upon him — 'And Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands on him' (Deuteronomy 34:9). The correct answer is B.
'Seek good, and not evil, that you may live, and so the LORD, the God of hosts, will be with you' — the prophet Amos gave this advice (Amos 5:14). The correct answer is B.

The incident which inspired King Josiah to undertake a reform was the discovery of the book of the law — Hilkiah the high priest found the book of the law during temple repairs and sent it to Josiah (2 Kings 22:8-13). The correct answer is C.

Sennacherib could not enter Jerusalem because thousands of his soldiers miraculously died overnight — the angel of the LORD struck down 185,000 Assyrian soldiers in their camp (2 Kings 19:35; Isaiah 37:36). The correct answer is B.

The vision of 'dry bones' teaches that exiled Israel will be restored — the valley of dry bones represented the whole house of Israel in exile; God promised to bring them back to their land (Ezekiel 37:11-14). The correct answer is D.

The Gilgamesh Epic is the Babylonian equivalent of the biblical story of the flood — like Noah's ark narrative, the Gilgamesh Epic contains a flood story with a man who builds a boat and saves animals (Genesis 6-9). The correct answer is D.

According to Herod, Jesus was John the Baptist raised from the dead because Jesus had the powers of John at work in Him — 'John, whom I beheaded, has been raised. That is why these miraculous powers are at work in him' (Mark 6:14-16). The correct answer is C.

Jesus heard the voice 'You are my beloved Son, with you I am well pleased' during His baptism — the Holy Spirit descended as a dove and a voice came from heaven (Mark 1:11; Luke 3:22). The correct answer is A.
The central message of John the Baptist was about a baptism of repentance — he preached 'a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins' (Mark 1:4; Luke 3:3). The correct answer is D.

'Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace among men with whom he pleased!' is usually referred to as the angels' song — it was sung by the heavenly host of angels at the birth of Jesus (Luke 2:14). The correct answer is A.

When John sent his disciples to ask if Jesus was 'the one who is to come,' Jesus' immediate reaction was to cure many diseases — He first healed many, then told John's disciples to report what they had seen and heard (Luke 7:21-22). The correct answer is B.

'I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such faith' was said during the healing of the centurion's servant — Jesus marveled at the centurion's faith (Matthew 8:10; Luke 7:9). The correct answer is D.
Jesus was led into the wilderness by the Spirit — 'the Spirit immediately drove him out into the wilderness' (Mark 1:12; Luke 4:1). The correct answer is B.

From the parable of the friend at midnight we learn that we cannot receive anything from God if we don't ask — the man's persistence obtained what he needed; Jesus taught 'ask, and it will be given to you' (Luke 11:8-10). The correct answer is A.

Joseph of Arimathea requested the body of Jesus after His death — he was a respected member of the council who had not consented to the verdict, and he courageously asked Pilate for Jesus' body (Mark 15:43; Luke 23:50-52). The correct answer is D.

'Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's' teaches obedience to civil authority — Christians are to fulfill their obligations to the state while also fulfilling their obligations to God (Mark 12:17). The correct answer is B.

'New wine must be put into fresh wineskins' was Jesus' response to the issue of fasting — the Pharisees and John's disciples fasted, but Jesus' disciples did not; Jesus explained that His new teaching could not be contained in old forms (Luke 5:33-38). The correct answer is C.

When Paul and Barnabas healed a cripple at Lystra, the people named them Zeus and Hermes — 'Barnabas they called Zeus, and Paul, Hermes, because he was the chief speaker' (Acts 14:12). The correct answer is A.

Paul was accused of preaching foreign divinities in Athens because he preached Jesus and the resurrection — 'he seems to be a preacher of foreign divinities — because he was preaching Jesus and the resurrection' (Acts 17:18). The correct answer is B.

'Did not our hearts burn within us while he talked to us?' expresses the reflection of Cleopas and one other disciple — they said this after recognizing that Jesus had been with them on the road to Emmaus (Luke 24:32). The correct answer is C.

'Do not be afraid, but speak and do not be silent; for I am with you...for I have many people in this city' — the city referred to was Corinth, where the Lord appeared to Paul in a vision (Acts 18:9-10). The correct answer is A.

Paul told the Athenians they were religious because they had dedicated an altar to the unknown God — 'For as I passed along and observed the objects of your worship, I found also an altar with this inscription: To the unknown god' (Acts 17:23). The correct answer is B.

During the voyage to Rome, some thought Paul was a god because he was not harmed by a viper — when a viper fastened on his hand and he shook it off with no ill effects, the people changed their minds and said he was a god (Acts 28:3-6). The correct answer is C.

To the Philippian jailer's question 'What must I do to be saved?' Paul replied, 'Believe in the Lord Jesus' — 'Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household' (Acts 16:31). The correct answer is B.

The four promises of God to Abram were land, many descendants, greatness, and medium of blessings — 'I will make of you a great nation, and I will bless you and make your name great, so that you will be a blessing...in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed' (Genesis 12:1-3). The correct answer is C.

'Be fruitful and multiply' first appears in Genesis following the creation of living creatures and birds — God blessed them on the fifth day when sea creatures and birds were created (Genesis 1:22). The correct answer is C.

'Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man shall his blood be shed; for God made man in his own image' — this passage explains the disapproval of violence and the value of human life (Genesis 9:6). The correct answer is D.

'Put off your shoes from your feet, for the place where you stand is holy' was said at Mount Horeb — God spoke these words to Moses from the burning bush on Mount Horeb (Exodus 3:5). The correct answer is A.

'God has made laughter for me; everyone who hears will laugh over me' was said at the birth of Isaac — Sarah said this, giving Isaac his name, which means 'laughter' (Genesis 21:6). The correct answer is B.

The main point of the story of Joseph's treatment of his brothers was that God's design for anybody cannot be stopped — Joseph saw it all as God's sovereign plan: 'You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good' (Genesis 50:20). The correct answer is A.

'Who is the LORD that I should heed his voice and let Israel go? I do not know the LORD.' What Pharaoh did next was increase their burden — he ordered that the Israelites be given no more straw for bricks, forcing them to gather it themselves while maintaining the same quota (Exodus 5:2, 7). The correct answer is A.

When the Israelites were trapped between Pharaoh's army and the Red Sea, God instructed Moses to stretch out his hand over the sea — 'Lift up your staff, and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it' (Exodus 14:16). The correct answer is D.

The condition that anything remaining until morning should be burnt is a correct Passover instruction — this eliminates option B as incorrect. Actually, the condition states the lamb should NOT be boiled but roasted (Exodus 12:9). The instruction that 'anything remaining until morning should be burnt' is a CORRECT condition (Exodus 12:10). The correct answer is B (anything that remains until morning shall be burned — this IS a correct condition).
To stay alive, anyone bitten by the fiery serpent had to look at the bronze serpent — 'everyone who is bitten, when he sees it, shall live' (Numbers 21:8-9). The correct answer is D.

'It is not the sound of shouting for victory, or the sound of the cry of defeat, but the sound of singing that I hear' was said during the worship of a new god — Joshua and Moses heard this sound as the Israelites were worshipping the golden calf they had made (Exodus 32:17-18). The correct answer is D.
Samson carried away the doors, posts, and bar of the city gate at Gaza — he arose at midnight and took hold of the doors of the gate of the city of Gaza (Judges 16:3). The correct answer is D.

The cities of the Amorites were completely devastated by Israel through the combined forces of panic, hailstone and sword — God threw them into a panic, cast down hailstones on them, and Israel struck them with the sword (Joshua 10:10-11). The correct answer is B.
'As I was with Moses, so I will be with you; I will not fail you or forsake you' — in this passage, God addresses Joshua at his commissioning (Joshua 1:5). The correct answer is B.
The city of Samaria was built by Omri — he bought the hill of Samaria and built the city (1 Kings 16:24). The correct answer is C.

The event that ultimately led to the destruction of the Northern Kingdom was the invasion of Syria by Assyria and Judah — the Assyrian empire conquered Syria (Aram) and eventually swept into the Northern Kingdom of Israel (2 Kings 17:5-6). The correct answer is A.

The theme of Amos' prophecies centers on the punishment of evil/social justice — Amos preached against social injustice, exploitation of the poor, and immoral behaviour among the privileged (Amos 2:6-7; 5:24). The correct answer is D.

Manasseh did what was evil in the sight of the LORD because he encouraged idol worship — he rebuilt the high places, erected altars for Baal, worshipped the host of heaven, and even placed an Asherah pole in the temple (2 Kings 21:3-7). The correct answer is C.

The image of jealousy which Ezekiel saw was the abomination in the temple — Ezekiel was shown the detestable things being done in the temple of God in Jerusalem, including idols and pagan worship (Ezekiel 8:3-6). The correct answer is C.

Zedekiah was the last king of Judah who suffered at the hands of Nebuchadnezzar — his sons were killed before his eyes, his eyes were put out, he was bound with bronze shackles, and taken to Babylon (2 Kings 25:7). The correct answer is D.

'Behold, this child is set for the fall and rising of many in Israel' means that many Israelites would be saved — Simeon's prophecy indicated Jesus would be a decisive turning point for many; some would fall and others rise because of Him (Luke 2:34). The correct answer is D.

The people around Jerusalem said they wanted to help rebuild the temple because they also worshipped the same God as the Jews — 'We seek your God as you do, and we have been sacrificing to him' (Ezra 4:2). The correct answer is D.
'The heaven was opened, and the Holy Spirit descended upon him in bodily form, as a dove and a voice came' — on this occasion Jesus was being baptized (Luke 3:21-22). The correct answer is A.

'Rob no one by violence or by false accusation' was the reply of John the Baptist to the soldiers — when soldiers asked what they should do, John told them to be content with their wages and not use their power to extort (Luke 3:14). The correct answer is C.

'Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?' — Jesus addressed these words to Joseph and Mary when they found Him in the temple after searching for three days (Luke 2:49). The correct answer is C.

The significance of Jesus allowing disciples to take certain things on their journey was that adequate material and spiritual preparation should be made for the work — the instructions ensured they went with what was needed but remained dependent on God's provision (Matthew 10:9-10). The correct answer is A.

James and John caused the other disciples to be angry because they asked for a special favour to sit with Jesus in His glory — they requested to sit at His right and left hand in glory, causing indignation among the other ten (Mark 10:41). The correct answer is B.

In the parable of the sower, seeds that fell on rock represent people who believed for a short while and later fell away — they receive the word with joy but have no root; when temptation comes they fall away (Luke 8:13). The correct answer is A.
The Sadducees did NOT believe in the resurrection of the dead — they denied resurrection, angels, and spirits (Mark 12:18; Acts 23:8). The correct answer is D.

Pilate delivered Jesus to be crucified because he wished to satisfy the crowd — 'So Pilate, wishing to satisfy the crowd, released for them Barabbas, and having scourged Jesus, he delivered him to be crucified' (Mark 15:15). The correct answer is A.
After His triumphal entry into Jerusalem, Jesus went to Bethany — 'And leaving them, he went out of the city to Bethany and lodged there' (Matthew 21:17; Mark 11:11). The correct answer is B.

The reason for the first Apostolic Council in Jerusalem was that circumcision was being enjoined on Gentile converts as necessary for salvation — 'Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved' (Acts 15:1). The correct answer is B.

The significance of laying on of hands was that the church under the guidance of the Holy Spirit initiated the missionary work of Paul and Barnabas — the Holy Spirit said 'Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them' (Acts 13:2-3). The correct answer is A.

The two disciples on the road to Emmaus recognized Jesus at the breaking of bread while at table — 'their eyes were opened and they recognized him' when He took bread, blessed it, and gave it to them (Luke 24:30-31). The correct answer is C.

When the ship was wrecked, the soldiers planned to kill the prisoners but the centurion prevented them because he wanted to save Paul's life — 'wishing to save Paul, he kept them from carrying out their plan' (Acts 27:43). The correct answer is C.

Before the Areopagus, Paul declared that the 'Unknown God' was indeed the creator of all — 'The God who made the world and everything in it, being Lord of heaven and earth...' (Acts 17:24). The correct answer is A.

One of the rules given to Noah after the flood was that he should not eat flesh with its blood — 'But you shall not eat flesh with its life, that is, its blood' (Genesis 9:4). The correct answer is B.
On arrival in Rome, Paul first addressed the Jewish Council (local leaders of the Jews) — 'After three days he called together the local leaders of the Jews' (Acts 28:17). The correct answer is D.

After Adam said 'I was afraid because I was naked, and I hid myself,' the question that immediately followed was 'Who told you that you were naked?' — God asked this before 'Have you eaten of the tree?' (Genesis 3:11). The correct answer is B.

Pharaoh oppressed the Israelites because he feared that they might join his enemies to fight him — 'Come, let us deal shrewdly with them, lest they multiply, and if war breaks out, they join our enemies and fight against us' (Exodus 1:10). The correct answer is A.

'The lad is gone; and I, where shall I go?' was said by Reuben, Joseph's eldest brother — when Reuben returned to the pit and found Joseph gone, he tore his clothes and said this (Genesis 37:29-30). The correct answer is C.

Moses could not enter the Promised Land because he did not give due regard to God — at the waters of Meribah, Moses struck the rock instead of speaking to it, failing to uphold God's holiness before Israel (Numbers 20:12). The correct answer is C.

The LORD fought for Israel by drowning the Egyptian army in the Red Sea — He parted the waters for Israel and then caused the waters to return, drowning all Pharaoh's horses, chariots, and horsemen (Exodus 14:27-28). The correct answer is A.

When Moses delayed coming down from the mountain, the Israelites asked Aaron to make gods for them — 'The people gathered around Aaron and said to him, Up, make us gods who shall go before us' (Exodus 32:1). The correct answer is D.
Rahab the harlot assisted the Israelite spies as they prepared to attack Jericho — she hid the two spies and helped them escape (Joshua 2:1-21). The correct answer is C.

Moses consecrated Joshua as the new leader in the presence of Eleazar — 'He laid his hands on him and commissioned him as the LORD directed through Moses,' with Eleazar the priest present (Numbers 27:22-23). The correct answer is B.

The pledge 'All that you have commanded us we will do...Just as we obeyed Moses, so we will obey you' was made to Joshua by the Reubenites, the Gadites, and part of the tribe of Manasseh (Joshua 1:16-17). The correct answer is A.

Gideon was able to defeat the Midianites with a reduced number of soldiers because he had faith in God — God reduced the army from 32,000 to 300 so that Israel would know the victory was from God, not their own strength (Judges 7:2-7). The correct answer is D.

'Out of the eater came something to eat. Out of the strong came something sweet' — this riddle was explained first to Samson's wife, who then told the Philistines (Judges 14:15-17). The correct answer is A.
For offending God, the Israelites were delivered into the power of Midian for seven years — 'the LORD gave them into the hand of Midian for seven years' (Judges 6:1). The correct answer is A.

Gomer was unfaithful to her husband as Israel was to God — Hosea married Gomer, who was unfaithful, as a living parable of Israel's spiritual unfaithfulness to God (Hosea 1:2-3; 3:1). The correct answer is A.

When Elisha received the message about Ben-Hadad's illness, the prophet wept because Hazael would be cruel to Israel — Elisha saw in a vision that Hazael would become king and do terrible things to Israel (2 Kings 8:12-13). The correct answer is D.

'As the LORD the God of Israel lives...there shall be neither dew nor rain these years except by my word' — this prophecy was during the reign of King Ahab; Elijah spoke this to Ahab (1 Kings 17:1). The correct answer is B.

'Incline thy ear, O LORD, and hear; open thy eyes, O LORD, and see; and hear the words of Sennacherib' was the prayer of Hezekiah — he spread the letter from Sennacherib before the LORD and prayed (2 Kings 19:15-16; Isaiah 37:17). The correct answer is D.

Saul initially desired to kill David because David became very popular after killing Goliath — 'Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands' — and Saul was filled with jealousy (1 Samuel 18:7-9). The correct answer is A.

God revealed to Solomon that the kingdom would be divided because he worshipped other gods — his foreign wives turned his heart to other gods, and God was angry (1 Kings 11:9-11). The correct answer is D.

'I am bringing upon Jerusalem and Judah such evil that the ears of every one who hears of it will tingle' — this was because of the sins of Manasseh, the most wicked king of Judah (2 Kings 21:12-16). The correct answer is B.

King Herod granted the request to behead John the Baptist because he was bound by oath and personal integrity — he had sworn an oath and felt he could not refuse in front of his guests (Matthew 14:7-9). The correct answer is C.
'In the year that King Uzziah died I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne' is associated with Isaiah — this was the year of his call and vision in the temple (Isaiah 6:1). The correct answer is C.

Having a good knowledge of the scriptures is NOT a stated condition for being a disciple of Jesus — the conditions Jesus stated were self-denial, taking up the cross daily, and following Him (Luke 9:23). The correct answer is C.

According to Mark's Gospel, the first miracle of Jesus was healing a man with an unclean spirit — in the synagogue at Capernaum, Jesus commanded the unclean spirit to come out (Mark 1:23-26). The correct answer is C.

'A great prophet has arisen among us!' and 'God has visited his people!' were said during the raising of the son of the widow of Nain — Jesus raised the widow's dead son, and this response of the people followed (Luke 7:16). The correct answer is B.
Peacemakers are blessed because they shall be called the sons of God — 'Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God' (Matthew 5:9). The correct answer is D.

'He who hears you hears me, and he who rejects you rejects me' was addressed to the 70 disciples whom He sent out to preach — Jesus said this as instructions to the seventy (Luke 10:16). The correct answer is C.
The Jews asked Jesus whether they should pay tax to entrap Him in His talk — they wanted to force Him into a politically dangerous answer (Matthew 22:15; Luke 20:20). The correct answer is A.

Jesus began teaching His disciples about His suffering after Peter's Confession — 'From that time Jesus began to show his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things' (Matthew 16:21). The correct answer is C.

Jesus gave the sign of Jonah to indicate His death and resurrection — just as Jonah was three days in the belly of the fish, so the Son of Man would be three days in the earth (Matthew 12:39-40). The correct answer is D.

Herod was very glad to see Jesus at the trial because he hoped to see Jesus perform some miracles — he had wanted to see Jesus for a long time and hoped to witness a sign (Luke 23:8). The correct answer is C.

'Blessed is the king who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!' was connected with Jesus' triumphal entry into Jerusalem — the disciples praised God joyfully as Jesus rode on the colt (Luke 19:38). The correct answer is B.

'The Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many' was said during the discussion that followed the request by the sons of Zebedee (Matthew 20:28; Mark 10:45). The correct answer is C.

'I have no silver and gold, but I give you what I have; in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, rise up and walk!' — Peter said this to the lame man at the gate called Beautiful (Acts 3:6). The correct answer is C.

The message of the risen Christ to the women at the tomb was to be relayed to the disciples and to Peter — 'go, tell his disciples and Peter that he is going before you to Galilee' (Mark 16:7). The correct answer is D.

According to Mark, the people who saw where Jesus was laid were Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of James — 'Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses saw where he was laid' (Mark 15:47). The correct answer is B.

Saul and Barnabas were sent on their mission by the church at Antioch — the Holy Spirit said 'Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them,' and the church at Antioch sent them off (Acts 13:1-3). The correct answer is A.

The immediate cause of the stoning of Stephen was his claiming to see Jesus at the right hand of God — 'But he, full of the Holy Spirit...said, Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God' (Acts 7:55-58). The correct answer is D.

The Jew alluded to when the crowd cried 'Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!' for two hours was Alexander — the Jews put Alexander forward, but when the crowd recognized he was a Jew, they shouted in opposition (Acts 19:33-34). The correct answer is B.

Paul purified himself in the Temple after the third missionary journey because he was advised to do so by the elders — James and the elders suggested Paul join four men under a vow and pay for their purification to show he lived in observance of the law (Acts 21:23-24). The correct answer is B.

'They have beaten us publicly, uncondemned, men who are Roman citizens and have thrown us into prison; and do they now cast us out secretly?' — this experience of Paul was in Philippi (Acts 16:37). The correct answer is C.

Of the four sent to Antioch with the letter, Paul and Barnabas remained behind in Antioch — 'But Paul and Barnabas remained in Antioch, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord' while Judas and Silas returned to Jerusalem (Acts 15:34-35). The correct answer is C.
According to Paul, the greatest is Love — 'So now faith, hope, and love abide, these three; but the greatest of these is love' (1 Corinthians 13:13). The correct answer is B.

During Paul's trial by the Tribune, he brought a division between the Pharisees and Sadducees by mentioning the issue of the Resurrection — he declared 'It is with respect to the hope and the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial' (Acts 23:6). The correct answer is A.

'Your blood be upon your heads! I am innocent. From now on I will go to the Gentiles' was said by Paul — he said this at Corinth when the Jews opposed and reviled him (Acts 18:6). The correct answer is B.

When Saul escaped from Damascus and came to Jerusalem, the disciples were afraid of him — they did not believe he was truly a disciple; Barnabas had to vouch for him (Acts 9:26). The correct answer is B.

'Abstain from what has been sacrificed to idols and from blood and from what is strangled and from unchastity' — this was a response to the circumcision controversy at the Jerusalem Council (Acts 15:20, 29). The correct answer is A.

Paul and Barnabas were called 'gods' in Lystra because they healed a crippled man — after Paul healed a man lame from birth, the crowds declared Barnabas was Zeus and Paul was Hermes (Acts 14:8-12). The correct answer is C.

The immediate effect of Peter's statement 'You have not lied to men but to God' on Ananias was that he fell down dead — 'When Ananias heard these words, he fell down and breathed his last' (Acts 5:5). The correct answer is C.
The apostles created the office of deacon to address the problem of injustice — the Hellenistic widows were being neglected in the daily distribution of food (Acts 6:1-3). The correct answer is A.
The first statement of Jesus on the cross according to Luke was 'Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they do' (Luke 23:34). The correct answer is C.

Very early on the first day of the week, three women went to the tomb to anoint the body of Jesus — 'And when the Sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices, so that they might go and anoint him' (Mark 16:1; Luke 24:1). The correct answer is C.

After Peter's declaration 'God has made him both Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified,' the Jews were deeply troubled and asked what they should do — 'Now when they heard this they were cut to the heart, and said...Brothers, what shall we do?' (Acts 2:37). The correct answer is C.

'My house shall be a house of prayer, but you have made it a den of robbers' — just before making this statement, Jesus drove out those who sold in the temple (Matthew 21:12-13; Mark 11:15-17). The correct answer is C.

After their mission, the seventy disciples reported to Jesus that demons were subject to them in His name — 'Lord, even the demons are subject to us in your name!' (Luke 10:17). The correct answer is D.

'This is my beloved Son, listen to him' was said on the occasion of Jesus' transfiguration — a voice from the cloud spoke these words while Moses and Elijah were present (Mark 9:7; Luke 9:35). The correct answer is C.

The story of the healing of blind Bartimaeus teaches that faith is a prerequisite for healing — Jesus said to Bartimaeus 'Go your way; your faith has made you well' (Mark 10:52). The correct answer is D.

According to Matthew's account, the most important divine requirement for entering the kingdom of heaven is doing the will of God — 'Not everyone who says to me, Lord, Lord, will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of my Father who is in heaven' (Matthew 7:21). The correct answer is B.

The parable of the prodigal son emphasizes that repentance and reconciliation are important — the father's joyful reception of the repentant son and his appeal to the elder son both emphasize reconciliation (Luke 15:20-32). The correct answer is B.

Jesus was mistaken for a ghost by His disciples in the miracle of walking on the sea — the disciples were terrified and said 'It is a ghost!' when they saw Him walking on water (Matthew 14:26; Mark 6:49). The correct answer is D.

'I adjure you by God, do not torment me' is a recognition that demons are subject to Jesus — the demon acknowledged Jesus' authority and power over it by begging not to be tormented (Mark 5:7). The correct answer is C.

According to Luke, the healing of the paralytic was intended to show that Jesus has authority to forgive sins — Jesus healed the paralytic as proof that 'the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins' (Luke 5:24). The correct answer is B.
Jesus said that whoever wants to be first or great among the apostles must be a slave of all — 'whoever would be first among you must be slave of all' (Mark 10:44). The correct answer is B.

A would-be disciple who puts his hand to the plough and looks back lacks total commitment — 'No one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God' (Luke 9:62). The correct answer is D.

'Lord, now lettest thy servant depart in peace...for mine eyes have seen thy salvation' was said at the presentation of Jesus in the temple by Simeon — the aged Simeon held Jesus and uttered this prayer (Luke 2:29-30). The correct answer is C.
'You brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?' was said by John to the Pharisees and Sadducees who came to his baptism (Matthew 3:7). The correct answer is A.
In the second angelic appearance in Matthew, the angel instructed Joseph to go into exile — 'Rise, take the child and his mother, and flee to Egypt' (Matthew 2:13). The correct answer is C.
'Let there be lights in the firmament of the heavens to separate the day from the night' — God said this on the fourth day of creation (Genesis 1:14). The correct answer is B.

The story of the Fall teaches that it is a sin to disobey God — Adam and Eve disobeyed God's direct command and suffered consequences; sin entered through disobedience (Genesis 3:17; Romans 5:19). The correct answer is B.
Darkness was upon the face of the deep on the first day of creation — 'The earth was without form and void, and darkness was over the face of the deep' (Genesis 1:2). The correct answer is D.
'Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would suckle children?' was asked by Sarah — Sarah said this in amazement at the birth of Isaac (Genesis 21:7). The correct answer is A.

'All the fountains of the great deep burst forth and the windows of the heavens were opened' — the result of this was heavy rainfall that caused the great flood (Genesis 7:11-12). The correct answer is B.

'Let me not look upon the death of the child' comes from the story of the expulsion of Hagar and Ishmael — Hagar put Ishmael under a bush and sat down saying this as she feared he would die of thirst (Genesis 21:16). The correct answer is B.
Joseph's dream about his future leadership was fulfilled when he became the second in command to Pharaoh — Pharaoh set him over all Egypt (Genesis 41:40-43). The correct answer is D.
The children of Israel cried out to God because they were in bondage — 'the people of Israel groaned because of their slavery and cried out for help' (Exodus 2:23). The correct answer is B.

'What is this we have done, that we have let Israel go from serving us?' was said by Pharaoh and his servants — they regretted releasing Israel when they needed the workforce (Exodus 14:5). The correct answer is D.
Israel's response to Joshua's challenge was 'We also will serve the LORD, for He is our God' (Joshua 24:18). The correct answer is A.
The manna the Israelites left till morning in disobedience bred worms and became foul — 'when they left part of it till the morning, it bred worms and stank' (Exodus 16:20). The correct answer is C.
While David was being anointed king, he received the Spirit of the LORD — 'and the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon David from that day forward' (1 Samuel 16:13). The correct answer is D.
The prophets Saul met at Gibeath-elohim were ecstatic prophets — they were prophesying with musical instruments, in a prophetic frenzy (1 Samuel 10:5-6, 10). The correct answer is C.

Solomon could devote attention to building the house of the LORD because there was neither adversary nor misfortune — 'there is no adversary and no misfortune' during his reign (1 Kings 5:4). The correct answer is C.

The Israelites were fighting against the Ammonites when David committed adultery with Uriah's wife — Joab was besieging Rabbah of the Ammonites while David remained in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 11:1). The correct answer is B.

According to Genesis 1, God charged man to have dominion over all the earth — 'let them have dominion over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the heavens and over the livestock and over all the earth' (Genesis 1:26). The correct answer is C.

'Arise, go to Zarephath...Behold, I have commanded a widow there to feed you' — what necessitated this was the drought caused by Elijah's word — the brook Cherith dried up because there was no rain (1 Kings 17:7). The correct answer is A.

The immediate cause of the division of the kingdom was Rehoboam's foolishness — he rejected the elders' advice and followed the young men's harsh counsel, causing the people to rebel (1 Kings 12:13-16). The correct answer is C.
After Jacob's dream at Bethel, he promised to give a tenth of all he would have to God — 'of all that you give me I will give a full tenth to you' (Genesis 28:22). The correct answer is B.

'Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man shall his blood be shed; for God made man in his own image' explains the disapproval of violence — human life is sacred because man is made in God's image (Genesis 9:6). The correct answer is C.

When God told Abraham that Sarah would have a child, Abraham laughed because they were too old to have a child — 'Shall a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old? Shall Sarah, who is ninety years old, bear a child?' (Genesis 17:17). The correct answer is C.

God redeemed the Israelites from Pharaoh because He remembered His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — 'God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob' (Exodus 2:24). The correct answer is A.
Judah advised his brothers against shedding Joseph's blood because Joseph was their brother — 'he is our brother, our own flesh' (Genesis 37:27). The correct answer is B.

When the people of Israel saw the great work of the LORD in drowning the Egyptians, they believed in Moses — 'Israel saw the great power that the LORD used against the Egyptians...and they believed in the LORD and in his servant Moses' (Exodus 14:31). The correct answer is C.
Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel for presentation before God at Shechem — 'Joshua assembled all the tribes of Israel at Shechem' (Joshua 24:1). The correct answer is A.

The golden calf Aaron made signified a return to the gods of Egypt — the calf was an Egyptian deity symbol; the people were reverting to idol worship they had known in Egypt (Exodus 32:4; cf. Acts 7:41). The correct answer is A.

The valley of Eshcol is symbolic because it was where the men of Israel cut down the cluster of grapes — the spies cut down a branch with a single cluster of grapes there, showing the land's fruitfulness (Numbers 13:23-24). The correct answer is A.

The report brought by the men who followed Caleb showed that the land devoured its inhabitants — the ten fearful spies said 'the land...devours its inhabitants, and all the people that we saw in it are of great height' (Numbers 13:32). The correct answer is C.
A good example of parental upbringing is manifested in the son of Asa — Jehoshaphat, the son of Asa, walked in the good ways of his father (1 Kings 22:43; 2 Chronicles 17:3). The correct answer is D.
'The LORD give you children by this woman for the loan which she lent to the LORD' — the loan was Samuel, who Hannah dedicated to God as she had vowed (1 Samuel 2:20-21). The correct answer is A.

The sin committed by Saul that cost him his kingdom was disobedience — he disobeyed God's command by sparing Agag and the best livestock in the battle against the Amalekites (1 Samuel 15:22-23). The correct answer is A.

'Blessed be you, my son David! You will do many things and will succeed in them' was said when David spared Saul's life — Saul said this after David spared his life in the cave at En-gedi (1 Samuel 24:20). The correct answer is A.
The consequence of Rehoboam's unwise decision resulted in a rebellion — the ten northern tribes rebelled under Jeroboam, dividing the kingdom (1 Kings 12:16-19). The correct answer is A.
According to Luke, John the Baptist instructed the multitudes to bear fruits that befit repentance — 'Bear fruits in keeping with repentance' (Luke 3:8). The correct answer is A.

Solomon asked God for wisdom to discern what was right — 'Give your servant therefore an understanding mind to govern your people, that I may discern between good and evil' (1 Kings 3:9). The correct answer is D.

One important fact about Mary at the wedding in Cana was that she had a deep insight of her son and His ability — she told the servants 'Do whatever he tells you,' showing her confidence in Jesus (John 2:5). The correct answer is D.

Jesus was tempted in the wilderness in order to prepare Him for His earthly ministry — the temptation proved His readiness to begin His public ministry by resisting Satan's challenges (Matthew 4:1-11; Hebrews 4:15). The correct answer is A.

'Go and search diligently for the child, and when...' — the intention of Herod in this context was to kill the child — he told the Magi this while secretly planning to destroy Jesus (Matthew 2:13). The correct answer is D.

The centurion's statement 'I am not worthy to have you come under my roof' and his continuation shows that he had faith in the power of Jesus' word — he believed Jesus only needed to say the word and his servant would be healed (Luke 7:7). The correct answer is B.

The epileptic boy could not be healed by the disciples because they had not yet received power — Jesus explained 'This kind cannot be driven out by anything but prayer and fasting' (Mark 9:29). The correct answer is A.

The raising of Lazarus illustrates that Jesus is the giver of life — 'I am the resurrection and the life' — Jesus demonstrated His power over death by raising Lazarus (John 11:25, 43-44). The correct answer is C.

Jesus' objective for sending out the twelve was to train the disciples in His ministry — He sent them to preach, heal, and cast out demons, equipping them for ministry (Matthew 10:1-8; Mark 6:7-13). The correct answer is B.
Those who are hated and reviled shall have a great reward in heaven — 'Rejoice in that day, and leap for joy, for behold, your reward is great in heaven' (Luke 6:22-23). The correct answer is A.
The poor in spirit are promised the kingdom of God — 'Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God' (Luke 6:20). The correct answer is B.

The request by the sons of Zebedee was not granted because it was not the duty of Jesus to grant their request — 'to sit at my right hand or at my left is not mine to grant, but it is for those for whom it has been prepared' (Mark 10:40). The correct answer is D.

The accusers of Jesus stayed behind at the Praetorium because they did not want to be defiled — Jews would not enter a Gentile's house lest they be ritually defiled for Passover (John 18:28). The correct answer is D.

Pilate was perplexed because Jesus gave no answer to the charges — 'But he gave him no answer, not even to a single charge, so that the governor was greatly amazed' (Matthew 27:14; Mark 15:5). The correct answer is B.
Simon of Cyrene was forced to carry the cross behind Jesus (Luke 23:26; Mark 15:21). The correct answer is D.

'Truly, I say to you, today you will be with me in paradise' was said to the repentant robber — the criminal who acknowledged his guilt and asked Jesus to remember him (Luke 23:42-43). The correct answer is B.

According to Luke, the people who first got to Jesus' tomb were Mary Magdalene and the other women — 'Now it was Mary Magdalene and Joanna and Mary the mother of James and the other women with them who told these things to the apostles' (Luke 24:1, 10). The correct answer is C.

'I am the resurrection and the life; he who believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live' was said on the day Jesus restored Lazarus back to life — Jesus spoke these words to Martha before raising Lazarus (John 11:25). The correct answer is C.

Jesus Christ, the Good Shepherd, was loved by the Father because He laid down His life for the sheep — 'For this reason the Father loves me, because I lay down my life that I may take it up again' (John 10:17). The correct answer is D.

'Now the company of those who believed were of one heart and soul' reveals that the early Christians had everything in common — 'no one said that any of the things that belonged to him was his own, but they had everything in common' (Acts 4:32). The correct answer is A.

According to Paul, if we give away all we have and deliver our bodies to be burnt but have not love, we gain nothing — 'If I give away all I have...but have not love, I gain nothing' (1 Corinthians 13:3). The correct answer is D.

'I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh' — this prophecy was fulfilled at Pentecost when Peter quoted Joel and the disciples were filled with the Holy Spirit (Acts 2:16-17). The correct answer is B.

'You shall be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria and to the end of the earth' commissions the apostles to carry the gospel to all continents — the Great Commission encompasses the whole world (Acts 1:8). The correct answer is B.
The suggestion to choose the seven deacons was made by the twelve — the twelve apostles called together the full number of disciples and proposed the plan (Acts 6:2-3). The correct answer is C.

Following his encounter with the apostles, the ruler of Cyprus (Sergius Paulus) believed the gospel — 'the proconsul believed, when he saw what had occurred, for he was astonished at the teaching of the Lord' (Acts 13:12). The correct answer is D.

'Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them' was made by the Holy Spirit — the Holy Spirit directed the church at Antioch through prophets and teachers (Acts 13:2). The correct answer is A.

Naboth did not agree to release his vineyard because it was the inheritance of his fathers — 'The LORD forbid that I should give you the inheritance of my fathers' (1 Kings 21:3). The correct answer is D.

The contest on Mount Carmel was to prove that God was supreme over all other gods — Elijah challenged Israel: 'If the LORD is God, follow him; but if Baal, then follow him' (1 Kings 18:21). The correct answer is C.
Jerusalem fell in 586 B.C. to the Babylonian king Nebuchadnezzar — he destroyed the city, burned the temple, and took the people into exile (2 Kings 25:1-11). The correct answer is A.

The greatest achievement of King Josiah was his sweeping reforms of the religious life of his people — he purged the temple, destroyed all idols and high places, and renewed the Passover celebration (2 Kings 23:1-25). The correct answer is B.

Gehazi deceitfully received two talents of silver and two festal garments from Naaman — he ran after Naaman and falsely claimed Elisha wanted these gifts for two young prophets (2 Kings 5:22-23). The correct answer is A.
Nebuchadnezzar said the fourth figure in the furnace was like a son of the gods (or a son of God) — 'the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods' (Daniel 3:25). The correct answer is A.

Nehemiah was sad because the condition of Jerusalem was deplorable — when King Artaxerxes asked why his face was sad, Nehemiah explained about the ruined walls and gates of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 2:2-3). The correct answer is A.

Daniel was not harmed by the lions because an angel shut the mouths of the lions — 'My God sent his angel and shut the lions' mouths, and they have not harmed me' (Daniel 6:22). The correct answer is A.

Daniel was distinguished above all others because he had an excellent spirit in him — 'Daniel became distinguished above all the other presidents and satraps, because an excellent spirit was in him' (Daniel 6:3). The correct answer is B.
God spared Nineveh because the people responded positively to God's mercy — they believed God, fasted, put on sackcloth, and turned from their evil ways (Jonah 3:5-10). The correct answer is B.

Selling the needy for a pair of shoes in Amos means oppressing the needy — treating human beings as mere commodities shows extreme devaluation of persons and oppression of the poor (Amos 2:6; 8:6). The correct answer is D.

In Amos' prophecy about Israel's transgressions, he condemned Israel for completely neglecting social justice — they sold the righteous for silver, trampled the poor, and perverted justice (Amos 2:6-8). The correct answer is D.
The Israelites did evil in the days of the Judges by serving the Baals — 'the people of Israel did what was evil in the sight of the LORD and served the Baals' (Judges 2:11). The correct answer is D.

The central theme of Isaiah's teachings is that no sinner is beyond redemption — Isaiah proclaimed both judgment and hope, showing that even sinful Israel could be restored through God's mercy (Isaiah 1:18; 55:7). The correct answer is C.

From Hosea's teaching we learn that God prefers steadfast love to sacrifice — 'For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings' (Hosea 6:6). The correct answer is D.

Isaiah offered himself to be God's messenger because, having been cleansed of his sins, he saw the need to warn others — after the seraph touched his lips and he was cleansed, he responded to God's call (Isaiah 6:7-8). The correct answer is B.

The expression 'dry bones' in Ezekiel refers to the whole house of Israel — God explained: 'These bones are the whole house of Israel. Behold, they say, Our bones are dried up, and our hope is lost' (Ezekiel 37:11). The correct answer is B.

God told Jeremiah He would give Jerusalem to the Chaldeans because the Israelites had provoked God to anger — by their persistent idolatry and wickedness, they provoked God's judgment (Jeremiah 32:28-30). The correct answer is A.

According to Ezekiel, the exiles blamed their fathers for their plight — they used the proverb 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge' to blame their ancestors (Ezekiel 18:2). The correct answer is C.

All Christians who have been baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death — 'all of us who have been baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death' (Romans 6:3). The correct answer is A.

Justification by grace shows that work is not required for salvation — 'For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God, not a result of works' (Ephesians 2:8-9; Romans 11:6). The correct answer is A.

The function of the law to believers before Christ was that of a custodian (guardian/tutor) — 'the law was our guardian until Christ came, in order that we might be justified by faith' (Galatians 3:24-25). The correct answer is A.

The main aim of teaching Christ's humility in Philippians is that every Christian should look into the interest of others and do nothing from selfishness — 'Let each of you look not only to his own interests, but also to the interests of others' (Philippians 2:3-4). The correct answer is D.

God condemned sin in the flesh by sending His own Son in the likeness of man — 'By sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and for sin, he condemned sin in the flesh' (Romans 8:3). The correct answer is A.
'But you are not in darkness, brethren, for that day to surprise you like a thief' — 'that day' refers to the coming of the Lord (Second Coming) (1 Thessalonians 5:4). The correct answer is C.
'Be angry but do not sin' means that anger could be an occasion for sin — Paul warns not to let anger persist and become a doorway to sinful behaviour (Ephesians 4:26). The correct answer is D.

God exalted Jesus and gave Him a name above all names because He was humble and obedient unto death — 'he humbled himself by becoming obedient to the point of death...Therefore God has highly exalted him' (Philippians 2:8-9). The correct answer is B.
Christians are encouraged to bear one another's burdens to fulfill the law of Christ — 'Bear one another's burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ' (Galatians 6:2). The correct answer is D.

All the varieties of spiritual gifts are given by the Holy Spirit — 'All these are empowered by one and the same Spirit, who apportions to each one individually as he wills' (1 Corinthians 12:11). The correct answer is D.
The overriding principle in the use of spiritual gifts is decency and order — 'all things should be done decently and in order' (1 Corinthians 14:40). The correct answer is A.

Contribution of relief materials for the needy, according to Paul, must be with cheerfulness — 'Each one must give as he has decided in his heart, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver' (2 Corinthians 9:7). The correct answer is C.

When Paul says 'If anyone will not work, let him not eat,' he is saying that every person should toil and labour with his hands — 'we worked night and day, that we might not be a burden to any of you' and 'work and earn their own living' (2 Thessalonians 3:10, 12). The correct answer is C.

Paul teaches we should obey governing authorities to avoid God's wrath and a bad conscience — 'he is God's servant, an avenger who carries out God's wrath on the wrongdoer...it is necessary to be in subjection...also for the sake of conscience' (Romans 13:4-5). The correct answer is D.

Paul worked harder than any of the apostles because of the grace of God that was with him — 'But by the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace toward me was not in vain. On the contrary, I worked harder than any of them, though it was not I, but the grace of God that is with me' (1 Corinthians 15:10). The correct answer is B.

The lawless one will be slain by the breath of His mouth — 'the Lord Jesus will kill with the breath of his mouth and bring to nothing by the appearance of his coming' (2 Thessalonians 2:8). The correct answer is D.
Christian wives are to be subject to their husbands because it is fitting in the LORD — 'Wives, submit to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord' (Colossians 3:18). The correct answer is B.

Paul's experience teaches that the attitude of Christians to sufferings should be that of perseverance — Paul catalogued his many sufferings (beatings, shipwrecks, dangers) and showed how he persevered through them all (2 Corinthians 11:23-28). The correct answer is D.

'What you sow does not come to life unless it dies' refers to the resurrection of the dead — Paul used this agricultural metaphor to explain the nature of resurrection (1 Corinthians 15:36). The correct answer is C.

An important feature of the second coming of Jesus as taught by Paul is the resurrection of the dead — 'the dead in Christ will rise first, then we who are alive...will be caught up together' (1 Thessalonians 4:16-17). The correct answer is D.

The men of old mentioned as examples of faith in Hebrews include Abel, Abraham, and Rahab — the 'Hall of Faith' in Hebrews 11 names Abel (v.4), Abraham (v.8), and Rahab (v.31). The correct answer is D.

Despite their faith, the men of old did not receive what was promised — the promise was Jesus Christ; they saw it from afar but did not live to see its fulfillment (Hebrews 11:39-40). The correct answer is A.

Abraham's faith and works were best illustrated when he offered his son Isaac on the altar — 'Was not Abraham our father justified by works when he offered up his son Isaac on the altar? You see that faith was active along with his works' (James 2:21-22). The correct answer is B.

Peter enjoins Christians to be good citizens by submitting to civil authorities — 'Be subject for the Lord's sake to every human institution, whether it be to the emperor...or to governors' (1 Peter 2:13-14). The correct answer is C.

According to James, effective prayer is that which is offered in faith — 'the prayer of faith will save the one who is sick' and 'the prayer of a righteous person has great power' (James 5:15-16). The correct answer is A.

According to Peter, Christians living among non-Christians should maintain good conduct — 'Keep your conduct among the Gentiles honorable, so that when they speak against you as evildoers, they may see your good deeds and glorify God' (1 Peter 2:12). The correct answer is A.

According to Paul, the law and the prophets bear witness to the righteousness of God — 'the righteousness of God has been manifested apart from the law, although the Law and the Prophets bear witness to it' (Romans 3:21). The correct answer is A.

According to Paul in Galatians, one is justified by faith in Jesus Christ — 'we know that a person is not justified by works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ' (Galatians 2:16). The correct answer is D.

In the country of the Gerasenes, Jesus healed the man possessed of demons (the Gerasene demoniac) — the man had a legion of demons and lived among the tombs (Mark 5:1-15; Luke 8:26-35). The correct answer is A.

According to Luke, when Moses and Elijah appeared during the Transfiguration, they spoke of Jesus' departure — 'they spoke of his departure, which he was about to accomplish at Jerusalem' (Luke 9:31). The correct answer is A.
Herod was delighted to see Jesus because he had heard of Him for so long and wanted to see Him perform miracles — 'he was hoping to see some sign done by him' (Luke 23:8). The correct answer is C.

The baptism of Jesus by John was to fulfill all righteousness — when John hesitated, Jesus said 'Let it be so now, for thus it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness' (Matthew 3:15). The correct answer is D.

In Luke, at the Last Supper, Jesus revealed His imminent sufferings — He spoke of His body given and blood poured out, and told of the one who would betray Him (Luke 22:19-22). The correct answer is B.
'Unbind him, and let him go' was said by Jesus when He raised to life the dead Lazarus — after Lazarus came out of the tomb still wrapped in grave clothes (John 11:44). The correct answer is A.
'Do you understand what you are reading?' — Philip found the Ethiopian eunuch reading the book of Isaiah (Acts 8:28-30). The correct answer is D.

'Can anyone forbid water for baptizing these people who have received the Holy Spirit just as we have?' was said by Peter at the conversion of Cornelius — the Gentiles had received the Holy Spirit just as the Jews had (Acts 10:47). The correct answer is D.
The Good Shepherd is one who lays down his life for his sheep — 'I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep' (John 10:11). The correct answer is A.

Jesus' stilling of the storm was to demonstrate His power — the disciples marveled asking 'Who then is this, that even wind and sea obey him?' showing His authority over creation (Mark 4:41). The correct answer is C.

The sin of the sons of Eli was that they treated the offering of the LORD with contempt — 'the sin of the young men was very great in the sight of the LORD, for the men treated the offering of the LORD with contempt' (1 Samuel 2:17). The correct answer is B.
The disciple who replaced Judas Iscariot was Matthias — he was chosen by lot from among the candidates (Acts 1:26). The correct answer is C.
'I will not eat until I have told my errand' — Abraham's servant's errand was to find a wife for Isaac (Genesis 24:33). The correct answer is A.
For worshipping the molten calf, God described the Israelites as a stiff-necked people — 'I have seen this people, and behold, it is a stiff-necked people' (Exodus 32:9). The correct answer is C.

When God called Moses but Moses said he could not speak, he was told to go with Aaron who would speak for him — 'He shall speak for you to the people, and he shall be your mouth' (Exodus 4:14-16). The correct answer is D.

According to Galatians, one benefit of being a joint heir with Christ is having His Spirit in the heart — 'And because you are sons, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, Abba! Father!' (Galatians 4:6-7). The correct answer is B.
David was anointed king over Judah at Hebron — 'the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah' at Hebron (2 Samuel 2:4). The correct answer is C.
'Let the waters under the heavens be gathered into one place, and let the dry land appear' — the dry land and the waters refer to earth and seas (Genesis 1:9-10). The correct answer is D.

Gideon called the altar he built 'The LORD is Peace' (Yahweh-Shalom) — after the LORD assured him he would not die, Gideon built an altar and called it 'The LORD Is Peace' (Judges 6:24). The correct answer is B.

When Nebuchadnezzar besieged Judah, he took away all classes of people but spared the poorest people of the land — he took the king, officials, craftsmen, and skilled workers, leaving only the poorest of the land (2 Kings 24:14). The correct answer is A.
After Ezekiel had eaten the scroll, he was sent to speak to the house of Israel — 'Son of man, go to the house of Israel and speak with my words to them' (Ezekiel 3:4). The correct answer is B.

God had pity on Nineveh because they turned from their evil way — 'When God saw what they did, how they turned from their evil way, God relented of the disaster' (Jonah 3:10). The correct answer is C.

The kingdom of Israel was divided because the last two kings made unwise policies — Rehoboam's harsh policy after Solomon's heavy-handed reign led to the split (1 Kings 12:1-16). The correct answer is D.
After 'Son of man, stand upon your feet' and the Spirit entered him — 'And as he spoke to me, the Spirit entered into me and set me on my feet' (Ezekiel 2:2). The correct answer is A.

Amos told Israel to hate evil, love good and establish justice in the gate so that God would be gracious to them — 'perhaps the LORD, the God of hosts, will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph' (Amos 5:15). The correct answer is C.

In addition to declaring freedom to the exiles, King Cyrus ordered a free will offering for the house of God in Jerusalem — he also returned the temple vessels and decreed that people should provide silver, gold, and supplies (Ezra 1:4-7). The correct answer is A.

In Timothy, Paul urges Christians to pray for kings and those in authority for a quiet and peaceable life — 'that we may lead a peaceful and quiet life, godly and dignified in every way' (1 Timothy 2:2). The correct answer is D.

Hosea named his second child 'Not Pitied' (Lo-ruhamah) because God would no more pity the house of Israel — 'for I will no more have pity on the house of Israel, to forgive them at all' (Hosea 1:6). The correct answer is D.

'If I tell you, you will not believe; and if I ask you, you will not answer' — Jesus said this in response to a request by the chief priests and scribes who asked about His authority (Luke 22:67-68). The correct answer is B.
The parable of the sower can be categorized under parables about the kingdom — it describes how people receive the word of the kingdom and its growth (Matthew 13:1-23). The correct answer is C.

When Jesus had the conversation with the Samaritan woman, the disciples had gone to the city to buy food — 'For his disciples had gone away into the city to buy food' (John 4:8). The correct answer is B.
According to Luke, the Last Supper took place in Jerusalem — Jesus sent Peter and John to prepare the Passover in Jerusalem, in the upper room (Luke 22:10-13). The correct answer is B.

'Not even in Israel have I found such faith' was said when Jesus healed the centurion's servant — the centurion's faith that Jesus need only speak the word amazed Jesus (Luke 7:9; Matthew 8:10). The correct answer is D.
'Teacher, do you not care if we perish?' — Jesus was in the stern, asleep, when a great windstorm arose on the sea and the disciples woke Him with this question (Mark 4:38). The correct answer is D.
Saul's mission to Damascus was to persecute the Christians — he obtained letters from the high priest to arrest Christians in Damascus (Acts 9:1-2). The correct answer is B.
In the Transfiguration, Moses and Elijah represented the Law and the Prophets — Moses represents the Law and Elijah represents the Prophets (Matthew 17:3). The correct answer is A.
According to John, the word Rabboni in Hebrew means Teacher — 'She turned and said to him in Aramaic, Rabboni! (which means Teacher)' (John 20:16). The correct answer is C.
'And in the last days it shall be God declares, that I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh' — Peter quoted this from Joel's prophecy (Acts 2:16-17; Joel 2:28). The correct answer is B.

Jesus was at the wedding in Cana because He was invited to the ceremony — 'On the third day there was a wedding at Cana in Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there. Jesus also was invited' (John 2:1-2). The correct answer is B.

'Seek out for me a woman who is a medium that I may go to her and inquire of her' — Saul made this statement when he was confronted by the Philistines, before the battle of Gilboa (1 Samuel 28:7). The correct answer is A.

In the mission of the seventy, Jesus said they were sent as sheep among wolves to indicate they would encounter difficulties — He warned them to be wise and alert amid dangers and opposition (Luke 10:3). The correct answer is D.

'I will go out as at other times, and shake myself free' — Samson was not aware that the LORD had left him — his strength was gone when Delilah had his head shaved (Judges 16:20). The correct answer is C.

God accepted David who killed Uriah but rejected Saul who spared Agag because David humbled himself when he realized his sin but Saul was stubborn — David repented genuinely (Psalm 51), while Saul made excuses and blamed others (1 Samuel 15:20-24; 2 Samuel 12:13). The correct answer is A.
The Hebrew midwives did not kill the Hebrew sons because of their fear of God — 'the midwives feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt commanded them' (Exodus 1:17). The correct answer is C.

When the Israelites left Egypt, God did not lead them by the shorter Philistine route because they might go back if they faced war — 'Lest the people change their minds when they see war and return to Egypt' (Exodus 13:17). The correct answer is B.
To confirm the covenant, Moses sent young men who offered burnt offerings and peace offerings of oxen to the LORD (Exodus 24:5). The correct answer is A.

An unwise decision of Solomon was the issue of forced labour — he imposed heavy forced labour on the people, which eventually led to the kingdom's division (1 Kings 12:4, 11). The correct answer is D.
'I will turn aside and see this great sight' — the great sight was the burning bush that was not burnt — 'the bush was burning, yet it was not consumed' (Exodus 3:2-3). The correct answer is A.

Asa did what was right in the eyes of the LORD by removing all the idols of his father — 'he put away the male cult prostitutes out of the land and removed all the idols that his fathers had made' (1 Kings 15:12). The correct answer is A.

God blessed the seventh day and made it holy because He rested on that day from all His work — 'So God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on it God rested from all his work' (Genesis 2:3). The correct answer is A.

According to Paul, the church that entered into partnership with him in giving and receiving at the beginning of his ministry was the Philippian church — 'you Philippians yourselves know that in the beginning of the gospel...no church entered into partnership with me in giving and receiving except you only' (Philippians 4:15). The correct answer is B.

According to Romans, the new life is comparable to Jesus' resurrection — 'just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, we too might walk in newness of life' (Romans 6:4). The correct answer is A.

According to Romans, when man confesses with his lips, he is saved — 'if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved' (Romans 10:9). The correct answer is A.

In Romans, believers are taught to obey those in authority because rulers are representatives of God — 'for he is God's servant for your good...he is the servant of God' (Romans 13:4, 6). The correct answer is C.

According to Luke, the Transfiguration of Jesus took place on the mountain while He was praying — 'as he was praying, the appearance of his face was altered, and his clothing became dazzling white' (Luke 9:29). The correct answer is D.
Prophet Isaiah received his vision and call when King Uzziah died — 'In the year that King Uzziah died I saw the Lord' (Isaiah 6:1). The correct answer is B.

The royal law in the scripture according to James is loving one's neighbour as oneself — 'If you really fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, You shall love your neighbor as yourself, you are doing well' (James 2:8). The correct answer is A.
In the covenant with Noah, God equates blood with life — 'But you shall not eat flesh with its life, that is, its blood' — blood represents the life principle (Genesis 9:4). The correct answer is B.

The covenant of Abraham stipulates that an uncircumcised male shall be cut off from his people — 'Any uncircumcised male...shall be cut off from his people; he has broken my covenant' (Genesis 17:14). The correct answer is D.
'Let us make man in our own image' — 'man' refers to male and female — 'God created man in his own image...male and female he created them' (Genesis 1:27). The correct answer is D.
In the burning bush, God revealed Himself to Moses as the God of deliverance — He said 'I have come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians' (Exodus 3:8). The correct answer is C.
Joseph was hated more because of his dreams — he dreamed that his brothers would bow down to him, and when he told them his dreams, they hated him even more (Genesis 37:5-8). The correct answer is C.
Eli's attitude to his children showed parental weakness — he knew about their sins and rebuked them, but failed to restrain them, showing weakness (1 Samuel 2:22-25; 3:13). The correct answer is C.

Samuel's reaction during his first encounter with God showed that he was inexperienced in dealing with God — he kept running to Eli, not recognizing the voice of the LORD, because 'Samuel did not yet know the LORD' (1 Samuel 3:7). The correct answer is A.

God did not lead the Hebrews by the way of the Philistines because He did not want them to see war and return to Egypt — 'lest the people change their minds when they see war and return to Egypt' (Exodus 13:17). The correct answer is B.

'The LORD has set the sun in the heavens, but he has said that he will dwell in thick darkness' was made in the context of the dedication of Solomon's temple — Solomon said this at the temple dedication when the glory cloud filled the temple (1 Kings 8:12). The correct answer is B.
When David repented of his adultery with Bathsheba, he said 'I have sinned against the LORD' — this was his immediate confession when confronted by Nathan (2 Samuel 12:13). The correct answer is B.

David demonstrated his submission to the will of God when he prevented the killing of Saul — he refused to harm God's anointed, saying 'The LORD forbid that I should...put out my hand against him' (1 Samuel 24:6; 26:11). The correct answer is B.

'Come let us return to the LORD; for he has torn, that he may heal us' — this call is to encourage response to God's love — Hosea's invitation to repentance shows God's loving call to restoration (Hosea 6:1). The correct answer is A.

The valley of Achor in Hosea is a door of hope — 'And I will...make the valley of Achor a door of hope' — God promised to transform the place of trouble into a place of hope (Hosea 2:15). The correct answer is B.

In the first three chapters of Hosea, his main teaching is that God loves us despite our sins — through Hosea's painful marriage experience, God showed His persistent love for unfaithful Israel (Hosea 1-3). The correct answer is B.
Jesus was baptized by John to fulfill all righteousness — 'Let it be so now, for thus it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness' (Matthew 3:15). The correct answer is C.

God gave Ezekiel a scroll to eat in his vision — 'And he said to me, Son of man, eat whatever you find here. Eat this scroll and go, speak to the house of Israel' (Ezekiel 3:1). The correct answer is A.

With reference to Isaiah's vision, a minister of God must possess holiness — Isaiah's reaction 'Woe is me! For I am...a man of unclean lips' and his cleansing by the seraph's coal shows holiness is essential for God's servant (Isaiah 6:5-7). The correct answer is D.
Jesus overcame Satan in the temptations because He depended on the word of God — He responded to each temptation with Scripture: 'It is written...' (Matthew 4:4, 7, 10). The correct answer is A.
Jesus overcame Satan in the temptations because He depended on the word of God — He quoted Scripture in response to each temptation (Matthew 4:4, 7, 10). The correct answer is A.

'Thou art my beloved Son; with thee I am well pleased' was made during the baptism of Jesus — the voice from heaven spoke as the Holy Spirit descended on Jesus after His baptism (Mark 1:11; Luke 3:22). The correct answer is D.

'Follow me and leave the dead to bury their own dead' means that following Jesus comes before anything else — Jesus demands total and immediate commitment; following Him has priority over even family obligations (Luke 9:60). The correct answer is C.

The disciples became terrified when they saw Jesus walking on the sea because they thought He was a ghost — 'they all saw him and were terrified' crying 'It is a ghost!' (Mark 6:49-50; Matthew 14:26). The correct answer is B.

The Jews sought to kill Jesus after healing the man at Bethzatha because they thought He made Himself equal with God — He said 'My Father is working until now, and I am working,' making God His own Father (John 5:17-18). The correct answer is B.

By raising Lazarus, Jesus wanted to convince the people that He was the Lord of life — 'I am the resurrection and the life; he who believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live' (John 11:25-26). The correct answer is C.

In Matthew's account, the disciples could not heal the epileptic boy because they had little faith — Jesus told them 'Because of your little faith. For truly, I say to you, if you have faith like a grain of mustard seed...' (Matthew 17:20). The correct answer is A.
Jesus charged the twelve to give without pay because they had freely received — 'You received without paying; give without pay' (Matthew 10:8). The correct answer is D.

The parable of the lost sheep teaches much about God's love — the shepherd's diligent search for the one lost sheep and his great joy when it is found represent God's love for every single person (Luke 15:3-7). The correct answer is B.

In the parable of the sower, seed on rocky ground refers to people whose conversion is superficial — they receive the word with joy but have no root; in time of testing they fall away (Luke 8:13). The correct answer is C.

Jesus did not appeal to angels to fight because He wanted the scriptures to be fulfilled — 'But how then should the Scriptures be fulfilled, that it must be so?' (Matthew 26:54). The correct answer is C.
The disciples with Jesus during the Transfiguration were Peter, James and John (Matthew 17:1; Mark 9:2; Luke 9:28). The correct answer is A.

The multitude rejoiced during Jesus' triumphal entry because of the mighty works they had seen done by Jesus — 'praising God with a loud voice for all the mighty works that they had seen' (Luke 19:37). The correct answer is B.

The words 'My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me' led a bystander to give Jesus vinegar — bystanders misheard 'Eli, Eli' as a call for Elijah and offered vinegar to see if Elijah would come (Matthew 27:46-48). The correct answer is C.
By sending Jesus to Herod, Pilate achieved the result that Herod and Pilate became friends — 'And Herod and Pilate became friends with each other that very day' (Luke 23:12). The correct answer is C.

Jesus wept over Jerusalem because the city did not know the things that made for peace — 'Would that you, even you, had known on this day the things that make for peace!' (Luke 19:42). The correct answer is B.
