The event of the day of Pentecost was prophesied by Joel — Peter quoted Joel 2:28-32 to explain the outpouring of the Holy Spirit (Acts 2:16-21). The correct answer is B.
A co-witness of the resurrection was elected to replace Judas — 'one of these men must become with us a witness to his resurrection' (Acts 1:22). The correct answer is B.

When Jesus said Lazarus would rise again, Martha thought her brother would rise again at the last day — 'Martha said to him, I know that he will rise again in the resurrection on the last day' (John 11:24). The correct answer is B.

The Christian concept of justification is that through faith in Jesus, the sinner is now regarded by God as guiltless — justification means being declared righteous by God through faith in Christ (Romans 5:1; Galatians 2:16). The correct answer is A.
The second martyr of the early church was James the brother of John — after Stephen, King Herod killed James the brother of John with the sword (Acts 12:2). The correct answer is A.

Those who rely on works of the law are under a curse because none can fully keep the law — 'For all who rely on works of the law are under a curse; for it is written, Cursed be everyone who does not abide by all things written in the Book of the Law' (Galatians 3:10). The correct answer is C.

Sin reigned in death, while grace reigned through righteousness to eternal life — 'so that, as sin reigned in death, grace also might reign through righteousness leading to eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord' (Romans 5:21). The correct answer is B.

Christians ought to be humble because Jesus Christ demonstrated it — 'Have this mind among yourselves, which is yours in Christ Jesus, who...humbled himself' (Philippians 2:5-8). The correct answer is B.

Christians are children of God because through faith, they were baptized into Christ and put on Christ — 'for in Christ Jesus you are all sons of God, through faith. For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ' (Galatians 3:26-27). The correct answer is D.

The order at the second coming will be that the dead will rise first before the living are caught up — 'the dead in Christ will rise first. Then we who are alive...will be caught up together with them' (1 Thessalonians 4:16-17). The correct answer is B.
Paul advised Thessalonians to keep away from any brother who is living in idleness — 'keep away from any brother who is walking in idleness' (2 Thessalonians 3:6). The correct answer is C.

According to Paul, spiritual gifts, if properly employed, help in edifying the church — 'Since you are eager for manifestations of the Spirit, strive to excel in building up the church' (1 Corinthians 14:12). The correct answer is D.

In extolling God's sovereignty, Amos contrasted Him with the Nile, which he described as rising and sinking — 'who makes the stars...who makes darkness...who calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out upon the surface of the earth' referring to the Nile's pattern (Amos 5:8; 9:5-6). The correct answer is A.
'You shall love your neighbour as yourself' is described by James as the royal law (James 2:8). The correct answer is C.
By keeping God's covenant, the people of Israel would become a kingdom of priests of God — 'you shall be to me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation' (Exodus 19:6). The correct answer is D.

Joseph saw his rise to leadership as a means of preserving the lives of his brothers — 'God sent me before you to preserve life...to preserve for you a remnant on earth' (Genesis 45:5-7). The correct answer is D.

The name Ichabod means 'departed glory' — Phinehas' wife named the child Ichabod saying 'The glory has departed from Israel' because the Ark of God was captured (1 Samuel 4:21-22). The correct answer is D.

'If you will go with me, I will go; but if you will not go with me, I will not go' — 'you' refers to Deborah — Barak told Deborah he would only go to battle if she went with him (Judges 4:8). The correct answer is C.

David perceived his child by Bathsheba was dead because he saw his servants whispering together — 'David saw that his servants were whispering together, and David understood that the child was dead' (2 Samuel 12:19). The correct answer is B.

The mother of the living child asked Solomon to give the child to the other woman because her heart yearned for the child — 'her heart yearned for her son, and she said...give her the living child, and by no means kill him!' (1 Kings 3:26). The correct answer is B.

Hosea's matrimonial experience symbolizes God's intention to redeem Israel from her unfaithfulness — Hosea took back his unfaithful wife as God would take back Israel; the love story shows God's redemptive love (Hosea 3:1-5). The correct answer is D.

'As one falls before the wicked you have fallen' is part of David's lamentation over Abner — David lamented at Abner's funeral, grieving that a great man had been killed treacherously (2 Samuel 3:33-34). The correct answer is C.
The harlotry of Gomer is compared to Israel's unfaithfulness to God — Gomer's adultery symbolizes Israel's spiritual adultery by going after other gods (Hosea 1:2; 4:12). The correct answer is D.

'Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory' was said in the year Uzziah of Judah died — Isaiah heard the seraphim singing this during his vision in the year King Uzziah died (Isaiah 6:1-3). The correct answer is C.

'Hear the word of the LORD, you rulers of Sodom! Give ear to the teaching of our God, you people of Gomorrah!' — the nation referred to as Sodom and Gomorrah is Israel (Judah) — Isaiah addressed the sinful people of Israel with this shocking comparison (Isaiah 1:10). The correct answer is A.

The devil's principal purpose for tempting Jesus was to lure Jesus from His mission — Satan tried to divert Jesus from the path of obedient suffering to a shortcut that bypassed the cross (Matthew 4:1-11). The correct answer is C.
Jeremiah was not anxious to accept God's call because he was too young and inexperienced — 'I do not know how to speak, for I am only a youth' (Jeremiah 1:6). The correct answer is D.

'Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests; but the Son of man has nowhere to lay his head' implies that discipleship costs much — Jesus warned the would-be disciple that following Him involves sacrifice and homelessness (Luke 9:58). The correct answer is A.
In Jesus' healing ministry, faith played a very vital role — He repeatedly said 'Your faith has made you well' and marveled at great faith (Matthew 9:22; Mark 5:34). The correct answer is A.
According to Luke, following Jesus involves self-denial — 'If anyone would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me' (Luke 9:23). The correct answer is B.

Jesus healed the only son of the widow of Nain because He had compassion on her — 'And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her and said to her, Do not weep' (Luke 7:13). The correct answer is C.

The healing of the paralytic brought by four friends demonstrates that the friends had faith in the healing power of Jesus — 'And when Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, Son, your sins are forgiven' (Mark 2:5). The correct answer is B.

According to Mark and Luke, the response of blind Bartimaeus to his healing was to follow Jesus immediately — 'And immediately he recovered his sight and followed him' (Mark 10:52; Luke 18:43). The correct answer is A.

The parable which teaches about God's judgement is that of the weeds (tares) — at the end of the age, the angels will separate the righteous from the wicked (Matthew 13:40-43). The correct answer is C.

The parable of the Good Samaritan implies that neighbourliness is expressed in love and concern — true neighbourliness means showing practical love and mercy to anyone in need, regardless of background (Luke 10:36-37). The correct answer is C.

Jesus' teaching on adultery, prayer, alms and fasting shows these are more matters of the heart — He emphasized inward motivation and sincerity rather than outward show (Matthew 5:28; 6:1-6). The correct answer is A.

Luke ends the Sermon on the Plain with an analogy of a building to emphasize the importance of hearing and obeying the word — building on a solid foundation represents hearing and doing what Jesus says (Luke 6:47-49). The correct answer is B.

Jesus' injunction not to lay up treasures on earth implies the Christian should be rich in good works — investing in heavenly treasure means using earthly resources for godly purposes and good deeds (Matthew 6:19-20; 1 Timothy 6:18-19). The correct answer is D.

The seventy disciples were told to rejoice because their names were written in heaven — 'do not rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven' (Luke 10:20). The correct answer is C.
When Pilate asked 'Are you the king of the Jews?' Jesus replied 'You have said so' (Matthew 27:11; Luke 23:3). The correct answer is A.

According to Matthew, when the women went to the sepulchre, they saw an angel sitting upon the stone — 'And behold, there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord descended from heaven and came and rolled back the stone and sat on it' (Matthew 28:2). The correct answer is A.

The prayer of Jesus before His arrest showed that He was sorrowful and troubled — 'And he took with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, and began to be sorrowful and troubled' (Matthew 26:37). The correct answer is A.

Jesus used the illustration of the vine to teach that a Christian who abides in Him will bear much fruit — 'Whoever abides in me and I in him, he it is that bears much fruit' (John 15:5). The correct answer is D.

'Give me also this power, that anyone on whom I lay my hands may receive the Holy Spirit' — Peter rebuked Simon the sorcerer for being money conscious (treating spiritual gifts as something to be bought with money) — 'But Peter said to him, May your silver perish with you, because you thought you could obtain the gift of God with money!' (Acts 8:20). The correct answer is B (money conscious).
Parmenas and Timon were two of the seven disciples chosen to serve tables — the seven were Stephen, Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolaus (Acts 6:5). The correct answer is A.

The condition for justification according to Paul is faith in Christ crucified — 'we know that a person is not justified by works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ' (Galatians 2:16; Romans 3:28). The correct answer is D.
At the Beautiful Gate, Peter and John healed a man who was lame — he had been lame from birth and was laid at the gate daily to beg (Acts 3:1-8). The correct answer is A.
The pillars of the Jerusalem church who gave Paul and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship were James, Cephas (Peter), and John (Galatians 2:9). The correct answer is D.

God sent His Son in the likeness of sinful flesh so that the law might be fulfilled — 'God has done what the law...could not do...in order that the righteous requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us' (Romans 8:3-4). The correct answer is B.
The greatest spiritual gift to seek is love — 'And I will show you a still more excellent way' — Paul places love above all spiritual gifts (1 Corinthians 12:31; 13:1-3). The correct answer is B.

'At the name of Jesus every knee should bow...every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord' demonstrates the Lordship of Jesus over all creation — the universal acknowledgment extends to all beings in heaven, earth, and under the earth (Philippians 2:10-11). The correct answer is B.

One civic responsibility Christians are commanded to carry out is obedience to lawful authority — 'Let every person be subject to the governing authorities' (Romans 13:1; 1 Peter 2:13). The correct answer is C.

Paul worked night and day so that he might not be a burden to anyone — 'we worked night and day, that we might not be a burden to any of you' (1 Thessalonians 2:9; 2 Thessalonians 3:8). The correct answer is A.

Those who have fallen asleep before the coming of the Lord are those who are dead physically — Paul uses 'fallen asleep' as a euphemism for physical death (1 Thessalonians 4:13-14). The correct answer is B.

James enjoins Christians to remain impartial by showing love to all without distinction — the sin of partiality contradicts the royal law of love; all people must be treated equally (James 2:1-9). The correct answer is A.
Peter admonishes that suffering for Christ's sake brings God's blessing — 'But even if you should suffer for righteousness' sake, you will be blessed' (1 Peter 3:14). The correct answer is B.

According to James, the man who prays and doubts is double-minded — 'for he who doubts is like a wave of the sea...he is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways' (James 1:6-8). The correct answer is C.

God made two great lights to rule the day and the night — 'God made the two great lights — the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night' (Genesis 1:16). The correct answer is B.

'Is it because there are no graves in Egypt that you have taken us away to die in the wilderness?' was asked when the Egyptians marched after them — the Israelites said this at the Red Sea when they saw Pharaoh's army coming (Exodus 14:11). The correct answer is D.

God promised to send bread from heaven so He could see if the Israelites would walk in His law — 'I am about to rain bread from heaven for you, and the people shall go out and gather a day's portion every day, that I may test them, whether they will walk in my law or not' (Exodus 16:4). The correct answer is A.
David spared Saul's life at Ziph because Saul was anointed by God — 'The LORD forbid that I should put out my hand against the LORD's anointed' (1 Samuel 26:11). The correct answer is A.

Nathan told David that although God put away his sin, David would still be bereaved of the child — 'The LORD also has put away your sin; you shall not die. Nevertheless...the child who is born to you shall die' (2 Samuel 12:13-14). The correct answer is B.

'Behold, I am about to do a thing in Israel, at which both ears of everyone who hears it will tingle' were the words of God to Samuel the prophet — God revealed to the young Samuel the punishment to fall on Eli's house (1 Samuel 3:11). The correct answer is B.

The ark of the covenant brought before Solomon contained two tablets of stone — 'There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets of stone that Moses put there at Horeb' (1 Kings 8:9). The correct answer is D.

Jeremiah was consecrated and appointed a prophet before he was born — 'Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations' (Jeremiah 1:5). The correct answer is C.

Hosea accused Israel of harlotry because the people worshipped other gods — religious unfaithfulness, going after other gods, is the central meaning of the harlotry metaphor in Hosea (Hosea 1:2; 4:12). The correct answer is C.
Satan promised Jesus all the kingdoms of the world if He would bow down and worship him — 'All these I will give you, if you will fall down and worship me' (Matthew 4:9). The correct answer is C.
'Son of man, stand upon your feet, and I will speak with you' was made during the call of Ezekiel — God addressed Ezekiel this way when He called him (Ezekiel 2:1). The correct answer is D.

Jesus had compassion for the five thousand because they were like sheep without a shepherd — 'he saw a great crowd, and he had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd' (Mark 6:34; Matthew 9:36). The correct answer is B.

According to Matthew, the first two disciples to be called by Jesus were Peter and Andrew — Jesus saw Simon (Peter) and Andrew casting a net and said 'Follow me' (Matthew 4:18-20). The correct answer is A.

When Jesus heard of Lazarus' illness, He said it was so that the Son of God may be glorified — 'This illness does not lead to death. It is for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it' (John 11:4). The correct answer is B.

Jesus' teaching on swearing is that Christians should not swear at all — 'But I say to you, Do not take an oath at all...Let what you say be simply Yes or No' (Matthew 5:34, 37). The correct answer is C.
At the country of the Gerasenes, Jesus healed the man who had demons — the Gerasene demoniac was possessed by a legion of demons (Mark 5:1-15; Luke 8:26-35). The correct answer is D.

The parable of the wheat and tares illustrates that both good and evil live in the world — the field is the world; wheat (children of the kingdom) and weeds (children of the evil one) grow together until the harvest (Matthew 13:38-40). The correct answer is B.

'The harvest is plentiful, but the labourers are few' was said during the commissioning of the seventy others — Jesus said this just before He sent out the seventy-two disciples (Luke 10:2). The correct answer is A.
'Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God' (Matthew 5:8). The correct answer is B.

The description peculiar to Luke's account of the triumphal entry is that the disciples set Jesus on the animal — 'And they...set Jesus on it' (Luke 19:35), a detail specific to Luke. The correct answer is D.

According to Matthew, when Christ was arrested He was led to Caiaphas — 'those who had seized Jesus led him to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders had gathered' (Matthew 26:57). The correct answer is A.

The criteria for choosing the seven deacons were good repute and being full of the Spirit — 'pick out from among you seven men of good repute, full of the Spirit and of wisdom' (Acts 6:3). The correct answer is B.
The two men referred to were Justus and Matthias — 'they put forward two, Joseph called Barsabbas, who was also called Justus, and Matthias' (Acts 1:23). The correct answer is A.

In John's account of the resurrection, Mary was first asked why she was weeping by two angels — 'And she saw two angels in white...They said to her, Woman, why are you weeping?' (John 20:12-13). The correct answer is B.
The Jerusalem Council resolved that Gentiles should abstain from food offered to idols, what is strangled, blood, and unchastity (Acts 15:29). The correct answer is C.
At Pentecost, Peter explained that God promised to pour out His Spirit on all flesh — 'I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh' (Acts 2:17; Joel 2:28). The correct answer is D.

The consequence of setting one's mind on the things of the flesh is death — 'For to set the mind on the flesh is death, but to set the mind on the Spirit is life and peace' (Romans 8:6). The correct answer is C.

Peter and John were arrested because they were preaching the gospel of Jesus — the captain of the temple and Sadducees were annoyed because they were 'proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection from the dead' (Acts 4:2-3). The correct answer is D.

Custodian here means the law — 'But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a guardian/custodian' referring to the Mosaic Law that served as guardian until Christ came (Galatians 3:25). The correct answer is B.

Paul admonished Romans to live a new life by yielding themselves to God as men who have been brought from death to life — 'present yourselves to God as those who have been brought from death to life' (Romans 6:13). The correct answer is A.

God exalted Christ because He was obedient and humble — 'he humbled himself by becoming obedient to the point of death...Therefore God has highly exalted him' (Philippians 2:8-9). The correct answer is C.

Paul considered the Philippians' gifts a fragrant offering and a sacrifice acceptable to God — 'a fragrant offering, a sacrifice acceptable and pleasing to God' (Philippians 4:18). The correct answer is D.
Spiritual gifts according to Paul should be used for the edification of the church — 'strive to excel in building up the church' (1 Corinthians 14:12; Ephesians 4:12). The correct answer is B.

'For rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to bad' — Christians who do good will receive the ruler's approval — 'do what is good and you will receive his approval' (Romans 13:3). The correct answer is A.

The second coming of Christ according to Paul will be preceded by the coming of the man of lawlessness — 'the man of lawlessness is revealed, the son of destruction' must come first (2 Thessalonians 2:3). The correct answer is C.

'Keep away from any brother who is living in idleness' was made to teach the dignity of labour — Paul insisted on working to support oneself and not being a burden (2 Thessalonians 3:10-12). The correct answer is C.

The wisdom of God is necessary for salvation, so James teaches Christians should ask in faith to get it — 'If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God...But let him ask in faith, with no doubting' (James 1:5-6). The correct answer is C.

'Is it not the rich who oppress you, is it not they who drag you into court?' — James asked this in his teaching on impartiality — the rich were dragging poor Christians into court (James 2:6). The correct answer is B.

According to Peter, when the chief shepherd is manifested, Christians will obtain the unfading crown of glory — 'And when the chief Shepherd appears, you will receive the unfading crown of glory' (1 Peter 5:4). The correct answer is D.

When Joseph narrated his second dream, Jacob rebuked him because the dream would subject his parents to his authority — the dream implied that even Jacob and his wife would bow down to Joseph (Genesis 37:10). The correct answer is B.

The LORD appeared to Abraham and promised the land at the Oak of Moreh — 'Abram passed through the land to the place at Shechem, to the oak of Moreh...Then the LORD appeared to Abram and said, To your offspring I will give this land' (Genesis 12:6-7). The correct answer is A.
'Behold, I have given you every plant yielding seed...and every tree with seed in its fruit' — God made all provision for man to have enough food (Genesis 1:29). The correct answer is B.

God told Noah 'Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man shall his blood be shed' because man is made in God's image — the sanctity of human life is grounded in the image of God (Genesis 9:6). The correct answer is A.

The division of David's kingdom was a direct consequence of Rehoboam's unwise decision — he rejected the elders' counsel and followed the harsh advice of young men, causing the ten tribes to rebel (1 Kings 12:14-16). The correct answer is D.

Abner sent messengers to David at Hebron because he wanted to bring over all Israel to David — Abner wanted to make a covenant with David to transfer the whole kingdom of Israel to him (2 Samuel 3:12). The correct answer is A.
The LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream at Gibeon — 'At Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream by night' (1 Kings 3:5). The correct answer is B.
The final consequence of Saul's disobedience was his death in the war front — Saul was fatally wounded by Philistine archers at the battle of Mount Gilboa (1 Samuel 31:3-4). The correct answer is D.

The reforms of King Josiah were made possible by the discovery of the book of the law — Hilkiah found the book during temple repairs; this prompted Josiah's sweeping religious reform (2 Kings 22:8-13). The correct answer is A.

God forgave David when David accepted his guilt — 'David said to Nathan, I have sinned against the LORD. And Nathan said to David, The LORD also has put away your sin' (2 Samuel 12:13). The correct answer is B.

God rejected the sons of Eli from priesthood because they were avaricious (greedy) and blasphemous (treating holy things with contempt/unrestrained) — they took meat by force and slept with the serving women at the tent of meeting (1 Samuel 2:17, 22-25). The correct answer is A.
Amos told Israel they have turned justice into wormwood — 'you who turn justice to wormwood and cast down righteousness to the earth!' (Amos 5:7). The correct answer is C.

Elijah's prayer brought down fire from heaven which consumed the burnt offering — 'Then the fire of the LORD fell and consumed the burnt offering and the wood and the stones and the dust' (1 Kings 18:38). The correct answer is D.

Naaman's leprosy was transferred to Gehazi as a punishment for the gifts he received from Naaman — Gehazi secretly received silver and garments from Naaman and Elisha pronounced leprosy on him (2 Kings 5:27). The correct answer is B.

'Even though you make many prayers, I will not listen' — God would not listen because their hands were full of blood — their prayers were hypocritical while they practiced injustice and violence (Isaiah 1:15). The correct answer is C.

As Nehemiah embarked on reconstruction of Jerusalem, he faced opposition from Sanballat and Tobiah — these two men along with Geshem the Arab opposed and mocked Nehemiah's work (Nehemiah 2:10, 19; 4:1-3). The correct answer is D.
Hosea compared Judah's love to the morning cloud because it goes away early like the dew — 'Your love is like a morning cloud, like the dew that goes early away' (Hosea 6:4). The correct answer is A.

The attribute of God which Isaiah emphasized most is His holiness — the seraphim cry 'Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts' and Isaiah's vision centered on God's transcendent holiness (Isaiah 6:3). The correct answer is B.

The parable of the lost sheep portrays the shepherd as loving — he leaves the ninety-nine to search for the one lost sheep and rejoices greatly when he finds it, demonstrating God's great love for the lost (Luke 15:4-6). The correct answer is D.

'To you it has been given to know the secrets of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given' was said after Jesus had told the parable of the sower — the disciples asked why He spoke in parables and Jesus gave this answer (Matthew 13:11). The correct answer is B.

Jesus commissioned the twelve to go to the lost sheep of the house of Israel — 'Go nowhere among the Gentiles and enter no town of the Samaritans, but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel' (Matthew 10:5-6). The correct answer is B.
In the feeding of the five thousand, the first thing Jesus did was to order the loaves and fish brought to Him — 'Bring them here to me' (Matthew 14:18). The correct answer is A.

When the man with an unclean spirit in the Gerasenes saw Jesus, he acknowledged Him as the Son of the Most High God — 'What have you to do with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God?' (Mark 5:7; Luke 8:28). The correct answer is A.

'Do not lay up for yourselves treasures on earth' shows that Jesus wants Christians to seek first the kingdom of God — He taught 'But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you' (Matthew 6:19, 33). The correct answer is C.

The six stone jars of water Jesus turned into wine were kept there for the Jewish rites of purification — 'Now there were six stone water jars there for the Jewish rites of purification' (John 2:6). The correct answer is C.

When Peter saw the great shoal of fish, he confessed being a sinner — 'But when Simon Peter saw it, he fell down at Jesus' knees, saying, Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, O Lord' (Luke 5:8). The correct answer is C.

'He was numbered among us, and was allotted his share in this ministry' — what happened to Judas Iscariot was that he committed suicide — 'going to his own place' after buying a field with the thirty pieces of silver (Acts 1:17-25). The correct answer is B.

According to John, the distinctive quality of disciples of Jesus is showing love to one another — 'By this all people will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another' (John 13:35). The correct answer is D.

The major issues that led Paul and Barnabas before the Council were circumcision and the Law of Moses — 'certain people...said, Unless you are circumcised...you cannot be saved' and others said they must keep the law of Moses (Acts 15:1, 5). The correct answer is C.
Thomas asked Jesus 'Lord, we do not know where you are going; how can we know the way?' — Jesus replied 'I am the way, and the truth, and the life' (John 14:5-6). The correct answer is C.
According to Mark, after Jesus triumphantly entered Jerusalem, He went first into the temple — 'And he entered Jerusalem and went into the temple' (Mark 11:11). The correct answer is A.

Speaking in tongues is meaningful where there is one with the gift of interpretation — 'if there is no one to interpret, let each of them keep silent in church' (1 Corinthians 14:28). The correct answer is A.

Paul advises Christians to obey authorities because they have divine mandate — 'for there is no authority except from God, and those that exist have been instituted by God' (Romans 13:1). The correct answer is C.
The sound from heaven on Pentecost was likened to that of a mighty wind — 'suddenly there came from heaven a sound like a mighty rushing wind' (Acts 2:2). The correct answer is A.

God extended His promise to Abraham to all who share his faith based on the grace of God — 'the promise...depends on faith, in order that it may rest on grace and be guaranteed to all his offspring' (Romans 4:16). The correct answer is C.
Paul says that anyone who does acts of mercy should do so with cheerfulness — 'the one who does acts of mercy, with cheerfulness' (Romans 12:8). The correct answer is D.
According to Galatians, faith in Christ Jesus makes all believers sons of God — 'in Christ Jesus you are all sons of God, through faith' (Galatians 3:26). The correct answer is B.

Paul's statement about the living being caught up implied he believed he would live to witness the second coming of Christ — 'we who are alive, who are left' suggests Paul expected to be among the living at Christ's return (1 Thessalonians 4:17). The correct answer is A.

Peter says Christians put to silence foolish men by doing right — 'For this is the will of God, that by doing good you should put to silence the ignorance of foolish people' (1 Peter 2:15). The correct answer is C.

The second coming of Christ shall be recognized by a cry of command — 'the Lord himself will descend from heaven with a cry of command, with the voice of an archangel, and with the sound of the trumpet of God' (1 Thessalonians 4:16). The correct answer is B.

According to Peter, if a Christian suffers for his faith, he should not be ashamed — 'if anyone suffers as a Christian, let him not be ashamed, but let him glorify God in that name' (1 Peter 4:16). The correct answer is A.

According to James, whoever keeps the whole law but fails in one point has become guilty of all of it — 'For whoever keeps the whole law but fails in one point has become guilty of all of it' (James 2:10). The correct answer is C.
Nathan's statement 'You are the man' made David immediately confess and ask for forgiveness — 'David said to Nathan, I have sinned against the LORD' (2 Samuel 12:13). The correct answer is C.

The request 'lighten the hard service' was made to Rehoboam because the people wanted some relief — Solomon had imposed heavy forced labour on them and they sought lighter treatment (1 Kings 12:4). The correct answer is D.
'The LORD will fight for you, and you have only to be still' was said by Moses when the Egyptians were pursuing the Israelites before the Red Sea (Exodus 14:14). The correct answer is A.
In the beginning, God created the heavens and earth — 'In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth' (Genesis 1:1). The correct answer is A.
Joab killed Abner because he wanted to avenge the death of his brother Asahel — Abner had killed Asahel in battle, and Joab took personal revenge (2 Samuel 3:27, 30). The correct answer is A.

Abraham laughed when God said Sarah would have a child because his wife was too old — 'Shall a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old? Shall Sarah, who is ninety years old, bear a child?' (Genesis 17:17). The correct answer is C.

In the creation story, man was permitted to name all the creatures — 'Now out of the ground the LORD God had formed every beast...and brought them to the man to see what he would call them' (Genesis 2:19). The correct answer is D.

The LORD sent Samuel to tell Saul to destroy the Amalekites because they opposed Israel on their way out of Egypt — 'I will punish what Amalek did to Israel in opposing them on the way' (1 Samuel 15:2). The correct answer is A.

Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego's statement portrays them as men of faith — they declared their faith that God could deliver them, yet committed to not worshipping the idol regardless of outcome (Daniel 3:17-18). The correct answer is A.

Ezekiel described Israel as having a hard forehead and stubborn heart because the people refused to listen to him — 'the house of Israel are not willing to listen to you, for they are not willing to listen to me' (Ezekiel 3:7). The correct answer is B.

The plant God appointed over Jonah taught him that God is merciful — when the plant withered and Jonah was distressed, God used it to illustrate His compassion for Nineveh's many people (Jonah 4:10-11). The correct answer is D.

'Why is your spirit so vexed that you eat no food?' — the addressee was Ahab, who was sad because Naboth refused to give him his vineyard — Jezebel asked Ahab this question (1 Kings 21:5). The correct answer is A.

Isaiah teaches that the LORD wants His people to demonstrate holiness by doing justice and not evil — 'learn to do good; seek justice, correct oppression; bring justice to the fatherless, plead the widow's cause' (Isaiah 1:17). The correct answer is C.

The reaction of Naaman to Elisha's instruction showed he was proud — he was outraged that Elisha didn't come out personally and told him to wash in the Jordan, saying the rivers of Damascus were better (2 Kings 5:11-12). The correct answer is A.

The main lesson of Hosea's teaching is that God prefers steadfast love to sacrifice — 'For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings' (Hosea 6:6). The correct answer is D.

The man appointed by the Holy Spirit to go on the missionary journey with Saul was Barnabas — 'the Holy Spirit said, Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them' (Acts 13:2). The correct answer is B.

Daniel became distinguished above all presidents and satraps because he had an excellent spirit in him — 'Daniel became distinguished above all the other presidents and satraps, because an excellent spirit was in him' (Daniel 6:3). The correct answer is D.

When Elijah escaped to the brook Cherith, he was fed by ravens — 'And the ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening; and he drank from the brook' (1 Kings 17:6). The correct answer is D.

Peter, James and John were asked to keep the transfiguration secret until the Son of Man is raised from the dead — 'Tell no one the vision, until the Son of Man is raised from the dead' (Matthew 17:9). The correct answer is D.

The mark of a true disciple according to Jesus is loving one another — 'By this all people will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another' (John 13:35). The correct answer is A.
The main complaint of the Hellenists against the Hebrews was that their widows were being neglected in the daily distribution (Acts 6:1). The correct answer is B.

When Jesus entered the temple in Jerusalem, He drove out all who sold and bought — 'he drove out all who sold and bought in the temple, and he overturned the tables of the money-changers' (Matthew 21:12). The correct answer is D.

According to John, for a man to have eternal life he must believe in the only Son of God — 'For God so loved the world, that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life' (John 3:16). The correct answer is C.
In Jesus' teaching on the true vine, branch refers to man — Jesus said 'I am the vine; you are the branches' (John 15:5). The correct answer is A.

In the stilling of the storm, the disciples were surprised because the wind and the sea obeyed Jesus — 'And they were filled with great fear and said to one another, Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?' (Mark 4:41). The correct answer is C.

'Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?' — the lawyer who asked this wanted to put Christ to the test — 'And behold, a lawyer stood up to put him to the test' (Luke 10:25). The correct answer is A.
Jesus' reply to the devil's command to throw Himself from the pinnacle was 'You shall not tempt the Lord your God' (Matthew 4:7; Luke 4:12). The correct answer is B.

Before Jesus raised Jairus' daughter, the people mocked Him because He told them the girl was not dead but sleeping — they laughed at Him when He said this (Matthew 9:24; Mark 5:39-40). The correct answer is A.

'Have nothing to do with that righteous man, for I have suffered much over him today in a dream' — Pilate's wife said this during Jesus' trial — she sent this message to Pilate while he was seated on the judgment seat (Matthew 27:19). The correct answer is C.

When Bartimaeus wanted Jesus to heal him, he persistently cried out for help — he shouted 'Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!' and kept calling out even when people told him to be quiet (Mark 10:47-48). The correct answer is D.

The teachers of the law accused Jesus of blasphemy because He declared that He had authority to forgive sin — 'Why does this man speak like that? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins but God alone?' (Mark 2:7). The correct answer is B.

In the parable of the wheat and tares, the bad seed was sowed by the devil — 'The one who sowed the good seed is the Son of Man. The field is the world, and the good seed is the sons of the kingdom. The weeds are the sons of the evil one, and the enemy who sowed them is the devil' (Matthew 13:37-39). The correct answer is A.

According to Paul, generosity produces thanksgiving to God — 'For the ministry of this service is not only supplying the needs of the saints but is also overflowing in many thanksgivings to God' (2 Corinthians 9:12). The correct answer is B.

According to Jesus, believers who forgive others will be forgiven by God — 'For if you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you' (Matthew 6:14). The correct answer is B.

In James, 'they' who blaspheme the honourable name refers to the rich — 'Is it not the rich who oppress you...Is it not they who blaspheme the honorable name by which you were called?' (James 2:6-7). The correct answer is D.
According to Paul, he who loves his neighbour has fulfilled the law — 'The one who loves another has fulfilled the law...love is the fulfilling of the law' (Romans 13:8, 10). The correct answer is C.
According to James, the prayer of a righteous man has great power in its effects — 'The prayer of a righteous person has great power as it is working' (James 5:16). The correct answer is D.

As by one man's disobedience many were made sinners, by one man's obedience many will be made righteous — 'by the one man's obedience the many will be made righteous' (Romans 5:19). The correct answer is A.

'The day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night' — the day of the Lord refers to the day of Judgment — Peter uses this phrase for the end-time judgment (2 Peter 3:10; 1 Thessalonians 5:2). The correct answer is C.

Peter urges Christians to live as free men without using their freedom as a pretext for evil — 'Live as people who are free, not using your freedom as a cover-up for evil' (1 Peter 2:16). The correct answer is A.

The signs God showed Moses at his call were meant to convince the people that he had been sent by God — 'that they may believe that the LORD...has appeared to you' (Exodus 4:5). The correct answer is D.

'The LORD give you children by this woman' — Eli offered this prayer because of Hannah's loan of Samuel to the LORD — Hannah had dedicated Samuel to the LORD's service (1 Samuel 2:20). The correct answer is A.
After his defeat of the Amalekites, Saul set up a monument for himself — 'Saul came to Carmel, and behold, he set up a monument for himself' (1 Samuel 15:12). The correct answer is B.

King Rehoboam refused the counsel of the elders because it was a turn of affairs brought about by the LORD — 'So the king did not listen to the people, for it was a turn of affairs brought about by the LORD' (1 Kings 12:15). The correct answer is C.
'Is not David hiding himself on the hill of Hachilah?' was said to King Saul by the Ziphites — the Ziphites betrayed David's location to Saul (1 Samuel 26:1). The correct answer is C.

'Let us flee from before Israel; for the LORD fights for them' was said by the Egyptians when their chariots were clogged in the sea — 'And the Egyptians fled into it...the LORD clogged their chariot wheels' (Exodus 14:25). The correct answer is D.

Moses told the Israelites the LORD would give them fish and bread because He had heard their murmurings — 'The LORD has heard your grumbling...At twilight you shall eat meat, and in the morning you shall be filled with bread' (Exodus 16:12). The correct answer is C.

The sign of the covenant between God and Noah was a bow in the cloud — 'I have set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and the earth' (Genesis 9:13). The correct answer is B.

'When my soul fainted within me, I remembered the LORD, and my prayer came to thee' was offered by Jonah in the belly of the fish — Jonah prayed this prayer from inside the great fish (Jonah 2:7). The correct answer is C.
The new covenant God made with Israel and Judah was written on their hearts — 'I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts' (Jeremiah 31:33). The correct answer is D.
The river from Eden divided into four rivers: Gihon, Pishon, Tigris and Euphrates (Genesis 2:10-14). The correct answer is C.

The men who threw Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego into the furnace were consumed by the flames — 'the flame of the fire killed those men who took up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego' (Daniel 3:22). The correct answer is A.

According to Hosea, the LORD would not have pity on the children because their mother had played the harlot — 'She conceived them and gave them birth, and has acted shamefully...therefore I will not have pity on her children, because they are children of harlotry' (Hosea 2:4-5). The correct answer is C.

'Cows of Bashan...who oppress the poor, who crush the needy' refers to the women of Samaria — Amos used this metaphor to rebuke the privileged women of Samaria who demanded luxuries while exploiting the poor (Amos 4:1). The correct answer is A.

'It is enough; now, O LORD, take away my life' was said by Elijah when he was threatened by Jezebel — Jezebel threatened to kill him and he fled in fear, sat under a broom tree, and prayed to die (1 Kings 19:2-4). The correct answer is B.

Isaiah admonished his people to demonstrate righteousness by learning to do good and seeking justice — 'learn to do good; seek justice, correct oppression; bring justice to the fatherless, plead the widow's cause' (Isaiah 1:17). The correct answer is B.

The Philistines were anxious to get rid of the Ark because the hand of God was heavy upon them — God struck the Philistines with tumors and panic wherever the Ark was (1 Samuel 5:6-11). The correct answer is D.

In rebuilding Jerusalem, Nehemiah prayed against the insults of Tobiah and Sanballat — 'Hear, O our God, for we are despised. Turn back their taunt on their own heads' (Nehemiah 4:4). The correct answer is C.

Josiah defiled Topheth so that no one might sacrifice human beings again to Molech — 'He defiled Topheth...so that no one might burn his son or his daughter as an offering to Molech' (2 Kings 23:10). The correct answer is A.

God decided not to bring evil in Ahab's days because Ahab humbled himself before God — 'Because he has humbled himself before me, I will not bring the disaster in his days' (1 Kings 21:29). The correct answer is C.

Abraham could not grant the rich man's request because there was a chasm between them — 'And besides all this, between us and you a great chasm has been fixed, in order that those who would pass from here to you may not be able' (Luke 16:26). The correct answer is C.
In the transfiguration of Jesus, Moses and Elijah represented the law and the prophets — Moses represents the Law and Elijah represents the Prophets (Matthew 17:3). The correct answer is C.
'He who enters by the door is the shepherd of the sheep' — the door refers to Jesus — Jesus said 'I am the door of the sheep' and 'I am the good shepherd' (John 10:7, 11). The correct answer is A.

Jesus did not go immediately to Lazarus because He wanted His disciples to believe in Him — 'that you may believe' was the purpose stated by Jesus for not going immediately (John 11:15). The correct answer is B.

To fulfill the law, Jesus told the healed leper to go and show himself to the priest — 'See that you say nothing to anyone, but go, show yourself to the priest and offer the gift that Moses commanded' (Matthew 8:4). The correct answer is A.
In the parable of wheat and tares, the harvest time refers to the close of the age — 'The harvest is the end of the age, and the reapers are angels' (Matthew 13:39). The correct answer is A.
According to Luke, Jesus' last words on the cross were 'Father, into thy hands I commit my spirit!' (Luke 23:46). The correct answer is B.

Paul teaches that believers have been buried and raised with Christ to walk in newness of life — 'We were buried therefore with him by baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised...we too might walk in newness of life' (Romans 6:4). The correct answer is D.
According to Luke, Jesus healed the epileptic boy by rebuking the unclean spirit — 'Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit and healed the boy' (Luke 9:42). The correct answer is C.

Paul warned the Thessalonians against false teachers concerning the second coming of Christ — some were teaching that the day of the Lord had already come, causing alarm (2 Thessalonians 2:1-3). The correct answer is B.

Peter teaches Christians to prepare for the day of the Lord by living holy and godly lives — 'what sort of people ought you to be in lives of holiness and godliness, waiting for and hastening the coming of the day of God' (2 Peter 3:11-12). The correct answer is D.

According to Paul, spiritual gifts should promote cooperation — 'the body does not consist of one member but of many...that the members may have the same care for one another' (1 Corinthians 12:14, 25). The correct answer is A.

God would send strong delusion on those who perish because they refused to believe the truth — 'they refused to love the truth and so be saved...God sends them a strong delusion, so that they may believe what is false' (2 Thessalonians 2:10-11). The correct answer is A.
According to Paul, the purpose of the law is to increase the knowledge of sin — 'through the law comes knowledge of sin' (Romans 3:20; 5:20). The correct answer is D.
The man who stirred up the people against Paul in Ephesus was Demetrius, a silversmith who made silver shrines of Artemis — he feared the loss of his trade (Acts 19:24-28). The correct answer is B.
Paul described the gifts he received from the Philippians as pleasing to God — 'a fragrant offering, a sacrifice acceptable and pleasing to God' (Philippians 4:18). The correct answer is B.

The greatest domestic problem David experienced which almost cost him his kingdom was the revolt of Absalom against him — Absalom organized a rebellion that forced David to flee Jerusalem (2 Samuel 15-18). The correct answer is A.

David did not allow Abishai to destroy Saul because he wanted to avoid being guilty before the LORD — 'The LORD forbid that I should put out my hand against the LORD's anointed' (1 Samuel 26:11). The correct answer is D.

The consequence of Solomon's failure to keep God's commandments was God's promise to tear away part of the kingdom — 'I will surely tear the kingdom from you...I will not tear away all the kingdom...I will give one tribe to your son' (1 Kings 11:11-13). The correct answer is D.

The chief butler said 'I remember my faults today' — 'faults' refers to forgetting the young Hebrew who interpreted his dream correctly while in prison — he forgot to mention Joseph to Pharaoh (Genesis 41:9-12). The correct answer is A.

The LORD repented of evil intended for His people because Moses reminded Him of His promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Israel — 'Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, your servants, to whom you swore by your own self' (Exodus 32:13). The correct answer is B.

The second creation story ends with the institution of marriage — God made woman from Adam's rib, and 'a man shall leave his father and his mother and hold fast to his wife, and they shall become one flesh' (Genesis 2:24). The correct answer is D.

God's declaration that He would make a nation of Ishmael meant He recognized Ishmael as Abraham's descendant — God showed He would bless Ishmael and his descendants even though Isaac was the child of promise (Genesis 21:18). The correct answer is D.

David escaped to the cave of Adullam — 'David departed from there and escaped to the cave of Adullam. And when his brothers and all his father's house heard it, they went down there to him' (1 Samuel 22:1). The correct answer is A.

Isaiah likens God's creative ability to that of a potter and his earthen vessel — 'Does the clay say to him who forms it, What are you making?...Woe to him who strives with his Maker, an earthen vessel with the potter!' (Isaiah 45:9; 64:8). The correct answer is B.

When Moses cast his rod on the ground at Mount Horeb and it became a serpent, he fled from it — 'he threw it on the ground, and it became a serpent, and Moses fled from it' (Exodus 4:3). The correct answer is C.
Adam named his wife Eve because she was the mother of all living — 'The man called his wife's name Eve, because she was the mother of all living' (Genesis 3:20). The correct answer is A.

Abram was at Haran when the command 'Go from your country' was given — 'So Abram went, as the LORD had told him...Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Haran' (Genesis 12:4). The correct answer is A.

After Nebuchadnezzar destroyed Jerusalem, he left behind the poorest people — 'Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard left some of the poorest of the land to be vinedressers and plowmen' (2 Kings 25:12). The correct answer is B.

The reward for total obedience to God's commandments is life and length of days — 'And now, Israel, listen to the statutes...that you may live, and go in and take possession of the land' (Deuteronomy 4:1). The correct answer is C.

Hosea declares that transgressors stumble in the ways of the LORD — 'the ways of the LORD are right, and the upright walk in them, but transgressors stumble in them' (Hosea 14:9). The correct answer is A.

According to Amos, the famine God would send was not hearing the word of the LORD — 'I will send a famine on the land — not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the LORD' (Amos 8:11). The correct answer is B.

Daniel was set up to be thrown to the lions by the presidents and satraps of Persia — they conspired against Daniel and tricked King Darius into signing the decree (Daniel 6:4-7). The correct answer is A.
Elijah knew of Gehazi's covetous act because he went with him in spirit — 'Did not my heart go when the man turned from his chariot to meet you?' (2 Kings 5:26). The correct answer is B.

'The soul that sins shall die' by Ezekiel means every person is responsible for his own sin — Ezekiel taught individual moral accountability; no one would be punished for another's sins (Ezekiel 18:20). The correct answer is C.

God exalted Jesus' name above every other because He humbled Himself to be born in human form and was obedient to death — 'he humbled himself by becoming obedient to the point of death...Therefore God has highly exalted him' (Philippians 2:8-9). The correct answer is B.

The consequence of Hiel's building of Jericho was that he lost two of his sons — fulfilling Elijah's curse: 'he laid its foundation at the cost of Abiram his firstborn, and set up its gates at the cost of his youngest son Segub' (1 Kings 16:34). The correct answer is A.
Joshua reacted to the defeat at Ai by renting his clothes — 'Then Joshua tore his clothes and fell to the earth on his face before the ark of the LORD' (Joshua 7:6). The correct answer is B.

Paul boasted about the Corinthians for their offering for the saints — he told the Macedonians about Achaia's readiness to contribute to the collection for the saints (2 Corinthians 9:2). The correct answer is A.

Paul admonished believers in Thessalonica to prepare for Christ's second coming by keeping awake and being sober — 'So then let us not sleep, as others do, but let us keep awake and be sober' (1 Thessalonians 5:6). The correct answer is C.

According to Peter, when the chief Shepherd is manifested, the elders will obtain the unfading crown of glory — 'And when the chief Shepherd appears, you will receive the unfading crown of glory' (1 Peter 5:4). The correct answer is C.

Paul declared that no one can say Jesus is Lord except by the Holy Spirit — 'Therefore I want you to understand that no one speaking in the Spirit of God ever says Jesus is accursed! and no one can say Jesus is Lord except in the Holy Spirit' (1 Corinthians 12:3). The correct answer is C.

While they were yet enemies of God, believers were reconciled to Him by the death of Jesus Christ — 'while we were enemies we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son' (Romans 5:10). The correct answer is A.

According to Peter, the genuineness of Christian faith is tested by trials — 'so that the tested genuineness of your faith — more precious than gold that perishes though it is tested by fire — may be found to result in praise' (1 Peter 1:7). The correct answer is D.

Paul admonished Colossian believers not to lie because they had put off the old nature with its practices — 'Do not lie to one another, seeing that you have put off the old self with its practices' (Colossians 3:9). The correct answer is B.

The woman with the flow of blood touched Jesus' garment because she believed she would be made well — 'She said to herself, If I only touch his garment, I will be made well' (Matthew 9:21). The correct answer is B.
The Macedonians who travelled with Paul to Ephesus were Gaius and Aristarchus — 'two Macedonians who were Paul's companions in travel, Gaius and Aristarchus' (Acts 19:29). The correct answer is D.
The blind man near Jericho, on receiving his sight, followed Jesus, glorifying God — 'And immediately he recovered his sight and followed him, glorifying God' (Luke 18:43). The correct answer is D.

God's response to the rich fool's speech was that his soul was required of him — 'But God said to him, Fool! This night your soul is required of you, and the things you have prepared, whose will they be?' (Luke 12:20). The correct answer is A.

Peter became frightened as he walked on the sea because of the wind — 'But when he saw the wind, he was afraid, and beginning to sink he cried out, Lord, save me' (Matthew 14:30). The correct answer is A.
The Jerusalem Council resolved that Gentiles should abstain from idolatry, unchastity, strangled meat and blood (Acts 15:29). The correct answer is B.

'The earth produces of itself, first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear' was said in the parable of the seed growing secretly — this parable describes the mysterious, self-powered growth of the kingdom of God (Mark 4:26-28). The correct answer is B.
'Let us make man in our image' implies man being like God — man was created to reflect God's character and nature, bearing His moral image (Genesis 1:26-27). The correct answer is C.

The two sons of Samuel that became Judges were Joel and Abijah — 'the name of his firstborn son was Joel, and the name of his second, Abijah; they were judges in Beersheba' (1 Samuel 8:2). The correct answer is A.

Moses sent men to spy out Canaan in order to know if it was good or bad — 'and see what the land is, and whether the people who dwell in it are strong or weak...and whether the land is good or bad' (Numbers 13:18-19). The correct answer is C.
After Moses addressed the people, they answered 'All the words which the LORD has spoken we will do' — they made this covenant pledge at Sinai (Exodus 24:3). The correct answer is C.

Saul visited the witch of Endor when he was besieged by the Philistines — the Philistines gathered at Shunem and Saul was afraid, so he secretly consulted the medium at Endor (1 Samuel 28:4-7). The correct answer is A.
The people responded to Saul's call because the dread of the LORD fell on them — 'the dread of the LORD fell upon the people, and they came out as one man' (1 Samuel 11:7). The correct answer is B.
Seven sons of Jesse passed before Samuel before David was chosen — from Eliab to Shammah and four others (1 Samuel 16:6-11). The correct answer is C.
Nehemiah functioned as the king's cupbearer — 'Now I was cupbearer to the king' (Nehemiah 1:11). The correct answer is C.

Joseph was made prime minister because he interpreted Pharaoh's dream and counselled him on what to do — Pharaoh saw that no one else could do this and said 'You shall be over my house' (Genesis 41:39-40). The correct answer is D.

Solomon's statement 'Do not forsake her, and she will keep you; love her, and she will guard you' is in reference to wisdom — the book of Proverbs personifies wisdom and urges the young man to embrace and love wisdom (Proverbs 4:6). The correct answer is D.
Elijah killed all the prophets of Baal at the brook Kishon — 'And Elijah brought them down to the brook Kishon and slaughtered them there' (1 Kings 18:40). The correct answer is A.

King Nebuchadnezzar assembled the satraps, prefects and governors for the dedication of the image — 'King Nebuchadnezzar had set up...and he sent to gather the satraps...to come to the dedication of the image' (Daniel 3:1-3). The correct answer is D.

After Jonah was thrown into the sea and it ceased raging, the men feared the LORD, offered sacrifice, and made vows — 'Then the men feared the LORD exceedingly, and they offered a sacrifice to the LORD and made vows' (Jonah 1:16). The correct answer is B.
Zedekiah was captured in the plains of Jericho — 'they overtook him in the plains of Jericho, and all his army was scattered from him' (2 Kings 25:5). The correct answer is B.

'The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge' — in Israel this proverb meant children are punished for the sins of their parents — Ezekiel refuted this and taught individual responsibility (Ezekiel 18:2). The correct answer is B.

According to Luke, the mandate given to the twelve at commissioning was to preach the kingdom of God and heal — 'he sent them out to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal' (Luke 9:2). The correct answer is C.
Two Christian virtues from the Good Samaritan are compassion and mercy — the Samaritan had compassion and showed mercy by helping the wounded man (Luke 10:33-37). The correct answer is D.

'What have you to do with us, O Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the time?' reveals that the Gadarene demoniacs recognized the supreme power of Jesus — they acknowledged Him as the Son of God with power over them (Matthew 8:29). The correct answer is A.

'Go and learn what this means, I desire mercy and not sacrifice' — the event that preceded this was eating with tax collectors — Jesus said this in defense of His eating with tax collectors and sinners (Matthew 9:10-13). The correct answer is B.

Jesus did not go with the centurion to heal his servant because the centurion exhibited great faith — the centurion said 'only say the word, and my servant will be healed,' showing remarkable faith that Jesus could heal from a distance (Matthew 8:8-10). The correct answer is A.
The condition Jesus required from Jairus was that he should not fear but believe — 'Do not fear, only believe' (Mark 5:36; Luke 8:50). The correct answer is B.
The men who taught that circumcision was necessary for salvation came from Judah — 'But some men came down from Judea and were teaching the brothers' (Acts 15:1). The correct answer is B.

According to Peter's speech at Pentecost, God made Jesus both Lord and Christ — 'Let all the house of Israel therefore know for certain that God has made him both Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified' (Acts 2:36). The correct answer is C.

Paul was arrested at Philippi because he cast out the spirit of soothsaying from a slave girl — her owners, losing their profit, seized Paul and Silas and dragged them to the authorities (Acts 16:18-19). The correct answer is C.

What was done to the apostles was that they were charged not to speak in the name of Jesus — 'So they called them and charged them not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus' (Acts 4:18). The correct answer is D.

The first and second in the hierarchy of spiritual gifts are apostles and prophets — 'And God has appointed in the church first apostles, second prophets, third teachers...' (1 Corinthians 12:28). The correct answer is C.
Believers reproached for Christ's name are blessed because the spirit of glory and God rests upon them — 'the Spirit of glory and of God rests upon you' (1 Peter 4:14). The correct answer is A.

According to James, God promises those who love Him the crown of life — 'Blessed is the man who remains steadfast under trial, for when he has stood the test he will receive the crown of life, which God has promised to those who love him' (James 1:12). The correct answer is A (the crown of life = heirs of the kingdom). The correct answer is A (Eternal life = crown of life).
The same Lord gives varieties of service — 'there are varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit; and there are varieties of service, but the same Lord' (1 Corinthians 12:4-5). The correct answer is A.

'Take heart, it is I; have no fear' was said by Jesus when He was walking on the sea in the night — He spoke this to the frightened disciples who thought He was a ghost (Matthew 14:27; Mark 6:50). The correct answer is C.
When the Seventy returned from their mission, they reported that even demons were subject to them — 'Lord, even the demons are subject to us in your name!' (Luke 10:17). The correct answer is A.
'Blessed is the kingdom of our father David that is coming!' was declared during the triumphal entry into Jerusalem (Mark 11:10). The correct answer is D.

'To you I will give all this authority and their glory...if you will worship me' was said during the temptation of Jesus — Satan made this offer in one of the three wilderness temptations (Luke 4:6-7). The correct answer is D.

After Peter's great confession, Jesus charged the disciples to tell no one that He was the Christ — 'Then he strictly charged the disciples to tell no one that he was the Christ' (Matthew 16:20). The correct answer is A.

Rahab's reward for hiding the Israelite spies was that she and her household were spared — the spies promised 'our life for yours even to death if you do not tell this business of ours...she and her household were saved' (Joshua 2:14; 6:25). The correct answer is D.

King Saul's promise to anyone who defeated Goliath was giving his daughter in marriage to that person — 'The king will enrich the man who kills him with great riches and will give him his daughter' (1 Samuel 17:25). The correct answer is B.
After Samuel told Eli the Lord's message about his sons, Eli's response was 'It is the LORD; let him do what seems good to him' — a resigned acceptance (1 Samuel 3:18). The correct answer is A.
After Saul realized God would have nothing to do with him, he sought the help of a medium — he consulted the witch/medium at Endor (1 Samuel 28:7). The correct answer is A.

God did not lead Israel by the Philistine route because He did not want them to see war and return to Egypt — 'lest the people change their minds when they see war and return to Egypt' (Exodus 13:17). The correct answer is D.
One of Solomon's unwise policies was the use of forced labour to build the house of God and his palace — he levied forced labour on all Israel (1 Kings 5:13-14). The correct answer is A.

Before meeting God on Mount Sinai, the Israelites were asked to be consecrated and have their garments washed — 'Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow, and let them wash their garments' (Exodus 19:10). The correct answer is B.

'Have this mind among yourselves, which is yours in Christ Jesus' — this mind means a mind of humility — Christ 'made himself nothing, taking the form of a servant, being born in the likeness of men...and humbled himself' (Philippians 2:5-8). The correct answer is B.
Joseph's brothers decided not to kill him because he was their brother and flesh — Judah said 'he is our brother, our own flesh' (Genesis 37:27). The correct answer is B.

David's victory over the Amalekites at Ziklag was due to his prayer and seeking God's approval before pursuing them — 'And David inquired of the LORD, Shall I pursue after this band?' (1 Samuel 30:8). The correct answer is C.
Paul declares Christians have differing gifts according to grace given to them — 'Having gifts that differ according to the grace given to us, let us use them' (Romans 12:6). The correct answer is D.
Those baptized into Christ have been baptized into His death — 'all of us who have been baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death' (Romans 6:3). The correct answer is C.

Christians are admonished to put on the Lord Jesus and not to make provision for the flesh — 'put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the flesh, to gratify its desires' (Romans 13:14). The correct answer is A.
After the murder of Naboth, God declared that dogs would lick Ahab's blood where they had licked Naboth's — Elijah announced this judgment to Ahab (1 Kings 21:19). The correct answer is C.
One of Manasseh's sins was the shedding of innocent blood — 'Manasseh shed very much innocent blood, till he had filled Jerusalem from one end to another' (2 Kings 21:16). The correct answer is C.

On the third day after capturing the Ark, the Philistines discovered that Dagon had fallen and broken to pieces — 'Dagon had fallen face downward on the ground before the ark of the LORD, and the head of Dagon and both his hands were lying cut off on the threshold' (1 Samuel 5:4). The correct answer is B.

God sent Jonah to Nineveh to cry against their wickedness — 'arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and call out against it, for their evil has come up before me' (Jonah 1:2). The correct answer is D.
'Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you' was said during the call of Prophet Jeremiah (Jeremiah 1:5). The correct answer is D.
Jesus said 'We must work the works of him who sent me, while it is day' after the healing of the man born blind — this statement introduces the account in John 9 (John 9:4). The correct answer is A.

Paul and Barnabas were sent out on the first missionary work by the Holy Spirit — through the prophets and teachers at Antioch, the Holy Spirit said 'Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul' (Acts 13:2-4). The correct answer is A.
The sudden death of Ananias and Sapphira caused great fear to grip all the disciples — 'great fear came upon all who heard of it' (Acts 5:5, 11). The correct answer is A.

The 'things that have happened' referred to on the Emmaus road were the crucifixion, death and resurrection of Jesus — the disciples explained 'the things concerning Jesus of Nazareth, who was a prophet...and how he was crucified...but some women of our company...told us that he was alive' (Luke 24:19-23). The correct answer is C.

According to Galatians, Christians are redeemed in Christ to receive the blessing of Abraham — 'Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law...so that in Christ Jesus the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles' (Galatians 3:13-14). The correct answer is A.

Paul commanded the Thessalonians to keep away from those who live in idleness — 'we command you, brethren...that you keep away from any brother who is walking in idleness' (2 Thessalonians 3:6). The correct answer is A.

Peter teaches that for being humble, a Christian obtains grace — 'Clothe yourselves, all of you, with humility toward one another, for God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble' (1 Peter 5:5). The correct answer is C.
'My God will supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus' was said to the church at Philippi (Philippians 4:19). The correct answer is B.

Peter recommends that elders should live exemplary lives — 'shepherding the flock of God...not under compulsion, but willingly...not domineering over those in your charge, but being examples to the flock' (1 Peter 5:2-3). The correct answer is B.

When the shepherd found the lost sheep, he called on people to rejoice with him — 'he calls together his friends and his neighbors, saying to them, Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep that was lost!' (Luke 15:6). The correct answer is A.

A condition a Christian must fulfill to become a joint heir with Christ is being baptized — through baptism we are united with Christ and become heirs; 'baptized into Christ...if you are Christ's, then you are Abraham's offspring, heirs according to promise' (Galatians 3:27-29; Romans 6:3). The correct answer is D.

When Jesus appeared to disciples on the evening of the first day of the week, He pronounced peace upon them — 'Jesus came and stood among them and said to them, Peace be with you' (John 20:19). The correct answer is B.

Paul rebuked Bar-Jesus with blindness because he sought to prevent the proconsul from the faith — 'you...making crooked the straight paths of the Lord...Behold, the hand of the Lord is upon you, and you will be blind' (Acts 13:10-11). The correct answer is C.
Jesus' reply to the devil's first temptation was 'Man shall not live by bread alone' — in response to the command to turn stone into bread (Matthew 4:4; Luke 4:4). The correct answer is B.

When Jesus sent out the seventy, He charged them to heal the sick and preach the message of the kingdom — 'heal the sick in it and say to them, The kingdom of God has come near to you' (Luke 10:9). The correct answer is C.
The first four disciples of Jesus were Simon, Andrew, John and James (Matthew 4:18-22; Mark 1:16-20). The correct answer is B.

The new commandment Jesus gave His disciples was that they should love one another — 'A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another: just as I have loved you, you also are to love one another' (John 13:34). The correct answer is D.

The voice at the Transfiguration was to affirm Jesus' Sonship — 'This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased; listen to him' — the Father declared Jesus' identity (Matthew 17:5). The correct answer is A.
The charge against Naboth was cursing God and the king — Jezebel arranged false witnesses to testify 'Naboth cursed God and the king' (1 Kings 21:13). The correct answer is B.

Pilate asked if they wanted him to release the King of the Jews because he perceived that the Jews were envious of Jesus — 'For he perceived that it was out of envy that the chief priests had delivered him up' (Mark 15:10). The correct answer is B.

'But say the word and let my servant be healed' implies faith — the centurion demonstrated extraordinary faith in believing that Jesus only needed to speak a word to heal from a distance (Luke 7:7). The correct answer is C.

'Then they laid their hands on them and they received the Holy Spirit' happened when Peter and John went to Samaria — they prayed and laid hands on those whom Philip had baptized (Acts 8:14-17). The correct answer is C.
In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus taught His disciples to love and pray for their enemies — 'Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you' (Matthew 5:44). The correct answer is C.

Paul initially persecuted the church because he was extremely zealous for the traditions of his fathers — 'I was advancing in Judaism beyond many of my own age among my people, so extremely zealous was I for the traditions of my fathers' (Galatians 1:14). The correct answer is B.

King Josiah killed the idolatrous priests of Judah — 'He deposed the priests whom the kings of Judah had ordained to make offerings in the high places...and he killed them' (2 Kings 23:5, 20). The correct answer is B.

After receiving Jezebel's threat, Elijah was afraid, arose and fled for his life — 'Then he was afraid, and he arose and ran for his life and came to Beersheba' (1 Kings 19:3). The correct answer is B.

Daniel was distinguished above all others because he had an excellent spirit — 'because an excellent spirit was in him...the king planned to set him over the whole kingdom' (Daniel 6:3). The correct answer is C.

'Whether they hear or refuse to hear, they will know that there has been a prophet among them' — the prophet referred to was Ezekiel — God said this to Ezekiel at his calling (Ezekiel 2:5). The correct answer is D.
God decided to destroy Nineveh because the people were wicked — 'their evil has come up before me' (Jonah 1:2). The correct answer is A.

Josiah's religious reforms led to the keeping of the Passover in Jerusalem — 'The king commanded all the people, Keep the Passover to the LORD your God, as it is written in this Book of the Covenant' (2 Kings 23:21). The correct answer is B.
Amaziah accused Amos before Jeroboam of conspiracy — 'Amos has conspired against you in the midst of the house of Israel' (Amos 7:10). The correct answer is A.

Abraham named the place where he had attempted to sacrifice Isaac 'The LORD will provide' (Jehovah-Jireh) — 'Abraham called the name of that place, The LORD will provide' (Genesis 22:14). The correct answer is B.
Moses complained that he could not go to Pharaoh alone because he was slow in speech — 'I am not eloquent...I am slow of speech and of tongue' (Exodus 4:10). The correct answer is C.

Joab and his soldiers entered the city quietly because the king was grieving for his son Absalom — the victory was turned to mourning, and the people came quietly into the city (2 Samuel 19:2-3). The correct answer is C.

David's servants refused to tell him his son died because they feared he might harm himself — 'How can we tell him the child is dead? He may do himself some harm' (2 Samuel 12:18). The correct answer is D.
When Israel did evil, God gave them into Philistine hands for forty years — 'the LORD gave them into the hand of the Philistines for forty years' (Judges 13:1). The correct answer is D.
David made the decision to pursue the Amalekites through the ephod — he asked Abiathar to bring the ephod and inquired of the LORD (1 Samuel 30:7-8). The correct answer is A.

God's covenant with Noah after the flood was that He would never again destroy the earth by flood — 'I establish my covenant with you, that never again shall all flesh be cut off by the waters of the flood' (Genesis 9:11). The correct answer is A.

According to Mark, John the Baptist's preaching centred on repentance for the forgiveness of sins — 'John appeared, baptizing in the wilderness and proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins' (Mark 1:4). The correct answer is D.

The vision Peter saw was to extend the gospel to the Gentiles — the sheet with unclean animals and the voice 'What God has made clean, do not call common' prepared Peter to accept Cornelius and preach to Gentiles (Acts 10:15, 28). The correct answer is C.

According to Matthew, the disciples fell on their faces during the Transfiguration when they heard a voice from the cloud — 'when the disciples heard this, they fell on their faces and were terrified' (Matthew 17:6). The correct answer is B.

Hosea said when Israel returned to the Lord, they would dwell beneath His shadow — 'They shall return and dwell beneath my shadow; they shall flourish like the grain' (Hosea 14:7). The correct answer is C.

The disciples could not heal the boy with the dumb spirit because they had no faith — Jesus said 'this kind cannot be driven out by anything but prayer' (Mark 9:29) implying failure of faith and dependence on God. The correct answer is D.

Pilate wondered greatly because Jesus gave him no answer to a single charge — 'But he gave him no answer, not even to a single charge, so that the governor was greatly amazed' (Matthew 27:14). The correct answer is A.
When the apostles heard Samaria had received the word through Philip, they sent Peter and John to pray for them to receive the Holy Spirit (Acts 8:14-15). The correct answer is B.
The gifts offered to Jesus by the wise men were gold, frankincense and myrrh (Matthew 2:11). The correct answer is D.
In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus taught His disciples to leap for joy when facing persecution — 'Rejoice and be glad, for your reward is great in heaven' (Matthew 5:12). The correct answer is D.

The chief priests bribed the guards to say that the disciples stole the body of Jesus — 'You are to say, His disciples came by night and stole him away while we were asleep' (Matthew 28:13). The correct answer is A.
'As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world' was said on the occasion of healing the man born blind (John 9:5). The correct answer is A.
Jesus washed the disciples' feet because He wanted to serve by example — 'For I have given you an example, that you also should do just as I have done to you' (John 13:15). The correct answer is B.

Jesus raised the son of the widow of Nain because He had compassion on the mother — 'And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her and said to her, Do not weep' (Luke 7:13). The correct answer is C.
Paul advises Roman Christians to bless those who persecute them — 'Bless those who persecute you; bless and do not curse them' (Romans 12:14). The correct answer is C.

Peter enjoins Christians to wait for the new heavens and new earth in which righteousness dwells — 'But according to his promise we are waiting for new heavens and a new earth in which righteousness dwells' (2 Peter 3:13). The correct answer is D.

According to Peter, God shows no partiality; in every nation anyone who fears Him is acceptable to Him — 'Truly I understand that God shows no partiality, but in every nation anyone who fears him and does what is right is acceptable to him' (Acts 10:34-35). The correct answer is B.

Peter admonishes that Christians should endure suffering because anyone who has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin — 'whoever has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin, so as to live for the rest of the time in the flesh no longer for human passions but for the will of God' (1 Peter 4:1-2). The correct answer is C.

According to Galatians, flesh and Spirit are opposed to each other — 'For the desires of the flesh are against the Spirit, and the desires of the Spirit are against the flesh, for these are opposed to each other' (Galatians 5:17). The correct answer is D.

'He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your resources' was made regarding Christian attitude to giving — Paul used this to encourage the Corinthians to give generously, promising God would replenish what they gave (2 Corinthians 9:10). The correct answer is A.
According to Romans, good citizenship involves obedience to those in authority — 'Let every person be subject to the governing authorities' (Romans 13:1). The correct answer is C.
